News.title: How ‘woke’ court ruling sparked explosion of thousands of migrants storming EU border at ‘weak spot’ Spanish enclave
News.content:
THOUSANDS of migrants storming a Spanish enclave’s borders will be emboldened by a “woke” court ruling protecting them.

Migrants intercepted while swimming to Ceuta or Melilla are not subject to immediate expulsion per a Supreme Court ruling three weeks ago.



It found that entering by sea does not involve crossing a physical land border, making “hot returns” at the border inapplicable to existing immigration law.

The decision has been exploited by people-smuggling gangs and encouraged a wave of undocumented migration.



Police in Ceuta have warned that they risk operational collapse as hundreds of migrants arrive by sea.

A Guardia Civil spokesperson said: “It has been a slow trickle since the Supreme Court’s ruling, but today has been an explosion.”

It has vowed to deport migrants who were seen sprinting along beaches and onto the street past the EU’s only land border with Africa.today

Spain‘s socialist government stands out for its pro-migration stance.



It has recently received a huge influx of applications after launching a scheme to provide legal status to 500,000 undocumented migrants.

Authorities in Ceuta have also asked the government in Madrid to declare a national emergency as they requested the army‘s help.

The President of Ceuta, Juan Jesus Vivas, was quick to declare a total humanitarian and social emergency in response.



He said: “In the past few days more than 1,500 migrants, both adults and minors, have come to Ceuta by sea.

“The reception centres are saturated – there is no more room for anyone in them and according to yesterday’s figures the number of people entering is more than 200 a day.”

Videos from Tarajal beach show crowds of people, mainly Moroccans, rushing across the sand attempting to make it to the road.

The majority are young men but several whole families, including young children, can also be seen.

They had managed to jump over the border fence separating the city from Morocco, according to Spanish state news agency EFE.



Some could be heard chanting “Viva Espana!” – Long Live Spain – as they walked past.

Ceuta sits between Morocco and Spain at the northwestern tip of Africa.

Along with Spanish autonomous city Melilla, it is the European Union‘s only land border with Africa.

Spain’s interior ministry said several ministries are “acting in coordination to respond with the utmost speed and efficiency to the situation in Ceuta”.

The Moroccan government also promised it would work “faithfully and permanently with Spain” in regards to the ongoing crisis.



They said: “Moroccan security forces are preventing the arrival of numerous people who are trying to reach Ceuta from Morocco.”

Morocco and Spain have reportedly agreed to return migrants who entered Ceuta during the latest surge, according to Hespress.

Vivas said 60 bodies had been recovered at sea in recent months with several washing up to shore in Ceuta.

He has warned the humanitarian crisis will only worsen while migrant centers are so full as hundreds of people will be forced to sleep on the streets.

He added that housing units for minors were now operating at 2,400 per cent capacity.



Back in 2021, 8,000 migrants swam from Morocco into Ceuta over a few days.

The arrivals also included the largest ever number of migrants in a single day, thought to be 6,000.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ceuta residents had locked themselves indoors as the army rounded up migrants fleeing Morocco, La Vanguardia reported.

Hundreds of migrants risk injuries or even death every year while trying to jump over fences, hide inside vehicles or by swimming around breakwaters that extend into the Mediterranean Sea.

News.title: Beachgoers stunned as bags packed with £600,000 in cash wash up on holiday island shore
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment stunned beachgoers discovered £600,000 in cash washed up on the shore of a holiday island.

Extraordinary footage shows holidaymakers lifting the lid of a shopping bag to reveal bundles of banknotes stacked inside.



One curious onlooker even pulls out a couple of wads of cash before quickly putting them back.

The remarkable discovery was made at Casuzze, a seaside resort on Sicily’s southern coast.



Beachgoers gathered around several bags stuffed with cash after they were allegedly thrown into the sea from a stranded speedboat.

Italian investigators said the 18ft vessel had been travelling from Malta when it reportedly suffered engine trouble.

After running out of fuel, it drifted towards the shoreline carrying three men and a boy believed to be about 13-years-old.

According to investigators, three of the four people on board jumped into the water as the boat continued drifting towards the beach.



As officers closed in on the vessel, they claim the only person left aboard was seen throwing sealed bags into the sea.

The current carried several of the floating bags ashore, where beachgoers helped retrieve them.

Authorities recovered almost all of the money, which is estimated to total between £500,000 and £600,000.

The four occupants were taken in for questioning, while the speedboat was towed to port for forensic examination.

Ragusa Police Commissioner Salvatore Fazzino said the vessel was intercepted only because of its unexpected mechanical failure.



He said: “An engine failure stopped the boat.

“If everything had gone smoothly, we would not have intercepted it.”

Fazzino added that the Coast Guard is believed to have recovered all of the cash.

Investigators have since revealed the boat was being driven by a man of Maltese origin.

The identities of the other three occupants remain unknown.



They are now trying to establish where the money came from and why such a large amount of cash was being transported on the route between Malta and Sicily.

Authorities are examining several possibilities, including money laundering, drug-related payments, currency smuggling and counterfeit banknotes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fazzino said: “We need to understand who the person is, where it came from, and reconstruct the movements.”

The four people have since been released pending further investigation and remain on police bail.

News.title: Diane Abbott expected to be let back into Labour under Andy Burnham following suspension over antisemitism row
News.content:
DI ANOTHER DAY Diane Abbott expected to be let back into Labour under Andy Burnham following suspension over antisemitism row

DIANE Abbott is poised to be let back into Labour under Andy Burnham, The Sun understands.

A year-long internal disciplinary probe into her antisemitism row is reaching its final stages and is expected to recommend her suspension be lifted.



The veteran left-winger was suspended as both a Labour MP and party member for the second time last year after saying she did not regret her past remarks on racism.

In 2024 Ms Abbott said that black people experience racism differently from the “prejudice” of Jews, Travellers and Irish.



The comments saw her suspended by Sir Keir Starmer, who then readmitted her in time to stand in the general election.

She was then “administratively suspended” once again last year after doubling down on her previous remarks.



Ms Abbott is the longest-serving MP in the Commons, having first been elected to represent Stoke Newington, and currently sits as an independent.

While her party membership is expected to be reinstated, it will be up to chief whip Anneliese Midgley to let her sit as a Labour MP.

But a Labour source told the Sun: “Once she has her membership back I’d imagine Andy will give her the whip back pretty sharpish.

“Keir waited months before doing it the first time, but the new regime want to keep people onside.”



Other suspended Labour MPs are also expecting decisions on their fate.

Outspoken Karl Turner was booted out of the Parliamentary Labour Party for repeatedly attacking Sir Keir’s plans to reduce jury trials.

The Burnham supporting-MP is confident he will have the whip restored shortly and is in touch with Ms Midgley.

News.title: Dramatic moment hero fishermen join dramatic mission to save tourists trapped on Crete beaches as deadly wildfires rage
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment hero fishermen rescued dozens of desperate holidaymakers stranded on Crete’s beaches as huge wildfires tore across Greek holiday islands.

Footage shows the locals braving choppy waters to evacuate the terrified tourists.



Footage shows the sky turning a terrifying shades of orange and black as a fleet of coast guard boats and fishermen’s vessels rushed to evacuate those stranded.

Thousands of locals and Brit tourists have been evacuated from Crete after wildfires ripping through the island killed three firefighters.





Terrifying infernos fanned by violent winds have ravaged the packed Greek island at the peak of the summer season.

Blazes also raged on the islands of Paros and Lesbos.

Young fisherman Nikos Matthaiakis was ready at a moment’s notice to join the rescue effort on the coast of Crete.

He leapt into action, telling Cretalive.gr: “We did our duty too… I was called by the Port Authority at 4 pm to be on standby.



“They asked me for help and I gave it generously. I went with my fishing boat.”

The sea raged, whipped up by “hurricane-force” winds – but 30 people were trapped on a beach in Agios Pavlos on Crete’s southern coast.

Nikos said: “It was stifling in terms of fire and smoke, but the winds were hurricane-force. They recorded up to 160kilometres of wind gusts (100miles).”



He battled to the shore where tourists were waiting as the flames fast approached.

Gas cylinders exploded as the island burned, causing deafening banging sounds.

The young fisherman said: “The tavern and the accommodations were burning above. Some bottles also exploded. We could hear bangs.”

Nikos ran several trips to shore, forging into the thick smoke to save everyone – including children and elderly people who struggled to climb into his boat.

Late on Wednesday, some 8,000 people were evacuated as massive fires threatened a resort village, deputy governor of the Rethymno region Maria Lioni said.



She said the flames had reached within less than a mile of the village.

It comes amid a spate of deadly wildfires wreaking havoc across Europe – including the UK – as the continent tackles record-breaking heatwaves.

Flames in Spain and France are understood to be dying down, leaving Greece and Turkey to bear the brunt of the soaring temperatures.



Two firefighters trapped on a mountain road near the Greek village of Krya Vrysi died as powerful winds kept changing direction.

Another emergency worker was killed after being found unconscious near the southern Peloponnese port town of Gytheio.

Lioni said: “It was a dark day.”

Local authorities have dedicated over 200 firefighters and 53 fire engines in the Rethymno area in southwestern Crete.

Nearly 100 firefighters were deployed to tackle a separate sprawling blaze on the Greek island of Lesbos.



As temperatures soar past 40C, the holiday island of Paros has also been hit by Europe’s raging infernos, forcing ten areas into evacuation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And in Suffolk, hundreds of holidaymakers were evacuated in the middle of the night as a wildfire raced towards a popular seaside resort.

Around 200 caravans were evacuated as a major incident was declared at the National Trust site Dunwich Heath.
