News.title: Why Bryan Kohberger’s arrest & jail interrogation footage is missing from Netflix’s The Idaho Murders: College Nightmare
News.content:
THE new Netflix documentary about the Idaho murders teases up to killer Bryan Kohberger’s dramatic early morning arrest, but there’s a reason fans are left without footage of him being cuffed.

Kohberger, who is now serving life in prison for fatally stabbing four University of Idaho students to death, was arrested on December 30, 2022, weeks after the murders.



The PhD student was captured at his parents’ home in Pennsylvania following a multi-agency investigation into the killings of Kaylee Goncalves, 21, Madison Mogen, 21, Xana Kernodle, 20, and Ethan Chapin, 20.

The documentary shows bodycam footage from police arriving at the 1122 King Road home in Moscow, Idaho, where the four students were brutally stabbed to death on November 13, 2022.



It also features police interviews with surviving roommates Dylan Mortensen and Bethany Funke, Kaylee’s ex-boyfriend Jack DuCoeur, who was cleared as a suspect, and other friends of the victims.

The three-part series explains how police captured Kohberger’s white Hyundai Elantra in the area around the time of the killings, and how investigators used genetic genealogy after DNA found on a knife sheath left at the crime scene pointed them toward a possible family connection.

Investigators then traveled to Pennsylvania, where FBI agents and police began surveilling Kohberger at his family’s home.

Officers collected trash discarded outside the residence and recovered DNA that investigators said matched the profile connected to the sheath, helping them build the case against him.



But true crime fans do not get to see Kohberger’s dramatic arrest, footage of any police interrogation, or interviews with his family, including his parents Michael and Maryann and his sisters.

The videos have never been made public for several reasons.

The arrest was carried out by the Pennsylvania State Police’s Special Emergency Response Team (SERT), with assistance from the FBI, the Moscow Police Department, and Idaho State Police.

Court records seen by The U.S. Sun show the state never received video of the arrest — because investigators said they were unaware any footage exists.

A filing reads, “The State has disclosed all items it is aware of relating to ‘the search and arrest of Bryan Kohberger in Pennsylvania.’



“The State is unaware of any ‘body cam and dash cam footage’ beyond what has been disclosed and, on information and belief, understands there is no body cam footage.”

At the time of Kohberger’s arrest, Pennsylvania State Police had not yet begun its body-worn camera rollout, which launched as a pilot program in 2023 and was completed statewide in 2025.

Other agencies involved in the arrest operation, including the FBI, also did not typically use patrol-style body cameras.



SWAT and tactical operations also often restrict recording to protect specialized law enforcement tactics, operational security, and the identities of undercover or specialized operators.

He was taken into custody around 1:30 am.

A booking photo was later released, while a separate image showing Kohberger moments after his arrest in handcuffs was not made public until August 2025.

Kohberger was taken to the Pennsylvania State Police barracks in Stroudsburg, where he was interviewed by Moscow Police Corporal Brett Payne, the lead investigator on the case, and Idaho State Police Detective Darren Gilbertson.

Kohberger, who is now appealing his conviction, answered a few basic questions before asking for a lawyer when detectives began asking him about the murders.



Because he agreed to a plea deal and the case never went to trial, the interview was not played in court.

The U.S. Sun can confirm the video does exist, as a police filing reveals, “The interview was recorded on the built-in video system.”

Transcripts from the interview, along with conversations involving his family, were later made public.

When Kohberger said he wanted officers to explain why he was there, investigators replied it was because of “what occurred in Moscow.”

Kohberger admitted, “I watch the news,” but said the only thing he knew about the case was a Washington State University crime alert that had appeared on his phone.



He repeatedly asked where his parents and dog were, said he had the “utmost respect” for law enforcement, and insisted it was his constitutional right to speak to an attorney before invoking his Fifth Amendment rights.

The video recordings remain withheld under public records exemptions that protect law enforcement investigative material and privacy concerns.

The first major footage released involving Kohberger came from a series of traffic stops before and after the murders.

On August 21, 2022, Kohberger was pulled over in Moscow, Idaho, while driving alone in his white Hyundai Elantra and received a citation for a seat belt violation.

He was stopped again on October 14, 2022, by a Washington State University police officer in Pullman after allegedly running a red light, with Kohberger the sole occupant of the vehicle.



Then, on December 15, 2022, bodycam footage captured Kohberger driving the Hyundai Elantra during a cross-country trip from Washington to Pennsylvania with his father in the passenger seat.

During the journey, the car was stopped twice in Indiana after officers accused Kohberger of following another vehicle too closely.

Both officers issued warnings and allowed Kohberger and his father to continue their trip.

A DMV surveillance video from November 18, 2022, was later released showing Kohberger at a Washington licensing office five days after the murders.

He was seen updating the registration and plates on his car.



Meanwhile, grocery store surveillance footage was released showing Kohberger at a Costco store on the afternoon of November 13, 2022, the day of the murders.

He was seen wearing a green shirt and slacks and was stopped from entering because he did not have his membership card.

Holding a water bottle, he appeared to search his pocket for the card before leaving.

Other investigative footage, including surveillance videos, interviews and police records, was released gradually through court filings and public records requests.

The releases provided a look at Kohberger’s movements before and after the murders.



Kohberger has since launched a brazen bid to overturn his conviction by filing a petition to withdraw the guilty plea that spared him the death penalty, per the New York Times.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He claims he was coerced into admitting to the murders, alleges his attorneys withheld potentially exculpatory evidence and made false promises about prison conditions, and insists he is actually innocent.

The request faces a steep legal hurdle, as Idaho law requires him to prove a “manifest injustice” to undo a plea entered after sentencing.

News.title: Missing child, 5, is ‘found dead in water’ after vanishing in UK village in ‘incredibly tragic incident’
News.content:
TRAGIC END Missing child, 5, is ‘found dead in water’ after vanishing in UK village in ‘incredibly tragic incident’

A MISSING five-year-old has been found dead in a body of water after vanishing in a UK village in an “incredibly tragic incident.”

Police had been frantically searching for the youngster after they vanished from Badsey, near Evesham, yesterday evening.

Tragically cops have now confirmed that a body has been found in the Badsey area amid their desperate search for the child.

Sadly, the five-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene.





The force said said it believed the “incredibly tragic incident” was the result of drowning.

Officers confirmed there were no suspicious circumstances and said a file would be prepared for the coroner.

A West Mercia Police spokesperson told Birmingham Live: “Officers were called to a report of a missing child in Badsey yesterday evening (Wednesday 29 July).

“Sadly, the child was found unresponsive in a body of water, and a short time later was pronounced dead.

“There is no third-party involvement in the child’s death, and a report will be prepared for the coroner.

“This is an incredibly tragic incident.

“We ask the public to avoid speculation online as this is incredibly distressing to the family and we ask that their privacy is respected at such a difficult time.”

A local business, Badsey Butchers, paid a moving tribute to the families “unimaginable loss” on their Facebook page.



The post said: “Today has left our whole community shocked and deeply saddened.

“Our hearts go out to a local family facing an unimaginable loss, along with everyone who knows and loves them.

“There are simply no words that can ease a heartbreak like this, but we hope they know the entire village is thinking of them.

“As a mark of respect, we won’t be posting any further content for the rest of this week.

“Please keep them in your thoughts and give them the privacy and compassion they deserve.”



West Midlands Ambulance Service told the BBC they were called at 6.50pm, sending an ambulance, two paramedic officers and the Midlands Air Ambulance Critical Care Car to the scene.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesperson said: “On arrival we discovered one patient, a young child.

“Ambulance staff and police worked quickly to treat the patient, but sadly, it became apparent nothing could be done to save them and they were confirmed dead at the scene.”

News.title: Second wildfire breaks out in UK as eight fire engines and crews battle huge field blaze
News.content:
FIELD INFERNO Second wildfire breaks out in UK as eight fire engines and crews battle huge field blaze

A SECOND wildfire has broken out in the UK as firefighters battled a raging blaze.

Around 60 firefighters and eight fire engines scrambled to the scene to tackle the large grass fire in Hornchurch, East London.



At the height of the fire, around six hectares were alight, said the London Fire Brigade.

But there are currently no reports of any injuries after the blaze near South End Road, the fire service said.



The Brigade’s Control Officers took the first of seven calls reporting the fire at 1.18pm and mobilised crews from Dagenham, Hornchurch, Wennington and surrounding fire stations.

One of the London Fire Brigade’s (LFB) Terrain Support Vehicles has also been deployed to support firefighting operations.



The off-road vehicle allows additional equipment to be transported closer to fires on open ground.

It carries around 475 litres of water, as well as a backpack blower, ear defenders, beaters and misting lance technology, enabling firefighters to tackle grass fires more quickly and safely.

LFB added that the blaze is now under control.

The cause of the fire has not yet been determined and is under investigation.

It comes after a raging wildfire broke out in Suffolk near Sizewell nuclear plant, sparking chaos as holidaymakers fled for their lives.



The alarm was raised at around 5.30pm yesterday evening as an ominous orange glow lit up the landscape.

Holiday parks and dozens of nearby homes were among those evacuated as the fire devoured the tinder-dry grassland at Dunwich Heath.

The rampant inferno grew ten-fold in a matter of hours as 120 firefighters scrambled to slow its pace amid a desperate race against time.

A major incident was declared and surrounding roads closed with 18 fire trucks deployed to the area in a bid to bring the blaze under control.

Fire chiefs reckon the heath – used to film BBC‘s Springwatch – could continue burning for another 72 hours due to the “live and dynamic situation”.



The blaze is not yet under control but Suffolk Fire and Rescue said it poses no risk to the nuclear plant.

News.title: American suffers execution-style death in Caribbean after sending chilling text
News.content:
American suffers execution-style death in Caribbean after sending chilling text

Tyler Wilkin was camping alone on a remote beach in Puerto Rico when he began sending messages about a man he called 'the howler' - and was later found dead

View 4 Images Tyler Wilkin, 35, was gunned down on a remote beach (Image: GoFundMe)

An American man was shot dead execution-style on a remote Puerto Rico beach after sending messages about a mysterious man known as "the howler".

‌



Tyler Wilkin, 35, was found with a single gunshot wound to the back of the head near the forest-isolated Playa la Selva in the Caribbean island's northeast.

‌



His body was discovered shortly after 6am on July 10, according to local reports.

‌



Police believe he was shot at close range in what investigators suspect was an execution-style killing.

Wilkin, originally from Ohio, had been living in Puerto Rico since January 2024.

His girlfriend dropped him off at the remote beach on July 8 and he planned to camp there for two days.

‌



View 4 Images Wilkin was shot while camping on a Puerto Rico beach (Image: FOX19)

During his stay, he sent increasingly unsettling messages about a man he had nicknamed "the howler," who had allegedly been setting off fireworks near his campsite and "howling like a wolf."

"The howler is back!" he wrote to a friend on the night he was killed.

‌



His girlfriend, Iva Mo, said his final message arrived at around 2am.

"At two in the morning, like two hours later, he said something like, 'This guy is getting rowdy, LOL': And that was the last that we ever heard of him," she told WKRC.

She became alarmed when Wilkin failed to send his usual early-morning message.

‌



"Like six in the morning he consistently, always, texts me, 'Good morning, love.' And I didn't get a text message from him," she said.

His body was discovered in the mangroves shortly after 6am by a beachgoer taking a morning walk, local outlet Tele 11 reported.

View 4 Images Wilkin was originally from Ohio but had been living in Puerto Rico since January 2024 (Image: GoFundMe)

‌



Police are yet to make any arrests over the killing.

Mo believes he may have been murdered during an attempted robbery, while friends and relatives have criticised Puerto Rico police over the lack of progress in the investigation.

"To have his entire future just taken away like that in just a split second for what? Like over a wallet or over, I don’t know, for whatever reason, like, it's just really hard to accept," Mo said.

‌



Loved-ones have launched a GoFundMe page to raise funds for a private investigator to "uncover answers and ensure that every possible avenue is explored."

The fundraiser reads: "We lost Tyler far too soon, and the grief left behind is impossible to put into words.

View 4 Images Family members are demanding answers over his death (Image: FOX19)

‌



"As his family and friends continue to navigate this heartbreaking loss, we are determined to do everything we can to seek the truth and ensure that Tyler receives the justice he deserves.

"Tyler deserved a full life, and he deserves for every possible avenue to be explored," Lilly Wright, the GoFundMe organiser, said.

Wilkin is survived by his parents, older brother, twin sister and younger sisters, according to his obituary.

Article continues below

"He lived life with enthusiasm and was never afraid to embrace the unexpected. He had a way of making life feel exciting and meaningful," his family said.

"His laughter was contagious, his smile was genuine, and his happiness was something he shared freely with everyone around him."

News.title: Crete wildfires live: Rethymno in flames amid mass evacuations on Greek islands
News.content:
Flames are tearing across Greek Islands, forcing the evacuation of entire villages on Crete, Paros and Andros as wildfires continue to sweep across Europe

Raging wildfires have taken hold across several Greek islands, forcing villages to be evacuated as firefighters struggle to contain the flames.

Wildfires in the Rethymno region of the south of Crete are burning "out of control on all fronts", with firefighting aircraft unable to be deployed due to strong winds. Thousands of people, including tourists, were evacuated overnight. Urgent evacuation orders have also been issued for parts of Paros and Andros.

Three firefighters have died in Greece, with two becoming trapped in a vehicle while tackling the flames in Rethymno. Meanwhile, Europe's emergency response chief warned that the entire continent could be engulfed as wildfires rage in France, Spain and Portugal.

"Italy will face risk at the beginning of August, and we will need to see what will happen with the Iberian Peninsula, because if [it is] there as well, we will have all Europe on fire," Maria Zuber, head of the EU's Emergency Response Co-ordination Centre, said yesterday.

News.title: Suffolk fire live: Nuclear plant monitors ‘unprecedented’ wildfire destroying rare bird habitat
News.content:
Fire spans 100 hectares as crews from other areas called in

It is understood the fire now spans 100 hectares. Fire services from as far away as Essex are arriving to help with the emergency effort.

The smell of smoke occasionally fills the air with changing wind, as well as the sound of sirens from passing fire trucks and the whirring of a helicopter passing intermittently overhead.

At Westleton Village Hall, locals are banding together to help others, including holidaymakers, who have been evacuated from holiday lets and caravans near the fire.

Volunteers set up the makeshift rescue centre late on Wednesday night after the scale of the fire became clear.

They are helping evacuees to sort accommodation and giving away free food and drinks, including sandwiches, delivered from supermarket chain Waitrose, to the needy, including babies, families, elderly residents and some in wheelchairs.

Volunteers are also handing out pet food to animals evacuated.

Shortly before midday, they anlso unpacked bedding and pillows from a delivery van before moving them into the main hall.

Among the volunteers is Barry Banks, 52, who has lived in the village full-time for the past five years.

He told the Mirror: "We were made aware by the smell of smoke and sirens. We’re lucky we haven’t had too many fires in the past but it’s always in the back of everyone’s minds.

"By the time we got down here to open up there was already a strong team of volunteers ready to help in any way they could.

"We were fully open and operational for refreshments from about 10pm and then we heard that people were being evacuated from the campsites up until about midnight, 1am.

"We managed to get 47 people housed with the village. Everyone that turned up here was successfully housed.

"It was a mixture of accommodation, but I’d say about 80-90 per cent was people’s houses. It was a great effort. We’re very proud.

"We arrived this morning to cook a full breakfast for everyone that was housed overnight."

Barry added: "From the two updates we’ve had this morning, we understand things are still very fluid as far as the fire is concerned.

"The fire service are trying to slow the spread, but with the wind whipping up and due to change direction shortly, according to the forecast, it’s still a bit of the unknown.

"We understand there were possibly 18 to 20 fire appliances at its peak. It was constant through the night with sirens.

"It was amazing to see the response from everyone, emergency services especially."

News.title: Small boat driver who filmed himself steering dangerously overcrowded vessel jailed
News.content:
Small boat driver who filmed himself steering dangerously overcrowded vessel jailed

EXCLUSIVE: Footage shot by Iraqi national Rekar Nabaz, 28, shows people onboard an overcrowded small boat with no safety equipment onboard. He was jailed for two years and three months under a new endangerment law

Home Office shares video filmed by people smuggler on small boat

A small boat pilot who filmed himself steering a dangerously overcrowded vessel has been jailed.

Iraqi national Rekar Nabaz, 28, was sentenced to two years and three months behind bars for endangering lives and arriving in the UK without valid entry clearance. He swerved the boat from side-to-side when the Border Security Command attempted to intercept it on June 20 this year.

There were 52 people onboard, many of them not wearing life jackets with no safety equipment on board, despite poor visibility on the day of the crossing. The footage was released to The Mirror the Home Office a day after four people died attempting to reach the UK from France.

Nabaz is the eighth person to be convicted of endangerment in less than two months, with 25 cases ongoing. The new offence was introduced under the Border Security, Immigration and Asylum Act, which was passed last year.

UK must put right failures that left Afghan allies in danger after Taliban takeover, MPs demand READ MORE :

3 View 3 Images The clip shows a dangerously overcrowded small boat on the Channel (Image: Home Office) 3 View 3 Images The clip was filmed by Rekar Nabaz as he steered the vessel (Image: Home Office)

Immigration Minister Anna Turley told The Mirror: “That’s eight small boat pilots jailed under the endangerment offence now. We are sending a clear message to those bringing migrants to British shores: we will use all available powers to put you behind bars.

“Arrests for organised immigration crime have surged by 74%, with wider disruption activity against these criminal networks including arrests, convictions and seizures up 50%.

“This government will go even further to restore control to our borders and smash these dangerous smuggling gangs.”

Last month The Mirror reported that Algerian national Azzeddine Ain-Bouzid, 29, had been jailed for two years after drone footage showed him steering a boat with 67 people onboard. The vessel was only designed to carry 20.

View 3 Images Rekar Nabaz was jailed for more than two years (Image: Home Office)

The government has pledged to tackle small boat crossings, reaching a landmark new deal with France to boost law enforcement action on beaches earlier this year. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has announced a series of measures to discourage people coming to the UK, including a controversial proposal to review refugee status every two-and-a-half weeks.

There has been a sharp fall in crossings, with Home Office figures showing a 42% drop in the number of people reaching the UK by small boat compared to last year. But at least 13 people are believed to have died so far this year after four lives were lost in 24 hours yesterday.

One man died after a boat capsized off France's northern coast on Wednesday, and a one-year-old child was hurt. Later three people were found dead on board a boat which had launched from Dunkirk.

Article continues below

Earlier this week Mr Burnham said the government's plan to stop crossings was working, but admitted there was more to do. Charity Safe Passage International described the deaths as "devastating and avoidable" while calling on the Government to "take accountability for the lack of safe routes for refugees".

News.title: Welsh village floods after ‘explosion’ as evacuation ordered – ‘Felt like earthquake’
News.content:
Welsh village floods after ‘explosion’ as evacuation ordered – ‘Felt like earthquake’

Police and fire crews have swarmed the village of Gwaelod-y-Garth in Cardiff which became flooded after an explosion at a nearby quarry, locals said

View 4 Images Locals stand on a flooded street in Gwaelod-y-Garth, Cardiff

Multiple homes in Cardiff have been damaged after water came gushing through a village, forcing residents to evacuate.

‌



Police and fire crews swarmed the village of Gwaelod-y-Garth which became flooded after an explosion at the nearby Breedon Group quarry, locals said.

‌



Residents said the explosion, which happened at around 2pm, was like an "earthquake" and the most powerful blast experienced in 20 years of living in the area.

‌



One local said she fears the incident could cause higher land in the area to become unstable.

View 4 Images A nearby industrial estate has been evacuated

An industrial estate on Main Road, neighbouring the quarry, has been evacuated.

‌



A spokesperson for South Wales Fire Service said: "We are currently responding to surface water flooding at Heol Berry and Heol Y Nant, Gwaelod-y-Garth in the Taff’s Well area.

"Please avoid the area to allow the emergency services to deal with the incident."

South Wales Police have asked members of the public to "avoid the area," reports Wales Online.

‌



View 4 Images Homes have been wrecked by the flooding

A spokesman for the force said: "Officers are currently in attendance to the area of Gwaelod-y-Garth, Taff’s Well, following reports of flooding.

"A road closure is in place at the junction of Heol Goch and Main Road. Please avoid the area to allow the emergency services to deal with the incident".

‌



There are reports of severe traffic delays between Radyr and Taff's Well as police have closed roads which are flooded.

View 4 Images The incident sparked traffic in the area

A spokesperson for the quarry operator, Breedon, has said they are aware of the incident but are unable to comment any further at this time.

Article continues below

"We are aware of an incident that took place at our Taffs Well Quarry this afternoon," the spokesperson said.

"Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities while engaging with the local community as we respond to the situation.

"Our priority is supporting the response, and we are not in a position to provide any further comment at this time."

News.title: Driver who filmed herself speeding at nearly 100mph on Snapchat before fatal crash has sentence changed
News.content:
Driver who filmed herself speeding at nearly 100mph on Snapchat before fatal crash has sentence changed

Liberty Mitchell, who recorded Snapchat videos of herself driving at nearly 100mph before a crash which left two people dead, has been told her prison sentence is to be increased

Liberty Mitchell arrested after killing two people in car crash in 2022

A reckless driver who recorded herself speeding at almost 100mph before she crashed and killed two people has been told she will now serve an additional three years in prison.

‌



Liberty Mitchell, now 21, had only passed her test days before killing taxi driver Octavian Codreanu and Moyra Whelan, his passenger, back in December 2022. The woman was driving at 96mph in a 60-zone as she attempted to overtake three other cars on the wrong side of the road in her Mini Cooper before losing control and causing a pile-up.

‌



Mitchell, who had recently turned 18 at the time of the horror smash, was arrested at the scene on the B4425 near Aldsworth, Gloucestershire. She wept in the dock as she was sentenced to six years and eight months behind bars in February, and was told she must serve half of her sentence in custody before being eligible for release on licence.

‌



6 View 6 Images Liberty Mitchell was sentenced back in February 6 View 6 Images But after an appeal, her punishment has been increased (Image: Gloucestershire Police / SWNS)

Drink driver hit 119mph before killing teen who sent chilling text moments before READ MORE :

But hours later, Attorney General Ellie Reeves KC MP referred her case to the Court of Appeal under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme. After hearing arguments that the punishment was too lenient, senior judges have now increased her sentence to nine years and three months.

Ms Reeves welcomed the outcome and said: "Liberty Mitchell’s reckless actions behind the wheel claimed the lives of two people and left many others with life-changing injuries. My deepest sympathies go to the loved ones of Octavian Codreanu and Moyra Whelan, and to all those whose lives have been devastated by this tragedy.

‌



"The offender had previously filmed herself speeding and shared it on social media, showing disregard for the danger she posed to others. I pay tribute to the emergency services who treated the injured at the scene."

6 View 6 Images Victim Moyra Whelan 'had so much left that she wanted to experience', her sister said (Image: Gloucestershire Police / SWNS) 6 View 6 Images Mitchell sent footage of her reckless driving to pals on the app (Image: Gloucestershire Police / SWNS)

‌



Mr Codreanu and Ms Whelan, a schoolteacher on her way to a wedding, died at the scene. Mitchell was charged with two counts of causing death by dangerous driving, three counts of causing serious injury by dangerous driving, and two counts of causing death while driving uninsured, as her insurance did not cover use of the vehicle for work. She pleaded guilty to all charges.

The court heard that other victims of the crash sustained injuries including a fractured hip, broken ribs, severe abdominal wounds and shattered bones protruding through the skin.

View 6 Images She filmed herself speeding and swerving in a Mini Cooper (Image: Gloucestershire Police / SWNS)

‌



Nicola Cooper, one of the passengers in the taxi, said: "The crash itself was traumatic, the impact felt endless. I live with survivor's guilt and the trauma of losing one of my closest friends, Moyra, who was sitting just inches from me. I lie awake at night thinking about the 'what ifs'."

At her trial earlier this year, Judge Lowe said: "At the time of this collision, you had held a full driving licence for less than three weeks. You were, at the time, a reckless and immature young driver suffering from the, frankly common, teenage delusion that you were invulnerable and free to do as you wished. The lives of all the victims and their families have been irrevocably changed."

Sergeant Williams of the Serious Collision Investigation Team said: "This case was due to go to trial, and I’m pleased that Mitchell pleaded guilty and has now been sentenced.

‌



View 6 Images Liberty Mitchell (Image: Gloucestershire Police / SWNS)

"Her actions tragically killed taxi driver Octavian Codreanu and his passenger, schoolteacher Moyra Whelan, as well as seriously injuring three others.

"Friday, December 2 2022 is a day that will be ingrained in not only the minds of the families who lost a loved one, but also the numerous victims who have suffered horrendous injuries and who are still recovering today, as well as the large number of witnesses who stopped to help and whose lives have also been affected.

Article continues below

"Our thoughts remain with those who have suffered loss and injuries, and I’d like to thank the families of everyone involved in the collision for their patience and bravery during what has been a lengthy process."

News.title: Ceuta chaos as thousands cross into Spanish territory amid 'national emergency' plea
News.content:
Ceuta chaos as thousands cross into Spanish territory amid 'national emergency' plea

Footage shows crowds of people, mainly Moroccans, walking around the breakwaters at Tarajal beach in Ceuta and running on the beach and roads

Crowd breaks through border from Spanish territory of Ceuta from Morocco

Authorities in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta have asked the government in Madrid to send in the army and declare a national emergency after thousands of people crossed into the tiny territory.

‌



Videos shot at Tarajal beach showed crowds of people, mainly Moroccans, walking around the breakwaters and running on the beach and roads. Shouts of "Viva Espana!" can be heard amongst the crowd.

‌



The escalation at the border between Spain and Morocco comes after a surge in migrants attempting to reach the small exclave, mainly by swimming.

‌



"The situation is absolute chaos," said Rachid Sbihi, head of the association that represents Spain's Civil Guard officers in Ceuta, who police the border. "It's not possible to give precise numbers, but there are thousands of migrants crossing," he said, adding that the border had "totally collapsed."

Achraf Maimouni, a member of the Moroccan Association for Human Rights in northern Morocco, described the situation as `'exceptional."

View 3 Images Thousands of people crossed the border (Image: Reduan Dris/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



"The Tarajal border was opened under unusual circumstances this morning and people crossed," he said.

Between 2,000 and 3,000 people have crossed into Ceuta, Spain’s national broadcaster, TVE, reported.

The scenes of people crossing the frontier come after the border crisis of May 2021 when more than 8,000 migrants entered Ceuta in just two days. Pedro Sánchez, Spain’s prime minister, said his government would provide “an immediate response” to the current situation.

‌



The escalation at the frontier between Spain and Morocco comes after a surge in migrants attempting to reach the small exclave, mainly by swimming, on Wednesday. It was not immediately clear what prompted so many migrants to cross to Ceuta. At least three people died attempting to reach Ceuta by sea, Sibhi and activists in both Morocco and Ceuta reported.

View 3 Images People cross from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta (Image: AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)

Juan Jesus Vivas, head of the Ceuta regional government, called for the national government in Madrid to declare a national emergency on grounds of national security, asking for more police and for the army to be deployed on the border.

‌



Vivas said the additional police and soldiers would be necessary "to guarantee the inviolability of the frontier and citizen safety."

He had warned on Wednesday that migrant reception centres were overwhelmed, with hundreds of people sleeping on the streets.

View 3 Images Crowds of people walked around the breakwaters and ran onto the beach and roads (Image: AP Photo/Antonio Sempere)

Article continues below

Spain’s central government said Fernando Grande-Marlaska, Spain’s interior minister, would travel to Ceuta on Friday. However ministers have stopped short of declaring a national emergency.

Pedro Sánchez said in a post on X: “We’re mobilising all necessary resources, working with Moroccan and international authorities, and preparing the necessary measures to restore normalcy as soon as possible,” he said in a post on X. “I just conveyed this to President Vivas. This is the moment to build solutions, with responsibility and cooperation.”

News.title: Brit rugby player dies after alleged attack left him brain dead on Turkey holiday
News.content:
Brit rugby player dies after alleged attack left him brain dead on Turkey holiday

Scot James, 34, who played for Maesteg Celtic RFC, was on holiday with family in Turkey when he was declared brain dead on July 11 after an alleged attack

View Image Scot James was on holiday in Turkey when he was allegedly attacked earlier this month

A British rugby player has died after an alleged attack while on a family holiday in Turkey earlier this month left him brain dead.

‌



Scot James, 34, was declared brain dead in Turkey on July 11 after what his family have described as an assault.

‌



He was brought back to the UK last Friday via air ambulance and passed away on Sunday at The Royal Glamorgan hospital in Wales.

‌



Scot, who played for Maesteg Celtic RFC, was described as a "loving father, son, grandson and partner" and an "all-round loveable man" in tributes on social media.

A GoFundMe was initially set up to raise money for the family as they extended their stay in Turkey to remain with Scot, Wales Online reports.

"Peacefully yesterday with all his loved ones around him my beloved brother Scot passed away," wrote his sister Hannah in an update on the GoFundMe page.

‌



"Scot was sadly declared brain dead in Turkey on Saturday 11th July 2026. For 13 days Scot’s family stayed in Turkey to be at Scot’s side as Scot was still on life support as the laws in Turkey are different to ours and they won’t just switch the life support off.

"On Friday 24th July Scot was flown home via air ambulance to the UK with my mother by his side where he was taken to ICU in The Royal Glamorgan hospital. We as a family got to spend and cherish his last few days with Scot and be by his bedside.

"But sadly yesterday afternoon 26/07 Scot decided it was his time to go and us as a family was there to hold his hand while his life support was turned off and while he sadly passed away.

‌



"I’m giving you this update as initially this was set up to help cover the cost of the family staying out in Turkey etc. But as I’ve explained the circumstances have changed and now Scot has passed away.

"So I’m giving this one final push now with this sad news as we was all hoping that the outcome would have been different, but sadly our Scot have passed away due to him having seizures in which it left him brain dead due to his injuries. [SIC]"

The Foreign Office confirmed it is working with local authorities following Scot's death.

‌



An FCDO spokesperson said: “We are supporting the family of a British national who died following an incident in Turkey and are in contact with the local authorities.”

His local rugby club, which hosted a football tournament to raise funds in recent weeks, paid tribute to Scot on social media.

"We are deeply saddened to share the heart-breaking news that our former player, Scot James, sadly passed away yesterday," said Maesteg Celtics RFC on Facebook.

Article continues below

"Everyone at the club is devastated by this news, and our thoughts go out to his family and friends at this difficult time.

"Scot will be remembered as an outstanding player and a great character and friend by everyone who had the pleasure of sharing the field with him."

The Mirror has approached the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Turkish Police Foreign Relations Office for comment.

News.title: European nations to boycott World Cup if Fifa goes ahead with investment plan
News.content:
European football's 55 member associations have voted to boycott World Cups if the sport's governing body proceeds with a plan to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors.

The decision was made at an emergency meeting called to discuss the proposal announced earlier this week by Fifa, which oversees world football.

Uefa, which governs European football, had already made its opposition clear by releasing two damning statements - and that strength of feeling has been reaffirmed.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product," it said on Thursday.

"It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale."

It is understood FA chairwoman Debbie Hewitt and chief executive Mark Bullingham were among those to speak during the meeting, with the atmosphere described as venomous, such was the strength of feeling against the proposals.

Despite being one of eight Fifa vice-presidents, Hewitt had no knowledge of the discussions that Fifa president Gianni Infantino had been having regarding the proposals.

Uefa's boycott would cover all Fifa competitions, including the men's and women's World Cups and Club World Cup, and be triggered if Infantino's proposals are voted through by member associations.

The first time this stance will be tested at a senior tournament is in October, when the Women's World Cup play-offs are due to be held.

News.title: Drought declared across whole of Wales as conditions 'deteriorate'
News.content:
Richard Anthony, whose farm stretches over the Vale of Glamorgan and Bridgend county, said the ground on his land was as hard as a "rock" and had "no moisture at all".

The dry land has left Anthony unable to plant his crops, who added he had "never ever been in this situation" before.

"As soon as we've harvested the one crop, we plant in the next crop, but we can't do any of that now," he said. "I've never seen it as bad as this."

Our wheat deals are down between 20% and 30%. That is massive. we'll have to cope, we will survive, but the knock-on effect is huge."

Anthony said he is concerned that once the rain comes it will not stop, leaving him unable to plant next year's crops.

"It'll go from this to being too wet", he added.

National Farmers Union Cymru president Abi Reader has warned that the cost of the continuing dry and hot weather will have a financial impact on farmers.

"We're going to see costs for these farms rising, because they might be having to buy in extra feed for their livestock, or they might be spending a lot of money carting water," she said.

"We've been in this a long time now, and it's going to take a long time to recover, and absolutely everybody needs to remember that food security starts with water security," she added.

News.title: Why limited war with the US may suit Iran better than peace
News.content:
At first glance, Iran's surprise missile strike on a US base in Jordan earlier this week appeared difficult to explain. The attack effectively ended the fragile pause in direct US-Iran fighting and prompted Washington to resume strikes inside Iran. It was also unusual.

If Tehran's priority had been a ceasefire, the strike is difficult to explain. But if Iranian leaders judge that a controlled confrontation could offer greater strategic leverage, the decision becomes more understandable.

One possible explanation is that Tehran believes that, despite its risks, a limited war serves its interests better.

Today, neither side appears ready for an all-out war. Washington has shown little appetite for a much broader regional conflict that could threaten energy infrastructure in the region, draw in more countries, push oil prices higher, and further stretch US military resources.

Iran may also try to avoid an all-out war because its weakened air defences, vulnerable industrial infrastructure and sanctions-constrained economy make rebuilding losses increasingly difficult and expensive.

Iran may have concluded that this creates room for a strategy based not on military victory but on sustained pressure.

A prolonged ceasefire under current conditions could actually leave Tehran in a weaker position. The US naval blockade of Iranian ports would continue, sanctions would remain, and Iran would still be largely excluded from international energy markets.

News.title: Hundreds of migrants swim from Morocco to Spanish enclave of Ceuta
News.content:
Hundreds of migrants have entered Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco over the past week, the territory's leader has said.

Juan JesÃºs Vivas said the influx is overwhelming resources and urged the Spanish government to intervene. Spain's Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska is expected to visit on Friday, according to news agency Reuters.

Footage showed migrants swimming and using inflatable rings and other flotation devices to swim to Ceuta on Thursday, while others ran through a gate in the border fence.

Ceuta, on Morocco's northern coast, is separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar and has long been a focal point for migrants attempting to reach Europe.

There are conflicting reports on the scale of the crossing, with figures ranging from hundreds to thousands of people.

Spanish media estimated between 2,000 and 3,000 people entered Ceuta on Thursday, according to Reuters, but said that the Guardia Civil had not confirmed the figure.

Meanwhile, Spain's public broadcaster RTVE reported that "hundreds" crossed into the territory during the day. It also said more than 1,500, mostly young Moroccan migrants, had reached Ceuta over the past two weeks.

Vivas said the bodies of 60 people had been recovered at sea in recent months, RTVE reported.

He also added the territory was facing a humanitarian and security emergency, warning that reception centres for unaccompanied minors were operating at several times their intended capacity, according to Reuters.

The surge has prompted comparisons with May 2021, when around 8,000 people entered Ceuta over a matter of days, exacerbating diplomatic tensions with Morocco.

Spain's Ceuta and Melilla enclaves, which are located in North Africa, represent the European Union's only land border with Africa.

Spanish authorities have increased security around the enclaves in recent years through increased surveillance, barrier reinforcement, and improved bilateral relations with Morocco, but people continue to attempt to cross.

News.title: British Airways flight called mayday on approach to Heathrow
News.content:
A British Airways flight issued a "mayday" distress call on its approach to Heathrow Airport earlier this month, according to a statement from France's accident investigation authority.

The call was made on an Airbus A320 flying from Dusseldorf airport in Germany on 6 July following two stall warnings on the aircraft, before it landed without further incident.

The UK's Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) said it was "investigating a serious incident".

A British Airways spokesperson said the airline was assisting the AAIB with its investigation and was not legally able to comment further at this stage.

The French Air Safety Investigation Authority, the BEA, said that as the plane approached Heathrow, there was a data system failure which triggered a stall warning.

The crew then flew the aircraft in a different mode called "alternate law", which removes some automated flight protection systems. Another stall warning then occurred at 3,000 feet - which experts say was likely to have been just miles away from the airport.

The urgency call the crew had already made was upgraded to mayday, indicating imminent danger. The

The BEA website attributed the statement to the AAIB, but the AAIB would not confirm it was from them.

They issued the following statement: "The AAIB is investigating a serious incident involving a commercial aircraft which occurred on 6 July on approach to Heathrow airport."

It said the investigation would be a correspondence investigation, meaning that no team would be sent to carry out field investigations.

Aviation safety investigator David Gleave said there are different forms of mayday calls, and to send an urgency message was "not unusual".

"You could have sick passengers on board who need urgent medical attentionâ¦ so it's up to the captains' discretion as to what they call, but its very unusual for it to be a significant failure on board the aeroplane."

News.title: Greens review social media operation as Polanski row rumbles on
News.content:
The current row began after Polanski shared a single post on Instagram that contained a carousel of 20 pictures.

The re-post was shared to Polanski's 713,000 followers, because he accepted a request to tag him as a collaborator, which on the platform makes him a "co-author," placing it on his page and into his followers' feeds.

Polanski said he had not noticed the offending image among the others on the post.

According to him, he had accepted collaborator tags for eight other posts from the same event in Bristol alone.

Reform UK leader Farage claimed the t-shirt amounted to incitement to murder and his party reported it to the police.

Neither the Metropolitan Police nor Avon and Somerset Police say the incident meets the threshold for further action.

But the political row has continued with Reform UK MP Robert Jenrick calling Polanski a "nasty piece of work", at a news conference earlier on Thursday.

Inside the Green Party, there has been some criticism of Polanski's behaviour online.

He has attracted positive and negative attention for the rate at which he posts, comments, likes and replies across multiple platforms including X, Bluesky, Facebook and Instagram.

And this is not the first time a quick reaction has attracted controversy; last month he had to apologise to police after posting about their response to the Golders Green attack.

One senior party source said it was clear that due diligence had not been done on Polanski's social media output, and that moving forwards he needs "tight controls" to stay credible, while keeping a similar tone of engagement with his followers.

They pointed out that the speed and number of Polanski's interactions came with a "small upside" but a "colossal downside", and with the latest incident he had "shot himself in the foot at precisely the wrong time".

It comes as recent polling suggests the Green Party has lost ground to Labour, following Andy Burnham's election as Labour leader, and down from a peak earlier this year.

They added their concerns about a wider problem with the party's vetting on social media and of candidates, including around antisemitic posts in recent months.

Several candidates in recent elections have stood down over their social media activity, with two candidates arrested during May's local elections, and another suspended after being elected.

But Green Party peer and former deputy mayor of London Baroness Jones said the criticism of Polanski's Instagram re-post seemed to be "mainly from our opponents, not internal discussions".

She said that her party leader had "made a mistake", adding "we've all done it and got flak."

But she added: "His online presence is what makes him relatable".

Along with relatability, comes popularity: Polanski is the second-most followed UK leader on Instagram after Nigel Farage. The Greens surpassed other parties to become the most popular on the platform this year.

It is also seen as where a good portion of their voters spend time, as they are the most popular party among the under-30s, according to pollsters YouGov.

News.title: Burnham says he told Trump UK will be pragmatic about North Sea oil
News.content:
Although the government has not made any announcements on the issue, Trump has praised what he perceives as a change of stance by the UK government.

In a social media post, published the day before Burnham became prime minister,, external Trump wrote: "The People of Aberdeen, in Scotland, are dancing in the streets because the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has stated that he will be opening up, all the way, the invaluable North Sea Oil!"

This week, when asked about his conversation with Burnham, Trump said: "He said he's going to open up North Sea oil.

"If he does that, you're going to be a wealthy country."

He later added: "You buy a lot of your energy, as you know, from the North Sea. You buy from Norway and Norway gets it from the North Sea... Norway's got trillions of dollars in the bank."

"Scotland has a better part of the North Sea."

Asked about Trump's comments, Burnham said: "I indicated in the phone call that we had a week last Monday that I would take a pragmatic approach when it comes to the North Sea, and that is my intention as we go forward from here."

In response, Green Party leader Zack Polanski said: "Our country is burning. Crops are failing. Thousands have been killed by extreme heat.

"Allowing new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea will worsen the climate breakdown putting more lives at risk and doing untold damage to our economy.

"It's not too late for Burnham to do the right thing and commit to leaving dangerous fossil fuels in the ground."

The Conservatives and Reform have urged the government to approve more drilling in the North Sea, arguing it would reduce energy prices.

Last year, Tory Party leader Kemi Badenoch said it would be "absurd" for the UK to leave "vital resources untapped".

Some Labour MPs have expressed unease about more drilling, with Rachael Maskell urging the government to "follow the climate science because we have got a climate emergency".

Simon Francis, from the End Fuel Poverty Coalition, said: "No household struggling with their energy bills will see a penny come off by drilling more from the North Sea.

"Gas is sold at the global market prices, so whatever is pumped out is sold to the highest bidder, not handed to British billpayers at a discount."

Sir Keir's government had already made concessions, allowing "tie-backs" - production in unlicensed areas close to or connected to already licensed areas.

Currently, the debate over North Sea drilling has focused on two oil and gas fields - Rosebank and Jackdaw, located in Scotland.

In 2022 and 2023, regulators approved drilling at the sites, but that was overturned in 2025 following a legal challenge.

The legal process is ongoing, but the government will at some point have to decide whether to permit companies to produce oil in the two areas.

Other oil and gas licences have been approved in recent years but remain largely undeveloped.

If he wanted to encourage more drilling in the North Sea, Burnham could also opt to scrap the Energy Profits Level, also known as the windfall tax.

News.title: Man impaled by a hiking pole treks 10 miles down mountain
News.content: David Cifaldi was hiking Montanaâs Granite Peak with friends when he slipped and was impaled by his trekking pole. Remarkably, the pole missed all major organs. Rather than call for a helicopter rescue, Cifaldi hiked 10 miles down the mountain on foot. As a wound care nurse, he immediately shifted into professional mode, assessing and managing his injury throughout the ordeal.

News.title: Palestine Action ban to be reviewed by Supreme Court
News.content:
The controversial ban under terrorism legislation of the protest group Palestine Action will be reviewed by the Supreme Court.

In a major blow to the Home Office, the court confirmed on Thursday that it had given the group's co-founder permission to appeal the ban which came into effect in July 2025.

While the full details of the reasons for the appeal are yet to be published, the BBC understands they relate to Huda Ammori's argument that the ban breaches human rights.

Officials at the court say the appeal will be expedited - which means it will be heard after the summer break. The eventual outcome of the case could have major implications for terrorism legislation in the UK.

The decision comes weeks after the end of the first major trial of members of the group which had caused more than Â£1m of damage to a defence firm near Bristol with an Israeli parent company. Four members of that break-in team were jailed, with one also sentenced for causing grievous bodily harm on a police officer who was hit with a sledgehammer.

Separately, more than 2,000 people are facing potential trial for protesting against the ban by declaring their support for a proscribed terrorism group in mass demonstrations.

The battle over the banning of Palestine Action has now gone on for more than year.

Former Home Secretary Yvette Cooper banned the group on advice from the police and security officials after an escalating spate of break-ins targeting Elbit, an Israeli-owned defence firm.

The High Court initially ruled that the ban was unlawful - but five judges on the Court of Appeal then overruled it, unanimously deciding the home secretary had acted lawfully and within her powers to proscribe Palestine Action.

That decision by the Court of Appeal will now be reviewed by the Supreme Court.

News.title: Bank holds interest rates but says it is ready to raise them if Iran war escalates
News.content:
The Bank of England has kept interest rates unchanged for the fifth meeting in a row but has indicated it could raise them if the Iran war escalates.

It expects inflation - the rate at which prices rise - to pick up due to volatile oil and gas prices caused by the Middle East conflict, although the peak will be slightly lower than previously thought.

The Bank voted to hold interest rates at 3.75% at its latest meeting.

Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey warned the future of UK interest rates depended on whether the US led war against Iran continues.

While major uncertainties remain because of the war, the Bank predicts the UK economy will grow this year by more than previously forecast.

Bailey told the BBC: "If we get a continuation of this conflict going on and oil prices stay above $100 a barrel... the odds are that interest rates will have to go up higher."

But he also said if a ceasefire, and memorandum of understanding, is established and sticks that would make a difference.

"So it depends on how the events in the Middle East, frankly, unfold. And sadly, we all know this is highly unpredictable," Bailey said.

"What goes on in the Gulf is not, I'm afraid, under our control."

Three members of the Bank's nine-member rate-setting committee voted for a hike, one more than the previous meeting - with that member explicitly citing the collapse of the US-Iran memorandum of understanding for their vote to raise rates.

However, speaking at an earlier news conference, Bailey said the Bank was not currently moving towards raising interest rates.

"Please do not leave this room thinking that the Bank of England is edging towards a hike, because frankly, there's nothing in what I said, and I think any of us have said along those lines," he told reporters.

If the Iran war continues and oil prices hover around $100 a barrel, then a rate rise seems likely. But many in the markets expect tensions to subside in the coming weeks, ahead of crucial elections across the US in the autumn.

News.title: Four people die after busiest day for small-boat crossings this year
News.content:
Four people died trying to cross the Channel overnight after the busiest day for small-boat crossings so far this year saw 752 arrivals in the UK.

One man died after a vessel capsized off France's northern coast late on Wednesday, local officials said, with a one-year-old child among those hurt.

Seven hours later, three people were found dead aboard a small boat after launching from Dunkirk overnight, some 100km (62 miles) up the coast.

French officials confirmed their deaths as the Home Office reported that Wednesday saw the highest number of crossings in a single day this year, with nine boats reaching the UK.

Local authorities in France said the first boat capsized off the coast at Hardelot around 23:30 local time (21:30 GMT) on Wednesday.

The man is thought to have been in his 30s or 40s, officials added. Six other people including the child sustained minor injuries.

Local officials said the vessel was a "taxi" boat - which cruise along the coast and pick up their paying customers who are waiting in the sea.

Security officials "neutralised" the boat and an investigation into the incident has been launched.

The second boat launched from the Dunkirk area overnight was spotted near a breakwater off the coast at 06:00, the French coastguard said.

Search and rescue officials subsequently found three unconscious people aboard. Their deaths were later confirmed by emergency medical personnel.

A UK government spokesperson said: "Every death in the Channel is a tragedy and a stark reminder of the dangers posed by criminal gangs exploiting vulnerable people for profit."

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, speaking separately about small boat crossings on Thursday, said the UK had made "significant progress" on reducing the number of arrivals.

But, asked by reporters about US President Donald Trump's remark that the UK had a "huge immigration problem", Burnham said there was much still to do "to get those numbers right down".

News.title: Homes flooded and residents evacuated after quarry 'incident'
News.content:
Residents of a village on the outskirts of Cardiff have been evacuated after a flood on Thursday afternoon.

Roads have been shut in Gwaelod-y-Garth, with reports of water up to 5ft (1.5m) deep in some homes.

Emergency services are at the scene and people have been advised to avoid the area.

The Breedon Group confirmed there had been an "incident in its quarry".

"Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities while engaging with the local community as we respond to the situation," the company said.

News.title: England on track for record heat-related deaths this year, UKHSA estimates
News.content:
England is on track this year for the highest number of heat-related deaths since records began, according to estimates by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

In a preliminary assessment, it said there were an estimated 2,877 heat-related deaths during the May and June heatwaves, almost double the figure for the whole of last year.

An estimated 753 deaths were associated with the 24-27 May heatwave and a further 2,124 with the one from 21-28 June. Definitive figures are expected in early 2027.

Both spells broke Met Office UK monthly temperature records, with 35.1C (95.2F) recorded at Kew Gardens on 26 May and 38.0C recorded at Lingwood, Norfolk on 26 June.

The current record for heat-related deaths was set in 2022, when 2,985 deaths were recorded.

Report author Dr Ross Thompson, from the UKHSA, said "while the figures are interim, they suggest that, if we experience more periods of hot weather this summer, we could see the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record".

Thompson added: "These figures highlight the significant danger that very hot weather can pose to people's health.

"This is particularly true for those who are more vulnerable including older adults and people with underlying medical conditions."

He said "as the climate becomes warmer, we can expect periods of hot weather to become longer, more frequent and more extreme", adding that it is vital the country is prepared to deal with higher temperatures.

Earlier this week parts of the UK sweltered through another heatwave that peaked on Wednesday, with temperature reaching 35.2C in Writtle, Essex.

Cooler conditions and some rain are on the way for some on Thursday and into the weekend, but likely not in the driest areas.

News.title: Missing child, 5, dies after being found in water
News.content:
A missing five-year-old child has died after being found in a body of water.

West Mercia Police said officers had responded to reports of a missing child in Badsey, Worcestershire, on Wednesday evening.

The child was found unresponsive in the water and a short time later was pronounced dead.

The force said they were believed to have drowned and called it "an incredibly tragic incident", adding there was no third-party involvement in the death.

Officers said they would not be identifying the child's sex out of respect for the family.

West Midlands Ambulance Service said they were called at 18:50 BST, sending an ambulance, two paramedic officers and the Midlands Air Ambulance Critical Care Car to the scene.

A spokesperson said: "On arrival we discovered one patient, a young child.

"Ambulance staff and police worked quickly to treat the patient, but sadly, it became apparent nothing could be done to save them and they were confirmed dead at the scene."

News.title: Suspected Kinahan gang leader faces extradition
News.content:
Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan is to be extradited back to Ireland, BBC News NI understands.

He was arrested in Dubai under a warrant issued by the Irish courts in April but has fought attempts to extradite him.

However, his appeals have been unsuccessful and he is due to be flown back to Ireland within weeks.

GardaÃ­ (Irish police) now expect authorities in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to sign his extradition which will formally commence the extradition process.

GardaÃ­ expect this will take place very quickly.

Bringing the suspected gang leader back to Ireland will now be the subject of a major security operation between the gardaÃ­ and the Irish Defence Forces.

The US government imposed sanctions on him in April 2022 after he and other members of his family were identified as leaders of the Kinahan organised crime cartel.

Kinahan also had ties to the world of sport via his now defunct boxing management company MTK Global, which represented more than 100 boxers including Tyson Fury and Carl Frampton.

However, Kinahan is now expected to face the Irish courts in the coming weeks and has previously been named as the head of the drug cartel.

The Irish authorities are expected to prosecute him for his involvement in leading an organised crime group.

An extradition agreement is in place between the UAE and Ireland and it was used to extradite Sean McGovern, a "senior lieutenant" in the organised crime group.

He was sentenced to 24 years in prison last month for directing the activities of a criminal organisation.

News.title: Dad pays tribute to son who died after sea rescue
News.content:
A seven-year-old boy who died a week after being rescued from the sea "never failed to bring happiness" to others, his father has told the BBC.

Musa Ahmed and five relatives got into difficulty in the water in West Mersea on 22 July, having travelled to the Essex seaside from east London.

His 15-year-old cousin, Sameeha Rahman, and her mother Shelina, 41, drowned at the scene.

Shahin Ahmed said his son was "a unique and happy personality, a sphere of joy" in a tribute after his death on Tuesday evening.

"Everyone who knew him had a unique relationship with him. He made every person feel special and never failed to bring happiness," Ahmed said.

"He was everyone's favourite and he made everyone feel like his favourite."

Ahmed also referred to Islam and said Musa "embodied" traits of the Prophet Muhammad.

News.title: Friday racing tips: Best bets and odds on Glorious Goodwood day four
News.content:
Friday’s Glorious Goodwood tips

Defiantly (Goodwood, 13.50) – 1pt each-way @ 13/2 ( Bet365 )

Bunyola Bay (Goodwood, 15.00) – 1pt each-way @ 10/1 (William Hill)

Night Raider (Goodwood, 15.35) – 2pts win @ 7/2 (Ladbrokes)

Kenergy (Goodwood, 17.20) – 1pt each-way @ 33/1 (Betfred)

It’s day four at Glorious Goodwood and there’s another cracking day’s action ahead. Our horse racing correspondent Jonathan Doidge has four selections using the best odds from betting sites for you to ponder.

Coral Goodwood Handicap (13.50, Goodwood)

Regular readers will now know that I love these staying handicaps, because we get similar fields meeting each other time and again and, therefore, we usually have some reliable form to work with.

This is a high-class handicap and is an extreme test of stamina, one that we know suits DEFIANTLY, who represents a team you’ll often find me siding with, that of Joseph O’Brien and Dylan Browne McGonagle.

Aged four, he’s still got time on his side and he remains progressive and unexposed at this stage of his career. His trainer stepped him up to a similar trip in the Ascot Stakes at last month’s Royal meeting and he produced a very good effort.

We now know that he stays extreme distances because he was up with the pace more or less throughout on a stiffer track than this one. He also showed a great attitude up the home straight and, after 2m4f, he was beaten by just a head by Kizlyar.

That was on fast ground and in first-time blinkers, and he retains the headgear for this race. It’s been cracking the flags down here in Sussex all week and conditions will again suit him, while a 4lb rise still gives him the look of a well handicapped horse on what is just his second start in this sphere with a solid price available on horse racing betting sites.

Valiancy is also unexposed and has been the ante-post favourite, after a staying on sixth of 16 over 1m6f at Royal Ascot and you can see why thoughts have turned towards an extreme trip for the William Haggas-trained four-year-old.

Believeitanducan has carried all before him this season and should again be a serious player. He’s scored three times at around 2m. There’s no reason why he won’t see out this new trip but he still has it to prove.

Neither St Mawes nor Alphonse Le Grande is dismissed but, in a really good race, I will be surprised if the selection is not in the first three and Defiantly may just prove good enough to bag his first handicap success.

Goodwood day four racing tip 1: Defiantly (Goodwood, 13.50) – 1pt each-way @ 13/2 (Bet365)

Coral Golden Mile (Heritage Handicap) (15.00, Goodwood)

Never an easy puzzle to solve and generally it’s a race where low drawn horses do well but there’s been a couple of recent winners (2023, stall 18 and 2024, stall 21) where high numbers have prevailed.

That offers some encouragement that stall 11 is not the worst of draws for my suggestion in this, BUNYOLA BAY. Richard Hannon is very much among the winners this week and, despite the availability of stable jockey Sean Levey, the best in the business has been booked for the mount, Ryan Moore.

You’d like to think that’s significant for this handicap newcomer who has won two of four starts and was clearly tilting at windmills when a well beaten 50/1 chance in last month’s Irish Derby (1m4f, good).

He’s back down in trip for this and I think he can bounce back. He’s by Ghiayyath, out of an Italian Group 3 1m winner, so you’d think his pilot will be likely to try to get him out and make use of him from not too far off the pace, while we know he’s already won over further than this, so he’ll have no problems seeing it out.

He acts on fast ground and although a mark of 102 is no ‘gimme’, there looks to be improvement in him and at a double-figure price on betting apps I think we can take that chance.

There are plenty of others with claims, not least Beagle Bay, although he was taken out of his latest intended engagement due to quick ground, so that would be a concern, while Indalo, Blue Brother and Scoville, who I think we’re yet to see the best of, are potential contenders.

Goodwood day four racing tip 2: Bunyola Bay (Goodwood, 15.00) – 1pt each-way @ 10/1 (William Hill)

King George Qatar Stakes (Group 2) (15.35, Goodwood)

He’s the favourite for this and carries a 3lb penalty but I still like the chance of NIGHT RAIDER, who is enjoying a fine season since being gelded.

Karl Burke’s five-year-old won the Group 3 Palace House Stakes at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) before adding the Group 2 Temple Stakes (5f, good to soft) at Haydock earlier in the campaign.

Don’t be fooled by the 0 against his name last time as we all saw when effect the draw had at Royal Ascot and he actually ‘won his race’ of those in the middle of the track, finishing tenth in a field of 26.

He likes to be out in front, as does one of his chief opponents, Jakajaro, and they’re drawn apart in this race so hopefully won’t be cutting each other’s throat in doing so. Rumstar, Jm Jungle and American Affair are others with claims if at their best, while Asfoora doesn’t seem to be quite on her game this term, for whatever reason.

I’m sticking with Night Raider, who should appreciate this downhill sprint track and will hopefully not see another rival.

Goodwood day four racing tip 3: Night Raider (Goodwood, 16.35) – 2pts win @ 7/2 (Ladbrokes)

World Pool Bet With The tote Handicap (17.20, Goodwood)

A maximum field of 14 has been declared for this 0-90 handicap over 1m3f and I’d like to take a chance at a big price on handicap newcomer KENERGY.

George Baker trains this three-year-old who cost €77,000 as a yearling. He’s had just the three qualifying runs so far, all on Kempton’s Polytrack and over 7f or 1m. He’s shown similar promise in all three and his most recent effort saw him stay on for fourth place over the shorter of those trips.

It’s his first try on turf, so he’ll have to prove himself on quick ground but I think the handicapper has been pretty fair with a mark of 79 for his introduction to this sphere and the marked step up in trip is what really interests me with him.

He’s brother to the useful French 1m1f-1m3f winner Veronesi, so it’s possible that this longer distance will enable him to really show his capabilities and at the prices I think we can take that chance.

I have a lot of respect for Astracornus, who could be suited by this slightly longer trip in his case, while Into The Light could find more for first-time headgear and Devil’s Peak is another to consider but a small stakes each-way play on Kenergy is my idea of a wager.

Yellowstone star Cole Hauser is looking forward to season two of the hit show’s spin-off Dutton Ranch.

The 51-year-old actor reprised his role as Rip Wheeler for the new series, which arrived on Paramount in May.

Last week, Hauser admitted there had been “challenges” for the new show, particularly the fact that creator Taylor Sheridan was not in the writers’ room.

Following the conclusion of the first season, showrunner Chad Feehan was replaced by a new head writer, Benjamin Cavell.

Speaking to People about the decision, Hauser said: “We have a wonderful new showrunner, Benjamin Cavell, and I’ve been talking to him. He’s a very special guy, and I think the future is bright — not only for myself, but Beth [Kelly Reilly] and Carter [Finn Little] and the show in general. I think this is going to be a really nice next step.”

open image in gallery Cole Hauser says ‘the future is bright’ for ‘Yellowstone’ spin-off ‘Dutton Ranch’ ( Paramount+ )

Cavell is known for co-creating the Stephen King adaptation The Stand and has also worked on shows including Homeland, SEAL Team and The Institute.

Dutton Ranch was the first series in the Yellowstone universe not to be written by Sheridan, although he remained involved in the show as an executive producer.

“There were challenges, you know?” Hauser told Film Inside NYC earlier this month. “Not having Taylor there, for us to really kind of be able to work with these new writers, these new directors, these people... everything had changed.”

He added: “I enjoy a challenge – it certainly was a challenge. We worked our asses off this year. And I don’t think a lot of the outside noise or the thought of ‘what’s the weight of the show?’ was really apparent to me at the time.”

Speculation about potential behind-the-scenes drama on the spin-off show swirled after actor Ed Harris told Variety that he was unhappy with his role during the first season.

open image in gallery Kelly Reilly and Cole Hauser in 'Dutton Ranch' ( Paramount+ )

“Prior to signing on for it, I was talked to quite a bit about what the season was, and what my character was going to do – and that I was one of the four main characters,” Harris told the outlet, adding, “And that wasn’t really the case.”

“I said, ‘I’m feeling underused and inconsequential’,” he continued. “I was just a little frustrated, to tell you the truth.”

Despite Harris’s complaints, the Oscar-nominated actor will return for the second season, and he said his character will have “a little bit more to do.”

Season two of Dutton Ranch is set to begin filming in February.

Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has announced plans to cut hundreds of jobs as part of a major transformation.

This decision follows the group's ongoing recovery from a major cyber attack that halted production last year, compounded by US tariff measures.

Fewer than 300 roles are understood to be affected at the UK’s largest car manufacturer. JLR, employing around 30,000 in the UK and 10,000 abroad, has not disclosed the specific locations of these job losses.

The majority of its vehicle production takes place at UK facilities, including Solihull in the West Midlands and Halewood in Merseyside, as well as in Slovakia.

A company spokesman said: “As we evolve our operating model to accelerate the growth of our house of brands and deliver our next-generation vehicles, we are transforming our business to improve decision-making and performance.

open image in gallery It is understood that fewer than 300 jobs will be affected at the UK’s largest car maker ( Jaguar Land Rover/PA )

“As part of our ongoing transformation initiatives, we have launched a limited redeployment and displacement programme.

“Impacted colleagues will be supported to find alternative roles wherever possible, alongside the option of voluntary early exit.”

Last month, JLR said it planned to cut around £1.7 billion in costs over the coming years to help support its recovery.

It indicated it would secure the savings through cuts in areas like materials, warranty and fixed costs.

JLR has been recovering from a cyber attack last year which had major impact on the business, its employees and the wider UK economy.

The carmaker was forced to stop production at its UK factories for five weeks from September 1 last year, which weighed on sales in late 2025 and led to heavy financial losses.

Nevertheless, in May, the firm revealed a further recovery in sales.

The group reported revenues of £6.9 billion for the three months to March 31, up 51.4% against the previous quarter.

But this was still down 11.1% year-on-year.

Revenues for the year were 20.9% lower at £22.9 billion after a heavy impact from the production shutdown.

Volumes for the year were also dragged lower by the impact of US tariffs, “market challenges” in China and the planned “wind down” of a number of outgoing Jaguar models.
