John Oliver has a message for Buc-ee’s: Buc off.

The Last Week Tonight host is trolling the beloved travel center chain with a limited-edition line of parody merchandise after mocking what he described as the company’s aggressive efforts to police its trademark.

Founded in Texas in 1982, Buc-ee’s has become famous for its roadside mega-stores and its logo featuring a grinning cartoon beaver in a red baseball cap.

During a recent episode of his show, the host accused the Texas-founded gas station giant of “outright bullying” other companies with “frivolous” trademark infringement lawsuits.

“It turns out Buc-ee’s loves to sue other companies, particularly those with animal mascots,” Oliver, 49, said.

The British comedian played a news clip featuring Jarrad Hewett, founder of the small apparel brand Nut Huggers, who recalled receiving a letter from Buc-ee’s demanding he stop using “cartoons, rodents, the colors red, yellow and brown, baseball hats, and only front-facing images.”

open image in gallery John Oliver ridiculed Buc-ee's over its string of trademark lawsuits against companies using cartoon rodents as logos ( HBO )

open image in gallery Bucc-ee's are popular travel centers, known for their exceptionally clean bathrooms and wide selection of snacks ( Getty )

“The initial request came in a little hot and heavy,” Hewett said. “They suggested they owned all cartoon rodents.”

“Oh come on, Buc-ee’s! You don’t own all cartoon rodents,” Oliver exclaimed before rattling off several famous examples, including Mickey Mouse, Minnie Mouse and Stuart Little.

Reacting to the company’s “ridiculous” list of demands, the Emmy-winning host called them out for inconsistencies.

“If front-facing images are OK, why the f*** did Buc-ee’s go after the Teddy’s [Market] koala? That bear is looking you right in the eyes. He is peering into your very soul,” Oliver quipped, describing “Buc-ee’s constant complaint that no one else has the right to use animal logos” as “absurd.”

He noted that the company has won a majority of its lawsuits after several of the defendants settled. “And that’s probably because most just don’t have the resources to fight a company this big,” the host said.

open image in gallery Oliver launched 'Buc-Off' a parody merchandise line, which is available to purchase until September 8 ( HBO )

“We very much have the will to get into a fight with Buc-ee’s,” Oliver flouted, introducing a new line of merchandise, called Buc-Off, which is available for purchase on Buc-Off.com until September 8. All proceeds will be donated to Hunger Free America.

The merchandise of clothing, umbrellas, and water tumblers features Last Week Tonight’s squirrel mascot, Mr. Nutterbutter, inside a yellow circle.

“If any prominent gas station chain out there has an issue with our new logo and products and wants to get lawyers involved, then you know what? Bring it the f*** on,” Oliver dared. “The next move is yours.”

The Independent has contacted Buc-ee’s for comment.

Buc-ee’s has filed more than a dozen lawsuits, mostly against small businesses that have used cartoon animals for their logos. In a March lawsuit against Ohio-based gas station Mickey’s, obtained by The Independent, Buc-ee’s claimed that its logo featuring a smiling cartoon moose set against a red hexagon was confusing customers, affecting its “iconic brand.”

British farmers are facing a perfect storm as drought conditions have been declared across half of England, putting further strain on already struggling crop yields.

It follows pressure on food supplies caused by the war in Iran, years of higher fertiliser and animal feed costs due to the invasion of Ukraine, and a series of extreme weather events that continue to hit the UK.

By the middle of July, England had only received 3 per cent of its average rainfall, with the Met Office not forecasting heavy showers in the coming weeks.

Experts are now warning that the extreme drought conditions will worsen supply shortages and push grocery prices even higher.

Andrew Opie, the director of food & sustainability policy at the British Retail Consortium, said: “Climate change continues to create challenges for retailers and their suppliers. Extreme weather, including drought, can affect crop yields and place upward pressure on prices.”

The Independent spoke to farmers and experts to find out how England’s droughts could affect food supply.

open image in gallery Farmers have seen significant reductions in crop yields ( PA )

Vegetables

Field vegetables, which are often grown in areas where there has been little rainfall this summer, are especially susceptible to the current drought conditions in England, University of Oxford professor Paul Behrens said.

This includes potatoes, carrots, onions, cabbage, lettuce, spinach, kale, brassicas, pumpkins, and cucumbers.

Julian Marks, the chief executive of international vegetable farming business Barfoots, has seen crop yield reductions of up to 20 per cent.

“We've had a variety of crops affected by the heat, including sweet corn, green beans, garden peas, and tender stem broccoli.”

“There have been examples already of shortages due to weather conditions,” he said, adding that shoppers will see more gaps in supply later in the autumn.

“It’s unlikely that these issues will continue beyond the autumn. But the implications for UK production in future years are very serious.”

Wholesale prices have already spiked, with the average cost of a homegrown cauliflower reaching £1.62 a head in Defra’s latest figures, up from £1.06 four weeks earlier and 89p at the same point last year.

Fruit

Jonathan Lukies, a farmer from Cammas Hall fruit farm, said the drought conditions have affected all of his crops, including strawberries, blackberries, blueberries, cherries and pumpkins.

Unlike vegetables, Britons are less likely to see an impact on fruit in the supermarkets. Only around 17 per cent of the UK’s fruit is grown on British farms, meaning supply and prices will only be affected if supermarkets can’t find replacements from other parts of the world, Mr Lukies said.

“If people want to eat English strawberries and cherries and things like that, there will definitely be less of them than previous years because of this extreme weather.”

open image in gallery Animals are suffering from heat stress as a result of the drought conditions ( PA )

Meat & dairy

Heat stress on animals is causing a reduction in the supply of meat products, including beef, chicken, and pork.

This will subsequently reduce egg production, and could cut milk production by up to 20 per cent.

Derek Watson, an associate professor in cultural management at the University of Sunderland, said it would affect all livestock.

“[It’s] very temperamental. If there's a change in environment, that will affect their production,” he said.

“These impacts could last well into 2027, possibly you know a year from Christmas.”

Cereals

Cereal harvests are also struggling, with Mr Lukies’ farm losing a quarter of its wheat crop this year.

“We've had little or no rain since April, apart from a couple of inches in June, but it was sort of too late for the wheat.”

Mr Watson said a reduction in cereal crops will have a knock-on effect further down the line on baking supplies, like flour, and “you’ll see certain retailers having to force up their prices”.

Limited cereal crops, like wheat and barley, will also affect animal feed, and subsequently, the production of meat and milk.

A Defra spokesperson said: “We will always protect the food security of this country to ensure that people have access to nutritious, affordable food.

“To help deliver this, we focused on strengthening national food security, investing a record £11.7 billion in sustainable and profitable farming and billions more in the development of new technology and climate resilient crops to increase yields.”

Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has launched his own cooking show to teach Americans how to cook healthy, inexpensive meals — including some inspired by his sauerkraut-heavy diet.

Kennedy, 72, who has championed the “Make America Healthy Again” movement, launched The Real Food Show Thursday to help Americans make sense of the new dietary guidelines and prepare healthy meals for less than $5 a serving. He also warned that he will eat anything, so viewers should be prepared.

“I don’t have a gag reflex,” Kennedy said.

For the first episode, Kennedy is joined by celebrity chef Andrew Gruel to make crispy salmon cakes with an apple, white bean and greens salad.

However, Kennedy, a lover of fermented foods, says the cooking show will also feature recipes including some of his fermented favorites — kimchi and sauerkraut, he told USA Today.

open image in gallery Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. launched his new cooking show Thursday, which he says will teach Americans how to cook healthy, inexpensive meals ( HHS/The Real Food Show )

The new set of dietary guidelines for Americans, released this past January to provide recommendations for a healthy diet, prioritizes protein and encourages consuming less sugar and processed foods.

“When we published the dietary guidelines, there was immediately sort of a good reaction, but also trepidation from the public and from critics saying that this food is a lot more expensive than the ultra-processed food that we’ve been eating,” Kennedy said. “And that’s not true.”

In his interview with USA Today, Kennedy discussed his deep love for the strongly-scented fermented cabbage

“I used to carry it with me, but I got too many complaints,” he said, noting it was mainly his wife who had an issue with the pungent dish being taken on-the-go with him.

“It’s hard to carry without spilling it. And when you spill it, it causes other problems.”

Fermented foods such as sauerkraut, yogurt, kimchi and sourdough, are good for gut health because they are packed with probiotics, or living organisms that balance the bacteria in the gut.

open image in gallery RFK Jr. said some of the dishes will feature one of his favorite foods, sauerkraut ( Getty )

The HHS Secretary also noted the correct way of eating the fermented fare.

“The way you’re supposed to eat it is bite for bite,” he said. “You take a bite of the meat, take a bite of the sauerkraut. This is kind of the prescribed, perfect way of eating it. You know, I don’t do that perfectly every time that I try.”

It’s not just Kennedy following the fermented foods diet in the Trump administration. Vice President JD Vance, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy have also taken to the pungent dish. Kennedy said they all lost weight following the diet.

He also bemoaned that Americans have “forgotten how to cook,” and are instead opting to spend money eating out or ordering unhealthy takeout.

“Fast food is not less expensive,” he said. “That meal costs $12 to $14. People can eat a lot cheaper at home and a lot better food. But many Americans have forgotten how to cook. It’s becoming a lost art.”

However, the price of food at home and at restaurants each rose .02 percent from May to June, according to the consumer price index.

Kennedy’s next episode is set to feature celebrity chef Robert Irvine.

News.title: Audience member faints on opening night of London play during graphic scene
News.content:

The opening night performance of Cleansed at London’s Almeida Theatre saw Sarah Kane’s provocative play live up to its reputation – with one audience member fainting during a graphic scene.

First staged in 1998, Cleansed is one of five plays by the late playwright Kane, who died by suicide in 1999 at the age of 28. It is noteworthy for its visceral violence, prolonged nudity, and dark themes.

Previous productions of the play have drawn similar responses from some theatregoers, with the 2016 version at the National Theatre making headlines thanks to a spate of faintings and walkouts among the crowd.

During Wednesday’s (29 July) press night performance of the play, directed for the Almeida by Rebecca Frecknall, an audience member was seen receiving assistance from staff before being helped from the auditorium.

open image in gallery Stuart Thompson in 'Cleansed' at the Almeida ( Marc Brenner )

In a statement, a spokesperson for the Almeida told The Independent: “One audience member required assistance during last night's performance of Cleansed. Our Front of House team were on hand to provide care and the audience member was quick to recover.

“We will continue to warn audiences of the content in the production on the Almeida website – here , on the booking page, in pre-visit emails, and on Front of House signage in the theatre.”

The content warning for Cleansed reads: “This production includes prolonged nudity, torture, mutilation, murder, sex, incest, violence including sexual violence, forced eating, suicide including hanging, drug abuse and drugging, gender reassignment surgery as well as homophobic and misogynistic language, needles and blood.”

Cleansed is ostensibly set in a university campus, and follows a sadistic ringleader (played here by Leo Bill) who tortures and abuses a disparate group of outsiders.

Speaking to The Independent earlier this month, Frecknall and Bill were asked about the play’s propensity for causing audience members to faint.

open image in gallery Lizzie Connolly and Leo Bill in 'Cleansed' ( Marc Brenner )

“It’s certainly not the aim,” Frecknall said, “but I don’t think it was [director Katie Mitchell’s] aim when she did it at the National. People have physical reactions to all types of works; it’s just some get reported more than others.”

Bill said he had had “quite a lot” of friends and acquaintances tell him they were “scared” to see the play due to its content.

“It’s like, ‘Well, we could all go and watch a Noël Coward play,’” he said, “And that’s fine – but what world are we in, where we are afraid to be challenged? It all becomes about that, about, like, ‘oh, some hands get chopped off.’ Whereas actually, it’s so beautiful.

“And the beauty in [Cleansed] is so much more important than whether somebody faints or not.”

Cleansed is at the Almeida Theatre until 29 August.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI), email jo@samaritans.org, or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call the National Suicide Prevention Helpline on 1-800-273-TALK (8255). This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

News.title: UK economy to flatline, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Britain’s economy is set to almost grind to a halt for the rest of the year, the Bank of England has warned.

Growth will drop to just 0.1pc per quarter, the Bank predicted, slowing sharply after a strong start to 2026.

Higher petrol prices and energy bills, a weak jobs market and rising mortgage costs are all draining confidence and spending power from the economy.

Inflation, which slowed to a 15-month low of 2.6pc in June, is also expected to rise again to 3.2pc later this year, the Bank warned.

Andrew Bailey, the Bank’s Governor, said inflation had “fallen faster than we’d expected” but warned that war in the Middle East would lead to a fresh spike.

He added that growth would “weaken slightly further in the near term as the effects of the conflict weigh further on demand”.

The Bank also predicted that unemployment will rise back above 5pc in the coming months, limiting workers’ ability to ask for higher wages to cope with rising living costs.

It presents a challenging backdrop for Andy Burnham and his Chancellor, John Healey, who have pledged to help voters struggling with the cost of living.

The forecasts came as policymakers led by Mr Bailey held interest rates at 3.75pc.

Although three members of the nine-strong Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted for higher rates, up from two at the previous meeting, the Governor dismissed suggestions the Bank is moving towards higher interest rates.

The public should “not… [think] the Bank of England is edging towards a hike,” Mr Bailey said.

“Frankly there is nothing I have said, or any of us have said, along those lines. We took a decision today to leave the Bank Rate unchanged and that is the relevant conclusion.”

Clare Lombardelli, a Deputy Governor, said voting to keep rates at 3.75pc “was not a close judgement”, calling the decision “pretty clear” given slowing inflation in the domestic economy.

Officials are monitoring the economy for any signs that increases in oil, gas and petrol prices caused by the war in Iran are creeping into higher costs and wages in the wider economy.

Mr Bailey said: “The possibility of repeated resumptions of conflict, combined with lower than usual European gas stock levels and a fall in global refining output, mean that risks to energy prices lie to the upside.”

He added: “Reassuringly, there are few signs so far that second-round effects are generating more broad-based inflationary pressures.”

Companies are struggling to pass higher costs on to their customers because of the economy’s weakness, he added.

Workers are typically securing only modest pay rises as the weak jobs market leaves them in a poor position to push for bigger salaries.

Mr Bailey stressed there are still major risks to the outlook given the war and promised to “monitor the situation carefully” and was “ready to adjust our stance”.

“It is our job to ensure that inflation gets back to the 2pc target and stays there, and that is what we will do,” he said.

Borrowing costs dropped in financial markets after the decision.

The Government’s two-year borrowing cost fell from 4.44pc to 4.34pc, the sharpest fall in a month.

The FTSE 250 index of mid-sized UK companies rose 0.8pc to a record high of 24,184.10.

Traders still believe the Bank will raise interest rates twice within a year.

However, Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said rate rises “remain more a threat than a reality”.

He said there was evidence of disinflation in the economy and interest rates could be “cut to 3pc in 2027”, adding: “That’s very different to market pricing for rates to be close to 4.5pc in 2027.”

News.title: Arsonists torch more Ebola clinics as misinformation spirals in DRC
News.content:
Two more Ebola treatment facilities have reportedly been burned down in recent days as health officials struggle to overcome violent public mistrust of medical teams.

At least a dozen facilities have now been attacked since Congo declared its Ebola outbreak amid fear, misinformation and suspicion of outside authorities.

The outbreak is the fastest growing on record and officials said the virus had now killed more than 1,500 people.

The official death toll from the outbreak centred on the north eastern Ituri province of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has risen by 500 in only a week.

Sources told the Telegraph the large jump in deaths was largely caused by a “data harmonisation exercise” between different regions, and the new deaths may not have all happened in the past week.

However, the daily confirmed toll has also continued to climb sharply with the latest government update reporting 50 people dying in the previous 24 hours.

Airfinity, a health analytics firm, said the outbreak “continues to outpace detection and the response” and there is a high chance of it spreading further inside DRC.

News.title: Race for vaccine against new Ebola strain gets $8.5m boost
News.content:
The “most promising” vaccine to tackle the Ebola strain behind an explosive outbreak in the Congo has been given an $8.5 million boost, as researchers race to develop an effective shot.

So far at least 3,360 people have been infected and 1,487 people have died in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in an epidemic triggered by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.

But unlike past outbreaks of the more common Zaire strain, there are currently no approved vaccines to tackle Bundibugyo.

On Thursday, the Coalition of Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi) revealed up to $8.5 million of funding for the only single-dose inoculation, which was described as the “most promising vaccine candidate” by the World Health Organization (WHO) in an analysis in May.

It is being developed by researchers at Hilleman Laboratories – a unique partnership between the pharmaceutical giant Merck and the British philanthropic powerhouse Wellcome, which is headquartered in Singapore.

The vaccine candidate is a Bundibugyo version of the Ervebo shot, which was created by Merck (MSD in Europe) and has already been approved for Ebola Zaire.

It uses a rVSV platform, where a modified version of VSV virus is used to train the immune system to react to target pathogens – in this instance, the Bundibugyo species replaces Zaire.

News.title: AMR chatbot could prevent drug-resistant infections in African hospitals
News.content:
A phone-based chatbot advising medics how to prescribe antibiotics has helped raise the quality of care in African hospitals and should stop bugs developing dangerous resistance, developers say.

Staff at four hospitals across Zambia and Kenya have been using two digital tools in a pilot project to try to address one of the world’s biggest health threats.

Anti-microbial resistance (AMR) is caused by germs evolving so that medicines such as antibiotics designed to kill them no longer work.

The menace is linked to nearly five million deaths each year and makes it increasingly difficult to treat infections. The annual death toll could nearly double in the next 25 years, according to some forecasts.

The rise in AMR is being significantly driven by the misuse and overuse of antimicrobials in human medicine and in agriculture.

Using antibiotics when they are not necessary, using the wrong ones, or getting the dosage wrong, all add to the chances that bugs will develop resistance.

With a shortage of new drugs in the development pipeline, one push to defeat AMR has been to get medics to stick to existing prescription, dosage and treatment advice.

The Antibiotic Stewardship Programme through Innovation, Research, and Education (ASPIRE) is trying to give them guidance using technology they already have in their pockets.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

Sports.title: Jadon Sancho training at 10th tier minnows just a stone’s throw away from Man Utd training ground after leaving
Sports.content:
JADON SANCHO has been training at 10th tier minnows Flixton FC – just a stone’s throw away from Manchester United’s training ground.

Sancho is now a free agent after his Old Trafford nightmare officially ended this summer, calling time on years of endless loan spells.



The 26-year-old winger, whom United splashed £73m on in 2021, has been using upgraded non-league facilities at Flixton’s 2,000-capacity Valley Road ground.

In a club interview, Sancho said: “You’ve got a nice layout here. It’s the first time I’ve seen a nice pitch [in this area] apart from United and City.”



Flixton are gearing up for their first competitive season since going bust in 2012, having been brought back from the dead by a new investor last year.

United legend Ryan Giggs‘ estranged brother Rhodri Giggs, who previously managed Salford City, was appointed as Assistant Manager last summer.

The cash investment in the facilities comes after American financier Christopher Garcia, CEO of US based Wilshire Quinn Capital, purchased the club in February 2025.

Originally opened by Sir Alex Ferguson back in 1995, Flixton’s Valley Road ground had been reduced to hosting Sunday League games before being slapped with a £500,000 price tag on Rightmove in January 2025.

While weighing up his next options, Sancho promised he’d be in the stands to watch Flixton play next Tuesday, just a 10 minute drive away from Carrington.

The London-born forward has drawn interest from Qatari club Al Rayyan and has been previously targeted by Roma in the Serie A.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Sancho spent the past three seasons on loan at Borussia Dortmund, Chelsea and Aston Villa, achieving the remarkable feat of playing in a European final for all three – all in different competitions.

He won the Europa League with Villa but failed to reignite the consistency that once made him one of Europe’s most sought-after young players.

The former England winger, who came through City and Watford’s youth ranks, played just 83 matches for United before his public row with former boss Erik ten Hag in 2023.

Villa have since signed ex-United star Alejandro Garnacho on a season-long loan from Chelsea to fill the void on the left wing.

Sports.title: Who is Matthias Jaissle? Newcastle set to appoint little-known Al Ahli boss as Eddie Howe’s replacement
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE are expected to name little-known Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach after Eddie Howe’s shock departure.

News of Howe‘s exit – just weeks before the start of the new Premier League season – has rocked fans on Tyneside.



The 48-year-old ends his five-year tenure as one of Newcastle‘s most successful managers after guiding the club to their first major trophy in 70 years by winning the Carabao Cup in 2025.

He also led the Magpies to Champions League qualification in 2023 and 2025.



It’s understood Howe‘s departure comes after he told Toon chiefs he wants to take a break from coaching.

Newcastle are now poised to name their replacement, with Jaissle expected to take the St James’ Park hotseat – SunSport brings you the lowdown on the young coach.

Who is potential new Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle?

Jaissle, 38, is currently in charge of Saudi Pro League side Al Ahli, who, like Newcastle, are majority-owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

The German was a talented centre-back in his playing days, but was forced to retire in 2014 at the age of just 26 after never truly recovering from a knee injury picked up five years earlier.

Former Manchester United boss Ralph Rangnick came to Jaissle’s aid after that and invited him on a trainee programme with RB Leipzig’s youth academy.



The pair knew each other as Rangnick coached a young Jaissle during his time as manager of Hoffenheim and he reached out in his new role as RB Leipzig’s head of sport.

He temporarily left the Austrian giants in 2021, becoming a head coach for the first time at Liefering.

In his first season, the German led the team to second in the Austrian second tier, the club’s joint best-ever finish.

Jaissle’s exploits earned him the top job at RB Salzburg, replacing Jesse Marsch.

During his time in charge at the Red Bull Arena, he managed the likes of Benjamin Sesko and Karim Adeyemi, who now play for Manchester United and Barcelona respectively.



He won the Austrian Bundesliga in both of his two seasons in charge and was heralded as one of the brightest young coaches in Europe.

In 2023, Jaissle joined Al Ahli, where he has won the Asian Champions League Elite twice and the Saudi Super Cup.

The Saudi club have England striker Ivan Toney and former Chelsea goalkeeper Edouard Mendy on their books.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel was a youth coach at Stuttgart when Jaissle was coming through as a player and the two Germans spoke before Toney was included in England’s World Cup squad this summer.

At the time of the squad announcement, Tuchel said: “I had fantastic feedback from his club coach, who was my player and I have a close connection with him.”



What is Jaissle’s style of play?

Newcastle fans will be happy to know Jaissle likes to play high-pressing attacking football, not too dissimilar to what we have seen from Howe’s sides in the past.

During his time at Al Ahli, the German has often played a 4-2-3-1, but Jaissle has previously explained it’s more about principles of play than the formation.

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “It is not about formations that much. It is more how you want to play, how you want to attack, how you want to defend.

“If you understand that and the players understand that, tactically you are much more flexible and the formation is not that important.”

“It can be demanding for players. These days the players are more and more involved in tactical things.



“Every coach and every club works with principles, so every player has to know a lot of things, tactically, in each phase of the game. I think that’s a big change.”

In 2024, Jaissle drew upon some of the coaches who have influenced his career, but he insisted he has his own style.

The German told GiveMeSport: “I have always tried to be authentic as a coach and find my own way.

“Of course, I have influences. Ralf Rangnick played a big part in developing my ideas because I played under him for most of my playing career.

“And in my youth, I had Thomas Tuchel, so I have followed his principles and career. Then there’s Jurgen Klopp – I often looked at the transitions he put in place with Liverpool.



“In possession, I like how Pep Guardiola finds structure and balance. And there’s a lot to take from Roberto De Zerbi’s build-up as well. It’s a constant learning process.

“I am always refining my style, but essentially, and I know it’s easy to say, we want dominance in all phases of the game.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s a never-ending process because you always need to develop your ideas as a coach without abandoning your roots.

“At Salzburg, I played a 4-4-2 with a diamond midfield. At Al-Ahli, we use a 4-2-3-1 system. You have to adjust to the squad you have as well as the circumstances.”

Sports.title: Fulham ‘buy two Real Madrid stars’ as Alvaro Arbeloa agrees bizarre  £50m double transfer
Sports.content:
FULHAM have bought Real Madrid pair Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios after sealing a very peculiar deal.

The Cottagers’ new manager Alvaro Arbeloa went back to his former club for reinforcements ahead of the 2026/27 Premier League season.



According to Marca, Arbeloa, 43, has landed Garcia, 22, and Palacios, 21, in a £50million package.

However, the same source claims the West Londoners only bought 70 per cent of the players’ rights.



The other 30 per cent will be covering a sell-on clause included in their contracts.

So Fulham will be full owners of the pair but any future sale would see Real getting a significant windfall.

Garcia played under Arbeloa at the Santiago Bernabeu after the Spanish tactician replaced Xabi Alonso at the helm in January.

The forward amassed eight goals and three assists in 39 appearances across all competitions last season.

That added to the Spain international’s total of 13 goals and five assists in 51 appearances since joining Real‘s senior team in 2023.

Palacios, on the other hand, has got Arbeloa to thank for his big break in Madrid’s first team last season.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The playmaker registered seven appearances across all competitions after making his senior debut in January.

Real are putting together a major revamp under returning manager Jose Mourinho.

And in order to realise Mourinho’s vision, sales of fringe players need to be made as the ex-Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham boss doesn’t wish to part with big names.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe’s exit shows Newcastle may never compete at top of Premier League, the owners’ 2030 title dream is impossible
Sports.content:
WHEN Eddie Howe agreed to take the reins at stricken Newcastle United nearly five years ago, he did not do so with the aim of treading water.

He had a vision, backed by the new Saudi money after the miserable years under Mike Ashley, and he was raring to go having taken a year out of the game.



We sat together in a hotel from where you could see across to St. James’ Park in the Tyneside night and Howe’s eyes lit up at the sight of the cathedral on the hill.

This was where he was meant to be, this was the big job he had always wanted.



For over an hour we chewed the fat and I left in no doubt that this man would spend every waking minute to try and make Newcastle great.

Not for a moment could that total commitment ever be questioned.



He also delivered us a first domestic trophy for 70 years and no Newcastle fan will ever forget the date, March 16, 2025, when we put Liverpool to the sword at Wembley.

But this is a man who knew he was spent.

Sports.title: Quarter of sports fans believe they could score a goal in a Premier League match, new poll finds
Sports.content:
A QUARTER of sports fans reckon they could score a goal in a Premier League match, while one in 10 claim they could last a round in the ring with a pro boxer.

The study of 2,000 adults who enjoy watching sport found many think they could hold their own against some of the best athletes in the world.



One in seven (14 per cent) think they could be on a par with a professional golfer over one hole, while 22 per cent are confident they could beat them in crazy golf, and 18 per cent reckon they would be able to return a serve from a top tennis player.

While 14 per cent even think they could manage a lap of a Formula 1 track against the top drivers without coming last.



It also emerged 14 per cent think they could finish a stage of the Tour de France without embarrassing themselves against the competition.

The study was commissioned by Staysure, ahead of the Legends golf tour sponsored by the brand, which gets underway next week at Trump International Golf Links, and gives amateurs the unique opportunity to play alongside the pros in its Pro-Am event.



Corin Rogerson, director of sponsorship for the insurer, said: “Pro sport isn’t as easy as people seemingly think it could be, but these findings show just how confident many fans are when watching from the sofa or the stands.

“It can seem easy when spectating, but in reality, elite athletes dedicate years to perfecting their craft, building the physical fitness, mental resilience and technical skill needed to compete at the very top.

“It is easy to underestimate just how difficult these sports are until you are faced with the speed, pressure and precision involved.

“That is what makes watching the professionals do what they do so impressive.”



But the research found reality clearly does not hold people back, as 57 per cent reckon there are some adults who think they could compete with a professional athlete.

While 66 per cent of those put this down to some simply over-estimating their own abilities, 59 per cent believe it’s due to the sports looking easier than they are.

More than half (56 per cent) also think it’s due to people undervaluing just how skilled the sportspeople really are.

With 80 per cent believing that watching professional sport can make people become ‘armchair experts’ who underestimate how difficult it is to play at that level.

When it comes to golf in particular, 38 per cent think an amateur would have a chance against a professional, believing it can all come down to one lucky shot (52 per cent), and because pros make mistakes too (51 per cent).



The research, carried out, via OnePoll, found 82 per cent find stories of amateurs and underdogs triumphing in sport inspiring, and 42 per cent would be keen to watch a novice take on a pro golfer in a head-to-head challenge.

Corin Rogerson for Staysure added: “As a nation, many of us are clearly willing to back ourselves when it comes to taking on the professionals, whether that is stepping onto a golf course, returning a serve, or lasting in the ring.

“It was a fun reminder of the confidence many sports fans have.”

Sports.title: Uefa statement in full as Gianni Infantino blasted for ‘governance by intimidation’ over shameless World Cup plan
Sports.content:
UEFA have “unanimously and unequivocally” slammed Fifa’s controversial World Cup plans and accused them of intimidation tactics.

The Fifa president’s controversial proposal involves transferring control of top tournaments like the World Cup to a new subsidiary, followed by the sale of a substantial portion of the business.



European football’s governing body has led the backlash against the plot and hosted a virtual meeting with its 55 member associations today.

And Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin has blasted Gianni Infantino for his plans amid the Uefa-Fifa civil war.



Uefa has since published a statement that reads: “UEFA and its national associations will not participate in Fifa competitions.

“UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one.

“We unanimously and unequivocally reject Fifa’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.

“The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies.

“It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent.

“No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

“It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game.

“This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of Fifa’s duty as the custodian of world football.

“National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences.

“This is not a ‘democratic decision’, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

“But our opposition goes far beyond process.



“The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in Fifa competitions, football changes forever.

“Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure.

“From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.



“This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return.

“Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns.

“Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

“Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy.

“No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.



“As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive.

“Unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that Fifa will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

“Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

“There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise.

“This is one of those moments. Some things are simply too important to sell.

“And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

Sports.title: Premier League stars face at least 10-MATCH bans for ‘aggravated breaches’ as FA impose new punishment
Sports.content:
CRACKDOWN Premier League stars face at least 10-MATCH bans for ‘aggravated breaches’ as FA impose new punishment

Credit: Not known, clear with picture desk

FOOTBALLERS will now be hit with a whopping 10-MATCH ban as standard if they commit an aggravated breach of FA rules.

The new sanction guidelines have been introduced ahead of the 2026/27 season as part of a firmer stance against discriminatory conduct.



An aggravated breach is defined in FA Rule E3.2 as “any misconduct that includes an express or implied reference to any one or more of the following characteristics: ethnic origin, colour, race, nationality, religion or belief, sex, gender, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, or disability“.

Recent sanction guidelines have recommended bans of between six and 12 matches to the independent regulatory commissions who dish out the punishments.



But now a standard suspension will be at least 10 matches, the FA has confirmed.

They wrote on their website: “We are committed to delivering a game free from discrimination.

“While significant progress has been made in recent years, discriminatory conduct continues to be a challenge across the game.

“Enhanced measures are necessary to tackle this abhorrent conduct, and our updated sanction guidelines will now require Regulatory Commissions to impose a standard suspension of at least 10 matches in these circumstances.”

Aggravating factors would allow commissions to impose a ban higher than 10 matches, with mitigating factors permitting them to lower it to a minimum of six matches.

Players could be slapped with bans in excess of 12 matches – or a time-based suspension – if they are charged despite already having an aggravated breach on their record.



Fulham‘s Chris Donnell was banned for six matches last year for using abusive and/or insulting words with a reference to disability.

That punishment could be heightened under the new guidelines, unless mitigating factors were presented to the commission.

Tranmere’s Sam Finlay was slapped with a 13-game ban last year for using a homophobic slur.

And Preston’s Milutin Osmajic was banned for nine matches in November after racially abusing Hannibal Mejbri.

Sports.title: Tottenham legend, 34, appointed kit man at club in Mexico after being forced to retire from football
Sports.content:
RAYADOS de Monterrey’s kit man happens to be none other than Puskas-winning Erik Lamela.

The former Tottenham star, 34, was forced into an early retirement with a hip injury that called for TWO surgeries.



But 12 months after hanging up his boots at AEK Athens, he’s back out earning his coaching badges in the guise of Monterrey’s kit man.

While he effectively operates as an assistant coach – mirroring his time at Sevilla – he can’t hold the official title yet because he lacks the required license under Article 17.1 of Liga MX statutes.



Goalkeeping coach Fabian Donelli faces the same restriction.

But with the UEFA Pro coaching course taking a year to complete, it’s possible that they’ll be named in Matias Almeyda’s coaching staff soon.



Lamela began his path to stardom at South American giants River Plate and then Roma, before joining Spurs in a deal worth £25.7million in 2013.

He arrived at White Hart Lane in the same window that Spurs sold Gareth Bale to Real Madrid for a world-record fee.

And while fellow wide man Lamela was not as productive as Bale, he still endeared himself to Tottenham fans with his tireless running and catalogue of memorable moments.

One of the fan favourites came with a 20-yard rabona in the Europa League in 2014 before he won the Puskas Award for scoring another rabona in the North London Derby seven years later.

After over 250 Tottenham games and late-career spells at Sevilla and AEK Athens, Lamela returned to Sevilla as a coach after hanging up his boots.

His starpower caught the attention of Alejandro Sabella and then of Gerardo Tata Martino who called him up to the national team.

He made appearances in the qualifiers for the 2014 World Cup in Brazil and in the 2015 and 2016 Copa Americas, where he won the double championship.

Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain have a long history of getting deals done in the transfer market. And this working relationship could be strengthened if the Reds convince Bradley Barcola to head to Anfield.

The club are set to open talks with PSG over a potential transfer for the winger. Initial talks with Barcola's representatives have prompted Liverpool to formalise their interest with an official approach.

‌



Andoni Iraola has been on the lookout for a wide player since Mohamed Salah's exit. Barcola has been on Liverpool's radar for some time, and the club will hope to make him their third summer signing.

‌



Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet have signed deals at Anfield, but there's certain to be more movement – both incoming and outgoing – before the new season starts. If Barcola does decide to join Liverpool, it wouldn't represent the first time that a transfer between the two clubs has taken place.

Here, Mirror Football examines some of the previous transfers between the two sides.

‌



Highly-rated teen

David Ngog signed his first professional contract with PSG in 2006 as a highly-rated teenager. Two years later, he arrived at Anfield as a fresh-faced 19-year-old under Rafael Benitez.

The striker would play under three different managers at Liverpool, including Roy Hodgson and Sir Kenny Dalglish. Ngog scored 19 goals and assisted six times across 94 appearances before leaving for Bolton Wanderers in 2011.

View 4 Images David Ngog spent three seasons with the Reds (Image: John Powell/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Despite such a promising start to his career, Ngog really failed to reach the heights his early days promised. He later played for Swansea City, Reims, Panionios, Ross County and Budapest Honved before retiring in Lithuania at the age of 31.

223-goal striker

Nicolas Anelka had already played in the Premier League before joining Liverpool on loan in 2001. The striker left PSG for Arsenal at 17 and made 42 goal contributions from 1997 to 1999.

A move to Real Madrid came next before Anelka returned to France a year later. PSG then loaned the striker to Liverpool in the 2001 January transfer window.

‌



View 4 Images Nicolas Anelka has plenty of experience in the Premier League (Image: Clive Brunskill/ Getty Images)

The France international made 22 appearances for the Reds and scored five goals, helping the team to a second-placed finish in the Premier League. Gerard Houllier opted against giving Anelka a permanent deal at Liverpool and he ended up at Manchester City.

He came back to haunt the Reds after scoring a brace in a 2-1 win over them in May 2003. Throughout his career, Anelka scored 223 goals for club and country, winning two Champions League titles and the European Championship with France.

‌



PSG title winner

View 4 Images Mamadou Sakho was a title winner before he arrived at Anfield (Image: VI Images via Getty Images)

Mamadou Sakho had already made 201 appearances for PSG before his £18million move to Liverpool in 2013. The defender had won the Ligue 1 title just weeks before he joined the Reds, bringing a wealth of experience to Brendan Rodgers' side.

Sakho would go on to make 80 appearances for Liverpool, scoring three goals and continuing his time at Anfield after Rodgers was sacked in 2016. Jurgen Klopp kept the centre-half around for a half a season before Crystal Palace signed him on loan.

After an impressive temporary spell, Sakho would sign a permanent move to Palace in 2017 for a fee of £26m. He would go on to have stints at Montpellier and Torpedo Kutaisi before retiring in January this year at 35.

Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott opens up on Aston Villa loan nightmare and second chance at Liverpool

Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott has spoken out about his future under Andoni Iraola after spending a season on the sidelines at Aston Villa under Unai Emery

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott has already featured in two friendlies for Andoni Iraola this summer (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

Elliott was left out of squads throughout the season as he struggled to play under Unai Emery.

‌



It was not the season Elliott wanted, having only started twice in the Premier League during Arne Slot's title-winning season at Anfield. It cost him any chance of making it into Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad and leaves him desperate to play football.

‌



Elliott holds no ill will toward Villa but is now firmly focused on establishing himself at Liverpool. He believes that with a new coaching staff to impress, he has the perfect opportunity to rekindle his career.

“Unfortunately, it didn't work out, but the way I see it is that's last season now, I'm here. It's kind of a second chance, if you want to call it," Elliott explained.

Rio Ngumoha provides Bradley Barcola transfer hint as Liverpool beat Wrexham in New York READ MORE :

“Especially with the gaffer and new coaching staff coming in. It's another chance to impress and hopefully get in their (good) books.

‌



"But whatever happened last season, I wish Villa nothing but the very best, had a lot of love for them, and they treated me very, very well. Unfortunately, the situation happened, but It's another learning curve.

“It's a situation that I can take on in my career, and just keep looking forward. I'm here now, and I'm trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad."

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott barely featured for Aston Villa last season but did win the Europa League (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

While Elliott is looking to move on from last season, he conceded it was a difficult situation to bear. The 23-year-old was pleased to be part of an historic Europa League win with Villa but endured a draining situation on the sidelines.

“Mentally, it was a very tough one," he added. "As I said, it was a learning curve. It was an opportunity for me to experience something new, as much as I didn't want to do it, and I don't wish it upon any other player, because it's not nice at all, but I have no hard feelings.

“I wish them all the very best. Well, I did greatly have a lot of love for them. They treated me as one of their own, as it were, and for that. I respect them highly.

“But it was tough, mentally and physically, but I'm on the other side of it now. I was able to get through it, and achieve something at the end of the season as well (with Villa winning the Europa League).

“That was another historical moment for the club, and to be part of that was another great situation. But my focus is on this season, at Liverpool, and I just need to see what happens.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino MUST GO - FIFA chief has no way back after brutal response to World Cup plot
Sports.content:
Over the course of the World Cup, Gianni Infantino attended 45 matches and was captured by television cameras at every one of them.

Rarely was there a moment when he was not wearing a smug look. Record-breaking commercial income was on its way, stadiums were full and he had a $20billion trick up his sleeve - he was going to flog off the rights to the greatest sporting show on earth to private investors, dressing it up as a way of making extra cash for FIFA’s 211 member nations.

Well, 55 of those member nations have told him what he can do with his scheme. Ditch it. Or face not having a World Cup at all. Or a Women’s World Cup. Or a Club World Cup. Or any FIFA-organised World Cup.

Because without the European nations, there is no World Cup, of any kind. You can bet Gianni is not looking so smug today.

‌



UEFA could not have been more unequivocal. A truly unprecedented statement read: “No UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.”

UEFA statement in FULL as they boycott World Cup until FIFA abandon controversial proposal READ MORE :

England and UEFA nations WILL BOYCOTT World Cup in protest over Gianni Infantino sale plan READ MORE :

But the UEFA statement goes way, way beyond announcing a boycott of FIFA competitions, in itself a genuinely seismic decision in the history of football governance.

It lacerates Infantino’s integrity and morality. It lays his fitness for purpose to waste.

When talking of it being ‘irresponsible and indefensible’ that the FIFA proposal was ‘conceived in secret’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

‌



When talking of a ‘profound failure of leadership’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

When talking of ‘an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

When talking of ‘governance by intimidation’, they are referring directly to Infantino.

This is UEFA, the association whose teams dominate the World Cup. The powerhouse association of world football. The association who provided six of the eight quarter-finalists at World Cup 2026.

‌



And in their landmark emergency meeting, they not only made sure Infantino’s outlandish scheme is dead in the water, they clinically and viciously dismantled the character of the man in charge of world football, the man who Donald Trump believes would make a good Secretary General of NATO.

Well, perhaps Trump can get his mate the NATO gig because his position as FIFA president is now untenable. Infantino’s thick skin is the stuff of legend but it is impossible to see how he can stay in his post after this evisceration.

The statement from UEFA is pretty grand in its own morality.

‌



It concludes: “Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”

It needs to be said that UEFA have not been slow to commercialise European football but that is another story.

They have been gunning for Infantino for some time, certainly since he launched the expanded Club World Cup.

And with this disgraceful, ill-judged, avaricious, mood-ignorant plot of his, Infantino has left himself open to be taken down.

‌



UEFA have taken their chance with cold brutality. Infantino has to go.

Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino offered FIFA's 211 members £30m a piece to back his controversial plans to create a company featuring private investors to run the World Cup and other FIFA events.

He attempted to effectively blackmail those nations, telling them that they would not get that £30m if they didn't back his proposal and the majority endorsed his FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) venture. Associations were asked to make a decision by September 19.

The lead investor to Infantino's scheme had been proposed to be Thrive Eternal, a company founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of United States President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. The same Donald Trump to whom Infantino has cosied up to no end in recent years.

Now, the FIFA president is experiencing the kind of backlash he either didn't foresee or did not expect, with UEFA leading the charge.

‌



European nations have announced that they will BOYCOTT all FIFA competitions until the global body drops its plans, following a crisis meeting on Thursday afternoon - called some 48 hours after Infantino's plans were initially leaked.

England and UEFA nations WILL BOYCOTT World Cup in protest over Gianni Infantino sale plan READ MORE :

PSG chief makes decision over UEFA plea to replace FIFA villain Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

UEFA's anger was made crystal clear, declaring: "UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale."

They labelled Infantino's proposal "irresponsible and indefensible". They added it was "not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football."

‌



They pointedly commented: "This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game."

They continued: “This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return."

They insisted: “Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination."

And UEFA ended by declaring war on Infantino and his plans, stating: “Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.”
