Sports.title: Diamond Necklace sparkles in Nassau Stakes
Sports.content:
Diamond Necklace lived up to her billing when extending her unbeaten record with a dominant display in the Qatar Nassau Stakes at Goodwood.

Having rounded off a perfect juvenile campaign with victory in the Prix Marcel Boussac on Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp, Aidan O'Brien's filly has returned to France to secure back-to-back Classic wins this year, in the French 1000 Guineas and French Oaks.

She was the 4-6 favourite to make it six from six as she faced her elders for the first time and while Friendly Soul did her best to shake her off, Ryan Moore always looked ultra-confident in the saddle aboard Diamond Necklace and she pulled two and three-quarter lengths clear with the minimum of fuss.

An impressed Moore said: "That's the best she's felt, she's improving with her racing. Aidan said she was up in her weight a bit today so she's obviously thriving.

"She's classy, it was very easy really. She travelled smoothly and quickened up well, she's a little bit idle in front still, but she's a proper racing machine.

"She gives you a classy feel, every time I've ridden her she's travelled with loads of pace, loads of enthusiasm and she has a turn of foot; that's what her father (St Mark's Basilica) had, a real good turn of foot and that's what's evident with her."

O'Brien was delighted to see Diamond Necklace enhance her unbeaten record and said: "She's lovely and she's progressing and she was heavier today, but Rachel (Richardson, work rider) was confident that was just strength she was building rather than just being heavy and it was the way she went through the line.

"There's a lot of people around her who help her and she's a lovely filly. This was a mile and a quarter against older fillies and we didn't know what was going to happen. We put in a lot of pace as we didn't want a Mickey Mouse race and she has options now.

"You can see her quality the way she travels through a race and Ryan was hoping they would lead him longer and he just had to go on as her stride was getting broken. She is a great cruiser and she has a lot of quality and is progressing great so I'm over the moon."

Diamond Necklace was shortened to 8-1 from 14s for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe by Paddy Power, but O'Brien is yet to commit on stretching her stamina any further than the 10 furlongs, with the star filly holding a multitude of options for later in the season.

He added: "Constitution River is the boss and everyone has to fall into line behind him. At the moment he is going to York and we're looking forward to that.

"She could stay at a mile and a quarter and go to the race at Leopardstown (Irish Champion Stakes), or France for an Arc trial, she has all those races open to her and she does handle soft ground as well as she handles fast ground.

"The Arc is possibility and she could be a Breeders' Cup filly, it will depend how far we ask her to go. Her next run will tell us where she is going to go and she has a long stride on her and loves nice ground and a fast track, she has a lot of options."

Friendly Soul has endured her fair share of drama since returning from injury this year, being the horse who put a foot in a hole at Haydock before a luckless run in the Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot.

"She's run a fine race against a top class three-year-old who is unbeaten," said Thady Gosden, who trains the five-year-old alongside father John.

"It was a very good effort and we will now in consultation with George and Julia (Strawbridge, owners) look at the programme ahead in which there are some good opportunities for older fillies."

Enceladus impresses in Gordon - but Leger run not set in stone

Joseph O'Brien is keen to keep his options open with Enceladus following his authoritative victory in the Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes at Goodwood.

The Sea The Stars colt has looked much improved since being stepped up in trip this season, with a comeback win at Cork followed by Royal Ascot success in the King George V Stakes.

The William Haggas-trained pair of Desert Hero (2023) and Merchant (2025) won the same Ascot handicap in recent years before landing this Group Three prize and after being sent off a well-backed 6-4 favourite to follow suit, Enceladus finished strongly under Dylan Browne McMonagle, keeping Geryon at bay by a length and a quarter.

Classic sponsors Betfred make Enceladus a 10-1 shot from 25-1 for the Leger, a race which saw O'Brien break his British Classic duck as a trainer with Galileo Chrome six years ago - but the trainer warned he is not certain to head for Doncaster in September.

O'Brien was at Galway rather than Goodwood, from where he told Press Association: "I'm delighted, it was a nice ride from Dylan. It was a really nice performance and he's a progressive, improving colt.

"It was a big step up in class and it's a hard thing to do, but he's going the right way and I'm delighted to have a horse of his potential for Maria and the Niarchos team."

On a Leger bid, he added: "It is one of the more obvious options, but I don't know if we'll rush him past a mile and a half either. Let's see how he pulls up and let the dust settle and we'll lock in his next target after that."

Image: Dylan Browne McMonagle riding Enceladus to win the Maison Perrier Gordon Stakes during day three of the Qatar Goodwood Festival

McMonagle said: "He's a lovely, big, straightforward horse. He's done nothing but improve and each run he's getting better.

"I think he's going to be a very nice horse going forward and I do think he's up to that level (Group Twos and Group Ones) with a bit of time.

"As you can see he's still a big baby - when he's getting there he's just doing enough, but he was a good winner.

"He handles that ground well and I think he's got a bit of class - he's a horse to look forward to and one to keep an eye on."

Colin Keane said of the runner-up: "I thought for a few strides that we were going to get to Dylan's horse (Enceladus) but he picked up and went away again.

"I'd say the winner is smart but we're smart as well, he's just a bit of a work in progress. He probably didn't (see it out as well as the winner), but I do think in time he will.

"He's a little hard on himself, he wears earplugs to help him relax so he's a work in progress but a horse with a big future hopefully."

Sports.title: Doyle: Raider can blitz King George rivals
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing’s ambassador Hollie Doyle previews the best of the action on Day Four of the Goodwood Festival with the Group Two King George Qatar Stakes headlining the action.

Fast five the key to King George favourite

Five furlongs down the hill is tailor-made for Karl Burke's lightning-fast Night Raider who can bounce back from his defeat at Royal Ascot in Friday's feature at The Goodwood Festival, the King George Qatar Stakes (3.35).

Ascot was just too stiff a test for him, but the Temple Stakes winner can show his class from a decent attacking draw in stall 13, despite having to concede a three-pound penalty for that Group Two blitz at Haydock.

Aspect Island, who was a close second in Listed company at York recently, looks a Group race winner in the making and can give another good account of himself for James Owen and Billy Loughnane. Third in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint last autumn, he is another who should enjoy this pure speed test.

New York can become a headline act

Talk Of New York can produce a headline performance for William Buick in the Group Three HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes (2.25) on Friday.

Godolphin's son of Wootton Bassett caught my eye in the Heron Stakes at Sandown before running a big figure in the St James's Palace Stakes at the Royal Meeting, despite refusing to settle. Indeed, he was less than two lengths behind Wednesday's brilliant Sussex Stakes winner Bow Echo.

Saber Strike has 9lbs to find with Charlie Appleby's colt on these terms but has always been well-regarded by William Haggas and the team. His third in the Group Three Criterion at York reads well and the combination of first-time blinkers and this idiosyncratic track should keep him interested.

Golden chance for Spencer in feature Handicap

The Coral Golden Mile (3.00) on Friday promises to be quite a spectacle with 20 runners thundering down the hill, including David Menuisier's Tribal Chief.

Everything points to a big run from the five-year-old with Jamie Spencer doing the steering. Jamie is a master on hold-up horses like him. He caught my eye in defeat in big handicaps at Ascot and Sandown and looks ready to enjoy his day in the sun at a track at which he has already won.

I am also hoping my husband Tom (Marquand's) mount Scoville can build on an encouraging run in the Royal Hunt Cup - his first following a wind operation. He was up there to be shot at at Ascot but may have to be ridden differently from his wide draw this time.

Believe in King stayer in Friday marathon

I am a big fan of Alan King's stayer Believitanducan who can extend his winning sequence to four this year in the marathon Coral Goodwood Handicap (1.50) on Friday.

The improving five-year-old can make light work of a five-pound rise for his win in the Northumberland Vase at Newcastle last month. He stays all day so won't mind the extra half mile and is another plum ride for William Buick.

Valiancy blotted his copybook in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot behind Alan King's Daiquiri Bay but looked hugely progressive before that and shouldn't be written off too soon. He is a worthy favourite but must give Believitanducan all of 10lbs.

At a bigger price, keep an eye on Irish raider Alphonse Le Grande who wasn't far behind my selection at Gosforth Park and races off the same mark he won off in that controversial Cesarewitch two years ago. I won the Vase on him at Newcastle in 2024 and know what a tough, thorough stayer he is on his day.

Step up in trip ideal for Hannon sprinter

Jaijai looks well drawn and well weighted in the six-furlong Hawes and Curtis Nursery Handicap (4.45) on Friday. Richard Hannon's course winner probably found five-furlongs at Windsor too easy a test last time but can prove a tougher proposition back up in trip.

Innichen is a typically tough Jack Channon handicapper who is another to keep an eye on. He is up eight-pounds in a hotter race than the one he won at Nottingham, but Tom (Marquand) knows him well and it wouldn't surprise me to see him continue that upward curve despite a questionable draw.

I'll be back on Saturday with my thoughts on the final day of a memorable Qatar Goodwood Festival, including the Stewards' Cup.

Sports.title: UEFA to boycott FIFA tournaments if World Cup sell-off goes ahead
Sports.content:
UEFA will boycott FIFA tournaments if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with his proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup.

The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of all UEFA's 55 member associations on Thursday afternoon.

In a statement released on Thursday afternoon, UEFA said: "We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors."

The boycott should effectively kill off Infantino's proposal as investors would be unlikely to put money into tournaments without European teams.

The first major tournament UEFA can boycott is the 2027 Women's World Cup, which starts on June 24 next year.

Upcoming FIFA Tournaments UEFA threatening to boycott: FIFA Under 20 Women’s World Cup (Poland) - Sep 2026

FIFA Under 17 Women’s World Cup (Morocco) - Oct 2026

FIFA Under 17 World Cup (Qatar) - Nov/Dec 2026

FIFA Women’s Champions Cup (Miami) - Jan 2027

FIFA Women’s World Cup (Brazil) - Jun/Jul 2028

A major row first broke out on Tuesday between football's governing bodies over FIFA's plans to seek private investment in the World Cup, with UEFA reacting angrily and European nations ready to discuss a boycott.

FIFA announced that it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments.

Under the proposal, FIFA would raise up to $4.2bn (£3.1bn) from external investors through the sale of minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it says would be valued at around $20bn (£15bn).

The governing body says its plans - which need approval from member associations - could deliver more than $10bn in "football development funding" over the next four years.

But UEFA, European football's governing body, released a furious statement that said the proposals "crossed a line".

There was further opposition to the proposal from Prime Minister Andy Burnham who said "football belongs to fans" on X while the FA, who were left completely unaware, expressed a "deep concern" over plans.

In a statement released on Thursday, the Scottish FA said they "agree unequivocally with concerns raised by all members over the manner in which these proposals have been issued, and deadline set, without a full consultation process or consideration to good governance".

The Premier League - who are a founding member of the European Leagues - backed the stance, saying it "fully supports this statement".

'The World Cup is not for sale' - UEFA's statement in full

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA's duty as the custodian of world football.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Prime Minister Andy Burnham disagrees with FIFA's attempts to bring in private investment for the World Cup.

"National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a "democratic decision", but governance by intimidation - an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

"But our opposition goes far beyond process.

"The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

"This model has no place in world football. Football's future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

"Europe's position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol looks back at the World Cup and debates whether or not it will be regarded as a success.

"As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

"Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

"There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

"Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale."

What happens to Infantino if plans collapse?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Kaveh Solhekol breaks down whether Gianni Infantino will succeed with his plan to 'sell-off' the World Cup.

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"It's shocking how nothing is shocking any more. I should be surprised but I'm not surprised at all. I've just come back from the World Cup. According to FIFA, it was the most successful World Cup ever. They made more money than they know what to do with. Fans were paying outrageous prices for tickets.

"Gianni Infantino and those close to him have looked at this and said, 'this is the future'. One way to make sure you have more tournaments like the one you've just had is to set up a subsidiary of FIFA that will look after FIFA's tournaments and to invite private investors to invest in that company.

"In the short term, there's going to be a big pot of money potentially available for the 211 member associations of FIFA.

"The big question is, are they going to accept what Infantino is proposing? What happens to Infantino if these plans collapse? Are we seeing a tipping point on the horizon where a lot of people in football are saying they don't like the way Infantino has been running football?

"I think there is such a groundswell of opposition to these plans that if I had to put money on it, I think they won't succeed. It reminds me of what happened to the European Super League where plans came out, there was outrage and pretty quickly the plans didn't come to fruition.

"Infantino knows everyone has got a price. FIFA have written to all 211 member associations and have said you have until September 19 to accept this plan. If you do, there is going to be a pot of £7.5bn for us to share. If you don't, that pot will drop from £7.5bn to £2bn.

"How many of these member associations are going to turn down that money?"

Sports.title: Eubank Jr's negotiations for Nigeria ring return 'coming along nicely'
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr's negotiations to fight in Nigeria this December are "coming along nicely," according to Balmoral Promotions founder Ezekiel Adamu.

Eubank Jr visited the African country in June as he assesses his next steps after defeat to rival Conor Benn at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in November.

Adamu has made his desire to bring British heavyweights Anthony Joshua and Moses Itauma to Nigeria clear, but the most realistic and attainable short-term target is Eubank.

Adamu hosted the British middleweight in Nigeria last month and the son of Chris Eubank Sr was mobbed during his walk through the streets of Mushin.

Even though he will not feature in Lagos on Friday when home favourite Taiwo Agbaje faces South Africa's Ayabonga Sonjika and WBO Africa cruiserweight champion Godday Appah takes on Lekan Muibi, Adamu has his sights set on the 36-year-old.

"Chris is as big as it comes. We've had big superstars, but for Chris to come here, it was actually emotional for me to get this guy," Amadu told the Press Association.

"We're looking at him coming here for a fight in December. We're still in negotiations, but that's coming along nicely.

"We had to bring him over here to see what we're doing, to meet the right people, to get the government support and get to meet the sponsors that are going to pay for the event, but exciting times ahead."

Image: Chris Eubank Jr posted 'watch this space' on his social media during his trip to Lagos

Eubank previously insisted he was a "free agent", however promoter Ben Shalom has claimed the Brit was in a long-term contract with Boxxer. Sky Sports News has contacted Boxxer for comment.

Lawrence Okolie fought on the Balmoral Promotions show in December and Amadu had discussions with Joshua's Matchroom Boxing promoter Eddie Hearn before the former two-time heavyweight champion was involved in a car crash in Nigeria at the end of 2025.

Other big names are on a hefty shortlist being drawn up by Amadu for the coming years.

He said: "We're speaking with Deontay Wilder because Deontay found out his roots are from Nigeria, so he is also keen to fight here.

"We are speaking with Michael Ofo to see if in the future we can have Fabio Wardley and then there is (Daniel) Dubois.

Image: Chris Eubank Jr hasn't been in the ring since his defeat to Conor Benn

"The options are endless for us here in Africa and at some point we'll see them.

"We've had Lawrence Okolie fight here, Tony Yoka fight here and hopefully we should have Chris Eubank Jr fight here at some point this year, so exciting times for African boxing."

Sports.title: Carra: Liverpool don't need Barcola - they need to replace Salah!
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher believes Liverpool do not need to buy Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain - urging his former club to focus on securing a replacement for Mohamed Salah on the right wing.

Sky Sports News has reported that Liverpool are preparing an opening offer for the France international forward - who is also wanted by Arsenal and, according to some sources, is valued at £128.5m by the European champions.

However with Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and new signing Victor Munoz as Liverpool's left wing options, Carragher believes Liverpool are stockpiling in one position - and argues there is no one to replace the departed Salah on the opposite flank.

"He's a great player, there's no doubt about that - I'd love to get Barcola at Liverpool," Carragher told Sky Sports News. "But he's a left winger for me.

"Liverpool's big thing that stands out like a sore thumb right now is replacing Mo Salah, a right winger. And I don't think Liverpool have got anybody really in the squad who looks fully comfortable playing right wing.

Image: Bradley Barcola's minutes by position for PSG in the Champions League

"They probably have at least four players in the squad before Barcola joins, if he joins, who could play on the left-hand side comfortably.

"Now, I'm not saying any of those players are better than Barcola. But in terms of the balance of the squad, it's not the position Liverpool need right now. They need a right winger.

"But if you're saying to me, do I want Barcola to come and Liverpool are going to sign a right winger as well? I'll be absolutely delighted because players would have to move on. Of course they would.

"But right now, I felt this summer would be about replacing Mo Salah. Barcola doesn't replace Mo Salah."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Karembeu assess potential destinations for Bradley Barcola after rumours linking the PSG star with a switch to Arsenal and Liverpool

Could Barcola block the path of Ngumoha?

It was also put to Carragher that signing Barcola, who turns 24 in September, could block the path of exciting young winger Ngumoha.

The teenage winger turns 18 in August and had a breakout season last term, scoring twice in 19 Premier League appearances.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp recounts a time when he saw Rio Ngumoha train at his house and was staggered by how fast his feet were, praising the 17 year-old's work ethic as well as his natural talent

Asked if Ngumoha's development could be stalled by Liverpool signing Barcola, Carragher replied: "That is a thought.

"Rio's a young lad, he's really good. I think he's going to kick on from where he did last season. But that is a point: you're buying a really young player for a lot of money in Barcola, who's better than Rio Ngumoha right now.

"But you think eventually in the next year or two, Rio would want to be playing week in, week out for Liverpool. And that's up to him to prove it.

"So when you pay that type of money for a young player in his position, it does leave you scratching your head a little bit.

"There's talk that Rio Ngumoha could play on the right and get some minutes there. As a young player, that's fine, playing on both sides. But I think his position is the left-right now.

"And the reason I'm a little bit confused with Barcola is because last season, when Liverpool sold Luis Diaz, the noise was coming from the club was: we're not buying a left winger because we've got Gakpo - and we also don't want to block the path of Rio Ngumoha.

"And you think, well, OK. I understand that to a certain extent.

"But Rio is now 12 months on. He's proven that he looks a tasty player. And you think Liverpool might have a player there for the future. Yet 12 months on, Liverpool are going to break the bank for someone in that position. When 12 months earlier they said they didn't want to block Rio's path.

"So there are a few things with Liverpool transfer-wise at the moment where I'm still scratching my head a little bit.

"But if they go out and get a player for the right wing, bring Barcola in and then sell a couple of the wide players that they have on the books right now, I think that'd be fantastic."

Sports.title: Britain's Allen becomes first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing
Sports.content:
Decorated British amateur Kayla Allen will make her professional debut in London in September after becoming the first female fighter to sign with Zuffa Boxing.

The 21-year-old Londoner will campaign as a lightweight and make her first professional appearance on September 26, live on Sky Sports, at the Copper Box Arena on the undercard of ZUFFA BOXING 11, headlined by heavyweight star Johnny Fisher.

Allen's deal with Zuffa Boxing marks the latest step in a remarkable rise to a boxing career that began when she first put on a pair of gloves less than five years ago.

"I'm delighted to have signed with Zuffa Boxing as their first female athlete," Allen said.

"I feel honoured to be in this position. With the backing of Zuffa and Sky Sports, I can become a big star on both sides of the Atlantic.

"I appreciate my team for believing in me and securing this landmark deal. I'll be bringing the heat in the ring, and my fans will bring the noise on September 26."

Allen's ascent to becoming one of Britain's most accomplished young amateurs started when she set up a heavy bag in her garden and began learning the craft by watching videos of Floyd Mayweather Jr. and Mike Tyson.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Heavyweight contender Johnny Fisher has signed for Zuffa and will fight live on Sky Sports at Copper Box Arena on September 26

After a short stint on the white-collar circuit, Allen joined GB Boxing and reached the Senior Elite finals in her first year as an amateur.

She captured gold at many of Europe's most prestigious tournaments, including the 2024 Haringey Box Cup and the 2025 Senior Elite Championships.

Allen concluded her amateur career with triumphs at the 2025 European U23 Championships and 2026 Boxam Tournament in La Nucia, Spain. She will begin her professional career under the guidance of long-time trainer Alex Leo.

Sports.title: Uefa agrees to boycott Fifa competitions if World Cup sell-off plans proceed
Sports.content:
European countries have agreed to boycott all Fifa competitions if Gianni Infantino pushes forward with his proposals to sell chunks of the World Cup to US-based private investment.

In an extraordinary development all 55 Uefa members resolved not to participate in future World Cups or other Fifa-run events, saying in a statement that they “unanimously and unequivocally reject” the proposals. An emergency meeting that lasted just short of two hours ended with a united front despite earlier fears that smaller countries, attracted by the money on offer through Infantino’s scheme, would be swayed in favour.

European FAs are expected to write to Fifa this week with a formal notification of their threat to boycott future tournaments unless the planned World Cup sell-off is withdrawn.

It means Infantino faces an uphill battle to push his plan forward. Countries had been given until 19 September to sign up but there will now be significant pressure to drastically revise his scheme or withdraw it completely. While the majority of European FAs had submitted letters of support in favour of his re-election next March, such a decisive line in the sand from Uefa weakens his position dramatically.

Uefa’s statement confirmed the decision. “As a result of today’s discussion, no Uefa national teams will participate in any Fifa competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that Fifa will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership,” it read.

Thursday’s meeting was introduced by the Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, with executive committee members and Uefa’s Fifa council representatives also addressing delegates. Those early speeches are understood to have set the tone, with around 20 further FA heads taking the floor and multiple sources describing an atmosphere of “unity”. Among those to offer their view was Debbie Hewitt, the president of the FA, who one attendee said gave a “very tough” exposition in favour of a boycott.

That was backed up in a statement by an FA spokesperson that read: “We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view. We oppose Fifa’s plans – the Fifa World Cup belongs to football and always will.”

Along the lines spelled out by Uefa, at senior level the proposed boycott would begin with next year’s Women’s World Cup, while the first age-group Fifa tournament to be boycotted is likely to be the Under-20 Women’s World Cup. It is due to take place in Poland from 5 September with six of the 24 competitors, including England, due to represent Uefa countries.

England’s women’s team also have a two-legged World Cup qualifying playoff tie against Greece in October, which would be a major test of the FA’s resolve if Fifa refuse to back down.

The European governing body invited other confederations to follow their lead. Uefa are understood to be confident that a number of Asian countries, in particular, are similarly minded. Infantino’s strongholds traditionally lie outside Europe and a collapse in support elsewhere could have severe consequences for the Fifa president.

“National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences,” Uefa said. “This is not a ‘democratic decision’, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.”

Sources within European football believe Uefa’s decision increases the chances of a Europe-backed candidate running against Infantino in next year’s Fifa election, which he had been expected to sail through without opposition.

Uefa has also held talks with the North American confederation Concacaf, who have expressed their opposition to Fifa’s plans but have yet to announce their support for a boycott.

The 41 Concacaf nations have arranged their own emergency meeting for 5.30pm UK time to discuss their own response to the crisis, with an announcement expected later on Thursday evening.

A number of European national associations are understood to have held talks with their respective governments over the matter, many of whom have backed a boycott in private.

The new UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, was the first politician to criticise Fifa’s plan on Tuesday evening, writing on X that the World Cup “was never anyone’s to sell”.

“This is a principled decision that we strongly support. Football belongs to the fans, not billionaire investors. Enough is enough. It’s time to take a stand to protect our game.”

On Thursday ⁠Britain’s culture ⁠minister, Lisa Nandy, backed ⁠Uefa’s decision. “This is a ‌principled decision that we strongly support,” Nandy said in a statement. “Football belongs to the ⁠fans, not billionaire investors. Enough is enough. It’s time to ‌take a stand to protect our game.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Thought leader Eddie Howe runs out of time and ideas at Newcastle
Sports.content:
FAREWELL, FAST EDDIE

That a vote of confidence isn’t worth the paper it’s written on has long been a footballing cliche. But not until this day did we know that this even applies to a vote of confidence that comes from Jonjo Shelvey – a man so devoted to the righteously upstanding that he once accused Alex Ferguson of grassing, following a high tackle committed in front of 45,000 fans, a worldwide television audience of millions and in full view of the referee.

“The games are on so late out here,” said the Arabian Falcons boss in April, when explaining why Eddie Howe should keep the Newcastle job. “It is hard to sit down and watch them constantly, but when there is a game on I will try my hardest to watch.” To his immense credit, though, Shelvey was undeterred by the daunting three-hour time difference that had the Magpies playing at all sorts of crazy hours, ranging from 3pm through to 11pm, mining the breadth and depth of his accumulated wisdom before surmising with characteristic erudition that “For me, they should stick with Eddie because he is a top, top manager.”

Despite so emphatic an endorsement, Newcastle’s honourable custodians were less certain. In September, David Hopkinson, the CEO, referred to Howe as the club’s very own Bruce Springsteen – which, at the time, seemed to characterise him as the treasured thought leader of integrity, personality and magnetism we all know him to be. But perhaps the absence of corpsing told us that Hopkinson was taking a Trumpian line – most recently, the US president said the Boss “looks like hell” – because by April, Hopkinson was equivocating on Howe’s position, advising that “we’ll talk about the future when it’s time”, the latent menace a trick of our collective mind. Well, it appears that time is now – even if, by Shelvey’s calculations, it’s the middle of an eternal night – and Howe is a goner, finally ushered through the door marked Do One.

“Every day as Newcastle manager is a great day for me,” he mused with typical candour, er … last night. “I believe great things are possible every season with a real buzz of what’s ahead. I see no reason for it to be any different this year.” Those with long memories could be forgiven for recalling 11 January 2011, when Howe announced he was staying at Bournemouth before, on 14 January 2011, he became the new Burnley manager. Which is to say that, though he may occasionally act to the contrary to avoid distracting questions about bone saws, Fast Eddie actually has a fairly good idea of how football works and may just have had an inkling that his employers – though renowned for their love of jigsaw puzzles and kindness to small animals – are occasionally capable of shedding their ruth for purely altruistic purposes. Rumours that the parting of ways was prompted by the new laws on goalkeeper “tactical time-outs” are understood to be wide of the mark.

Replacing Howe and taking responsibility for preserving the tradition of Wor Jackie, George Robledo and John Carver, best captured by that famous green-and-white away kit, will be Matthias Jaissle. After protracted, complex negotiations between the majority owners of Newcastle – Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund – and the owners of Al-Ahli – Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund – he will soon be released from his contract, many thousands of seconds after talks began. Though Jaissle is highly regarded by those in the know, the rest of us now have a problem: given the intimidating hour-long time difference between Saudi Arabia and Abu Dhabi, when will Jonjo Shelvey be available to break down the essentials?

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott revels in ‘second chance’ at Liverpool and has no regrets over Aston Villa loan
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott believes he has been given “a second chance” at Liverpool and denied his ill-fated loan to Aston Villa was a lost year in his career.

Elliott joined Villa on a season-long loan last September with an obligation for them to buy the midfielder for £35m once he made 10 appearances for the club. However, Elliott featured only nine times, playing 277 minutes in total, with Unai Emery and Villa unconvinced over completing the deal. Having made an 89th-minute substitute appearance for Liverpool at Newcastle in August, the 23-year-old was unable to sign for a third club in a single season.

Elliott has featured in both of Liverpool’s pre-season wins under Andoni Iraola in the United States. While non-committal about his long-term future – Sunday’s opponents Leeds have been linked – Elliott spoke positively about his time at Villa, the first time he has discussed last season’s issues, and claimed he could yet feature in Iraola’s plans.

“Everyone knows how much I love the club so the feeling never goes of putting the shirt back on, representing the club, and fulfilling your childhood dream,” said Elliott, a boyhood Liverpool fan. “But truthfully, yes [I felt it would never happen again], because I wanted a new challenge. I wanted to explore something, come out of my comfort zone, and I thought that would take me on as a player. Unfortunately, it didn’t work out, but the way I see it is it’s kind of a second chance, especially with the gaffer and new coaching staff coming in.

“It’s another chance to impress and hopefully get in their good books. But whatever happened last season, I wish Villa nothing but the very best. I had a lot of love for them and they treated me very well. I’m here now, and I’m trying to cement my spot in the team or within the squad.”

Elliott insists he harbours “no hard feelings” towards Villa. The Liverpool player was named player of the tournament at the European Under-21s Championship in the summer of 2025 and was touted as a possible member of Thomas Tuchel’s World Cup squad before his career stalled in the Midlands. But he insists: “I wouldn’t say it was a lost year because, at the end of it, I won the Europa League. To have that on my CV is incredible, especially with Villa. I saw with my own eyes how much it meant for them and I wouldn’t say it’s a lost year when you achieved something like that, because that’s selfish.

“It was a situation I couldn’t control. It was just a case of accepting it, and just trying to get my head clear and get myself in the best position to come back here, and I tried as hard as I could. I still feel like I can get better and I’m working as hard as I can to do that.”

Elliott admits Emery discussed his reasoning several times and that enabled him to handle the frustration of being sidelined for the majority of the season. “He explained very, very clearly and a fair few times. The whole club were very apologetic about the situation and, ultimately, it was a situation that I couldn’t control,” Elliott said. “But I knew 100% what the case was. It was like, ‘Ok, I can get over it, I know what the situation is now’.

“It was just about me handling it and showing my professionalism. I’m not that kind of guy who wanted to kick up a fuss and cause problems, because no one really deserves that. It’s just part of football and it was a learning curve for me and an opportunity that I hope I don’t experience again. But it’s a situation where I know I’ve been able to get through it.

“I’m really happy to be back and putting a Liverpool shirt on again. Playing at Liverpool, there’s no better feeling.”

Sports.title: FA raises minimum ban for racism and other forms of discrimination to 10 matches
Sports.content:
The FA is to increase the minimum punishment for discriminatory behaviour to 10 matches, in an attempt to counteract behaviour it says “continues to be a challenge across the game”.

The changes will come into force at the start of the new season and will apply to players and other football participants who are found guilty of an “aggravated breach” of the FA’s disciplinary rules on improper conduct, effectively actions that included discriminatory behaviour against any protected characteristics. Currently the minimum suspension for such a breach is six matches.

Across the 2025-26 season 10 individuals were found guilty of aggravated breaches, with their punishments, decided by independent Regulatory Commissions, ranging from six to nine matches. Under the new rules a punishment of fewer than 10 matches will only be allowed if sufficient mitigating factors have been presented, and the individual themselves has pleaded guilty to the charge.

Among the cases heard involved the Preston’s Milutin Osmajic, in which the Montenegrin was found to have made racist remarks to the Burnley player Hannibal Mejbri during a Championship match. Osmajic, who denied making the remarks, was served with a nine-match ban and given a minimum fine of £20,000. There has been growing concern that the behaviour of players in the professional game has trickled down the pyramid, creating greater problems in the grassroots game.

“We are committed to delivering a game free from discrimination. While significant progress has been made in recent years, discriminatory conduct continues to be a challenge across the game,” the FA said in a statement. “Enhanced measures are necessary to tackle this abhorrent conduct, and our updated sanction guidelines will now require regulatory commissions to impose a standard suspension of at least 10 matches in these circumstances.”

The new rules do afford commissions some flexibility. Cases that involve aggravated breaches “in writing only or via any communication device” – ie comments made online – could receive a punishment as low as three matches in the event of mitigating factors being accepted. If, however, an individual found to have breached the rules then commits a second offence, bans of over a year could be applied.

Sports.title: France defender Maxence Lacroix joins ‘beautiful club’ Chelsea from Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Maxence Lacroix has joined Chelsea from Crystal Palace to become the club’s fifth signing of the summer so far. The France international, who won the FA Cup and Conference League with Palace, has been the Blues’ main defensive target of the window.

Lacroix, 26, signs a six-year deal with Xabi Alonso’s side. “I am really happy to be part of this beautiful club,” said Lacroix, who played three times for France at the World Cup, including in their 6-4 bronze medal match defeat to England.

“Everyone knows the legend of Chelsea, its tradition of winning, and to be a part of that is a proud moment. I think it’s the best move for me because it’s the best club in the world. When I spoke with the manager, I saw that we have the same direction and desire for this club.

“We want to win. When you see the quality of the players here, everything we have around the club, it’s something that we can achieve. The ambition is to lift trophies, and I can’t wait to contribute.”

Chelsea had been looking to add experience to their back line having missed out on Rennes’ Jérémy Jacquet in January, with the player opting to join Liverpool. Levi Colwill, who is considered to be a key part of the club’s long-term plans, missed almost all of last season with an anterior cruciate ligament injury, with Wesley Fofana and Trevoh Chalobah forming the central-defensive partnership for much of the campaign.

After a dismal season that saw the club finish 10th, the club’s hierarchy has acknowledged a change in recruitment policy is needed, with a refocusing away from young, inexperienced players towards ones that can help the team compete for the title.

Lacroix, who made 55 appearances last season for Palace, has been one of the league’s most consistent defenders since moving to Selhurst Park from Wolfsburg in 2024.

The Blues confirmed the club-record arrival of Aston Villa forward Morgan Rogers last week, and have also added Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, striker Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg and Sporting Lisbon’s Geovany Quenda.
