Sports.title: Premier League agrees proposal to share an extra £1.5bn with EFL clubs
Sports.content:
The Premier League has agreed on a proposal to reset financial distribution within English football’s top four divisions, one that would lead to an extra £1.5bn being shared across the pyramid over the next decade.

Clubs voted unanimously to support the so-called “new deal for football” at a meeting on Thursday, after discussions with the EFL. The offer will now be presented to the EFL’s board for consideration.

According to details originally published by Sky News, the Premier League’s offer would run for 10 years and result in an additional £1.5bn being shared with EFL clubs on top of the £1.6bn currently distributed to clubs and communities every three years. Some of the money would be put into discrete funds – a “lifeboat” fund for clubs in immediate crisis and one that is directed exclusively at infrastructure.

To cover the extra costs, Premier League clubs have reportedly agreed to raise the transfer levy applied to all top-flight deals from 4% to 6%. The Guardian reported this week that Manchester City were initially opposed to increasing the levy.

The Premier League said in a statement that its clubs had “unanimously voted to approve a funded proposal for a new strategic partnership with the EFL”. It said it would now “look forward to continuing discussions with the EFL on progressing this proposal” and remain “committed to finding a football-led solution”.

The EFL has yet to officially receive the offer but acknowledged “constructive” discussions with the Premier League and said its board would “review the full detail of the proposal, including its potential benefits, implications and alignment with the long-term interests of our 72 clubs, ahead of further dialogue with the Premier League”.

This is the first time that Premier League clubs have officially agreed a proposal that could be put to the EFL since they were first asked to give more money to the rest of the pyramid five years ago. The Covid pandemic had revealed the precarious nature of finances at many EFL clubs and in 2022 the then sports minister Nigel Huddleston said the British public were already “out of patience” over a failure to reach an improved settlement.

The belief that the Premier League’s riches could be shared more effectively across the game helped lead in part to the creation of the Independent Football Regulator, which came into being last year. The regulator has played no direct part in the negotiations, but has a “backstop” power to force a settlement if none is agreed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

While there is cautious optimism that a deal can now finally be agreed, it is not a guarantee that the EFL will accept the Premier League’s offer, with sources suggesting it sees the proposal as being very similar to one that was mooted in 2023 but ultimately never approved by Premier League clubs. Both sides say they remain committed to ongoing dialogue.

Sports.title: Fifa’s sales pitch revealed: more tournaments, more debt … but no mention of women’s game
Sports.content:
Fifa’s sales pitch to persuade members to approve the sale of the World Cup’s commercial rights clearly states that their plans for financial growth will be achieved by staging more tournaments, having higher ticket prices and debt financing.

A 25-page sales deck titled “Fifa Forward Enterprise Member Materials”, which has been seen by the Guardian, makes the case for the creation of a new company to run Fifa’s commercial operations, 20% of which would be sold to Joshua Kushner, a US investor who is the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

The prospectus has been produced by JP Morgan, the US bank that was also behind the failed European Super League breakaway five years ago.

In addition to the previously reported $20m (£15m) sign-up payment Fifa has offered to all 211 member associations, which could be made available as soon as next January, the document projects that the four-year Fifa Forward payments would increase to $24m for each member by the 2035-39 cycle.

JP Morgan makes clear in the sales deck that such growth will come from “a growing tournament portfolio”, “third party sources of capital and debt financing”, and prioritising “high yield” partnerships and events.

There is also a reference to more than doubling the number of global tournaments held each year, from 200 to 450, which if followed through would put a huge strain on player workload.

Staging the World Cup more frequently would be most obvious way of raising revenue, with Gianni Infantino having previously proposed making it a biennial tournament five years ago.

The bank also raises the prospect of TV coverage of the biggest events such as the World Cup being sold to subscription channels or streamers, by referring to a plan to “expand and optimize media rights monetization”.

JP Morgan claims that Fifa is “undermonetized” but significantly makes comparisons with other sports leagues with the revenue figures based on club or franchise earnings, rather than with comparable governing bodies.

Fifa’s stated annual revenue of $3.6bn therefore compares unfavourably with the NFL’s compared revenue of $21.2bn, Major League Baseball’s $13.1bn and the NBA’s $12.5bn.

The document was sent to all 211 member associations on Wednesday night and immediately provoked a strong reaction.

One senior figure queried why Fifa, which has cash reserves of around $4bn and accumulated revenues of $15bn over the current four-year cycle, would need to take on debt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Another highlighted the odd comparison of a world governing body with private, member-run leagues, while JP Morgan’s proposed timeline for completing the deal was also questioned.

According to the document “Investors will be given access to a term sheet and select materials” in August before a vote of Fifa members has taken place.

Significantly there is little mention of the investor group elsewhere in the prospect, with no reference to their identity, their projected returns or exit terms.

There is one more major omission in the document, as there is not a single mention of women’s football anywhere across the 25 pages.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership returns with McInnes adding new twist to Old Firm rivalry
Sports.content:
Only residents of cloud cuckoo land can hold the firm belief that Scottish football will emerge promptly from a summer of discontent. The onset of a new domestic season, ordinarily a cause for excitement, instead gives reason to ponder the grim realities of what came before.

That it is unsurprising there has been no detailed explanation or plan from the Scottish Football Association following a lamentable World Cup does not prevent the scenario from being so deflating.

Mike Mulraney, the president, was last seen peeking out from the crowd behind Gianni Infantino and the US president at Trump Tower. Ian Maxwell, the Scottish FA’s chief executive, bemoaned “hysterical commentary” around his country’s World Cup performance during a brief media appearance after Steve Clarke had resigned. These executives had all but spurted with laughter when it was suggested handing Clarke a four-year contract immediately before Scotland set sail for the United States was perhaps a needless dalliance with risk.

Perhaps Mulraney and Maxwell are too engrossed in the sourcing of Clarke’s replacement to speak out on the overall state of the national sport. It is only fair to give them the opportunity to appoint a coach who can oversee much-needed transition in a geriatric Scotland squad.

The nation’s leading clubs have been moot on a big picture they wilfully ignore but that was exposed at a World Cup. The problem is that lingering and legitimate anger over Scotland’s showing on the biggest stage – despite all rationale behind it – mirrors so much broader sentiment as the Premiership returns. This has scope to be a troublesome, toxic campaign.

Celtic’s supporters remain irate at the custodians of their club, whom they perceive as complacent and out of touch. In Derek McInnes, Rangers have a new manager who is deeply unpopular on the other side of the city. Nobody should underestimate the lingering resentment that exists among followers of Hearts over the way the campaign of 2025-26 concluded.

The most reprehensible element of that arrived on 11 June, when the Scottish Professional Football League published the outcome of a disciplinary process into the pitch invasion that forced the ending of Celtic’s title-clinching clash against the Edinburgh club.

View image in fullscreen Celtic fans run on to the pitch after their team went 3-1 up against Hearts in the title-deciding game. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Snuggled in alongside wrist tickles for Hamilton Academical, Inverness and Stenhousemuir was a meagre fine for Celtic and a suspended, paltry ticket reduction. Rangers fans, who need little encouragement to rail against officialdom, were subdued until McInnes was slapped with a touchline ban for comments made against a refereeing decision.

Rangers have criticised elements of an independent report into the chaos which followed their March Scottish Cup loss to Celtic. Motherwell are speaking with lawyers due to objection to a Scottish FA fine for a video posted on social media.

A 2-0 European qualifying first-leg defeat in Kosovo last week was rightly sufficient to send Hibs fanatics into the internet’s version of orbit. Such results stopped being a shock long ago.

Certain clubs do actually have reasons to be cheerful. Celtic’s signing of Kasper Høgh for a club record fee not only demonstrated the kind of fiscal muscle-flexing that supporters wish happened more often but provided the most intriguing transfer arrival of the close season. Scepticism exists over the ability of players to perform outside the perennially successful environment of Bodø/Glimt.

Without such doubts and at a fee which even many Championship clubs would think little of, Høgh would have moved long ago. The 25-year-old, though, has a physical profile and direct style that should succeed in Scotland.

Celtic’s challenge is to replace existing first-team performers – Arne Engels and Alistair Johnston the prime examples – should irresistible bids arrive without posting the kind of net profit that makes balance sheets look more important than trophies. Fans have rightly welcomed the Høgh signing but need more.

Rangers, in contrast to their oldest foes, have burned through extraordinary amounts of cash in recent years while generally watching others lift trophies. This has fuelled rage in and reputational damage from the stands, which an American ownership has curiously opted not to challenge.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In McInnes, Rangers – who kick off the season at Dundee United on Friday – have a manager whose knowledge of club and culture looks better placed than most before him in recent years to lay gloves on Celtic. Vanja Dragojevic looks a smart midfield signing from Partizan Belgrade. Rangers need attacking spark yet it should be no surprise that McInnes’s first act was to implement a stronger core. He lacks nothing in motivation or work ethic in the job he has always craved. This version of Rangers should be much improved. Yet on the simple basis of course and distance specialism, Celtic remain the title favourites.

View image in fullscreen Motherwell’s recent success offers a template for other top-flight clubs to follow. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Nobody linked to Hearts should have been expected by now to fully process the circumstances in which they came within minutes of a first title win in 66 years, only for that dream to be snatched away. McInnes’s departure for Rangers, the completely new style implemented by Wouter Vrancken and a palpable raising of expectations all contribute to a period of upheaval.

Hearts’ tilt at glory came earlier than anyone could anticipate. The club remains on the minds of people who previously had no interest in the Scottish game. A comprehensive Champions League qualifying defeat by Sturm Graz showed the scale of work Vrancken has ahead of him. Patience, however, would be wise.

Motherwell’s work with and post the management of Jens Berthel Askou proved those below the Premiership’s biggest fish needn’t only cling on for dear life. The football was superb, the attendance figures boosted and a broader market was impressed. Motherwell’s sales of Elijah Just and Elliot Watt for multimillion pound fees completely justify a club model that thinks outside the box.

St Mirren have clear aspirations of introducing more young players and a more alluring brand of football. Kilmarnock displayed that at the end of last season under Neil McCann. Aberdeen will surely be a stronger force this time under Stephen Robinson.

Only one artificial pitch remains in Scotland’s top flight, which provides cause for celebration.

Football remains a Scottish obsession. It is also undeniably a sick patient. The dawning of a fresh season should appeal only if there is a glimpse of fresh thinking.

Sports.title: England legend demands unprecedented Argentina punishment from ‘greedy’ FIFA
Sports.content:
England legend Stuart Pearce wants to see heavy punishments handed out to Argentina after they were charged for numerous breaches by FIFA.

FIFA have charged Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina with assault. Thiago Almada has been done for unsporting behaviour as well.



4 Argentina as a nation and a few players are in deep trouble Credit: AFP

As a nation, Argentina face several very serious charges. These include racism and discrimination by their supporters.

They have also been charged with using sport to promote a non-sporting political message.

This relates to the use of the banner after their win over England in the World Cup semi-finals in which they claimed that the Falkland Islands were Argentine territory.



The banner read 'Las Malvinas son Argentinas', which translates as 'The Falklands are Argentine'.

The final charge is to do with breaching order of security, directly relating to delayed kick-offs.



And speaking on Breakfast with Andy Goldstein and Angelina Kelly, Pearce said: "What do you think they are going to do to the Argentinian players?

"Bear in mind, they upgraded Jarell Quansah's suspension and a six-game suspension to a Qatari [Assim Madibo].



"So, a player, after the game has finished, throwing punches...

"If you set a precedent for banning a player for six games for an accidental tackle, which I think is ludicrous because he wasn't a well-known player.

"Then bans for Ronaldo were quashed."

4 Argentina are almost certain to be found guilty of the breach relating to the Falklands banner Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Pearce goes in on FIFA

It wasn't just Argentina in Pearce's sights this morning as he took aim at FIFA as well.

Gianni Infantino plans to sell off the World Cup and has offered each nation up to $40million to ensure they voted for it by the middle of September.



Since, UEFA have revealed that every single one of their nations would boycott the FIFA's competitions should Infantino's plan come to fruition.

The FA are one of the associations to back these plans, so if they go ahead, England won't be at the World Cup and no English team would be at the Club World Cup either.

Pearce was speaking before the UEFA statement dropped, but he feels that fans and players would be harmed by these plans.

He said: "I am really dubious of any idea that comes out of them. Any idea, I mistrust.



4 Infantino's plans have been met with widespread rejection Credit: Getty

"Greed seems to be at the centre of everything, and not the fans.

"But I then feel sorry for the players if you end up boycotting it. What about the generation of footballers that never get to play in a World Cup because of that?"

What next?

talkSPORT exclusively understands that UEFA are set to be joined by other football federations in proposing a FIFA boycott.

Infantino's plan is to potentially merge FIFA's commercial and operational arms merged into one private-equity firm.



They involve selling stakes of the World Cup to private investors, with Donald Trump said to be involved in discussions.

4 Plans to sell off the World Cup are set to be decided by the middle of September Credit: AFP

The 57-year-old plans to run for FIFA president again, but talkSPORT understands that UEFA are trying to find a candidate.

One name who had significant support in UEFA circles was Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi.



However, those close to Al-Khelaifi insist he had no aspirations to stand, nor give up his roles at PSG and beIN Sports.

A spokesperson for Al-Khelaifi said: "Mr. Al-Khelaifi has absolutely no ambition, no intention and no interest in the FIFA role and all this media noise, and instead will continue to quietly and constructively support all the institutions of world and European football."

UEFA's statement

The UEFA statement against Infantino's plans is damning.

They said: "UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions.

"UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.



"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

"National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

"But our opposition goes far beyond process.

"The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.



"This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

"Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

"As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

"Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.



"There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

"Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale."

Sports.title: Chelsea signing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson is not ‘insane’ – it’s exactly what they need
Sports.content:
Chelsea signing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson is not ‘insane’ – it’s exactly what they need

Somehow, Chelsea have managed to surpass their own unpredictable standards this summer.

In a dramatic pivot from their transfer policy of signing young players for future success or profit, they have set sights on two names with a combined age of 71.

6 Welbeck is a signing that people did not expect Chelsea to make Credit: Getty

News of the surprise interest in Brighton striker Danny Welbeck broke on Monday and a move for the 35-year-old could be finalised by the end of the week.

Later that evening, 36-year-old midfielder Jordan Henderson became the next seasoned pro to emerge on the Blues' shortlist in what is set to be one of the most unexpected transfer moves of the summer.

The pair have made a combined 863 Premier League appearances at seven clubs that include Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool as well as Sunderland, where they played together in the 2010/11 season.

Add their collective 132 caps with England, and they boast a depth of experience for club and country that any top player would cherish.

Nevertheless, talkSPORT's Andy Goldstein cannot understand why Chelsea are looking to complete deals for Welbeck and Henderson.

"I think it's insane," he said on Tuesday's Breakfast show. "I always look at transfers like this, and people ask me what I think of that transfer.

"If it's the same level as my club, and Chelsea are top six, Man United are top six... if I turned on talkSPORT tomorrow morning and found out we were going after Welbeck and Henderson, I'd be like 'What on Earth is going on at my club?"

Andy Townsend then asked him about how he responded when United signed Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Henrik Larsson and Cristiano Ronaldo (for a second time), all of whom were at least 34-years-old.

Goldstein argued they were all world-beaters, before adding: "I'm going above and beyond to prove my point, but (Lionel) Messi, if he signed for Chelsea, I'd go, 'I can totally get that, it's Messi'. "But Danny Welbeck? No disrespect... Jordan Henderson, I mean?"

Yes, the moves have raised eyebrows and both players are not seen as long-term additions given their age but, when looking at the current Chelsea squad, Welbeck and Henderson could be huge influences.

6 Henderson is another shock name on the Chelsea shortlist Credit: Getty

Improving the lack of discipline

Chelsea had a whopping ten dismissals throughout last season, eight of which came in the Premier League - only Tottenham and Everton were closest on four each.

The average age of all nine players to get red cards was 24.6, which narrowly drops to 24.4 when you remove Marc Cucurella now that he has joined Real Madrid.

Just three matches in which a Chelsea player was sent off ended in a victory and they all came in the 86th minute or later, so more than likely had little to no impact on the result.

Chelsea red cards during the 2025/26 season Robert Sanchez - Manchester United 2-1 Chelsea - September 20 Trevoh Chalobah - Chelsea 1-3 Brighton - September 27 Joao Pedro - Chelsea 1-0 Benfica - September 30 Malo Gusto - Nottingham Forest 0-3 Chelsea - October 18 Liam Delap - Wolves 3-4 Chelsea - October 29 Moises Caicedo - Chelsea 1-1 Arsenal - November 30 Marc Cucurella - Fulham 2-1 Chelsea - January 7 Trevoh Chalobah - Chelsea 1-1 Burnley - February 21 Pedro Neto - Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea - March 1 Wesley Fofana - Sunderland 2-1 Chelsea - May 24

However, when coupling this with their 90 Premier League yellow cards in the 2025/26 season, the second-highest total, it's clear that discipline was a major issue at Stamford Bridge.

Welbeck has never been sent off during his career and averaged just one yellow card per 16.9 matches

Meanwhile, Henderson's numbers are a little higher as he has had two dismissals and been booked every 8.4 matches but, given his natural midfield position, he is more prone to giving away fouls.

6 Chelsea were very familiar with yellow and red cards last season Credit: Getty

What makes them smart signings for Chelsea is not just their strong willpower, but also their ability to keep a cool head in high-pressure situations on the pitch.

Welbeck and Henderson are no minnows in English football - they are two players who have represented some of the biggest clubs in world football and featured on the biggest stages.

Alongside a Premier League trophy, two FA Cups, two League Cups and a Club World Cup, Welbeck has played for England at three major tournaments - Euro 2012, as well as the 2014 and 2018 World Cups.

Henderson has appeared at seven such tournaments as a Three Lions international, and is a Premier League and Champions League winner, with three outings coming in finals of the latter competition.

'When the going gets tough, the tough get going' is applicable to the pair, and something that can't be said for many of those at Chelsea as of now.

But with level-headed and experienced players such as Welbeck and Henderson in the squad, there is a sense that they can bring a level of composure that has evidently been missing.

Setting standards

The competition for midfield places at Chelsea is strong - even if Enzo Fernandez eyes a summer exit - with players such as Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia and Dario Essugo among their options.

Bournemouth star Alex Scott is also understood to be of interest so Henderson, who turns 37 at the end of the new season, may not be a guaranteed starter.

6 Bellingham spoke very highly of Henderson at the World Cup Credit: Getty

This does not do anything to undermine his influence though - just listen to his World Cup teammates Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers, who has joined Chelsea in a £117million move from Aston Villa.

"Don't get us started on Hendo, we could speak about Hendo for hours," Bellingham said on Lions' Den, with Rogers adding: "The best guy I've ever come across, I think, in football."

Bellingham continued: "If there's ever an issue that you maybe think, 'I'm 22, 23, maybe it's a bit too much for me to go and address', he'll do it for you.

"If there's a problem between two people, he'll bring them together, he's that kind of person. Even staff will go to him to sort out issues. He's got no ego when it comes to supporting the team.

"He's a Champions League-winning captain, Premier League-winning captain... he was doing the sets for the finishes yesterday, he doesn't have to do that, he doesn't have to be that humble.

"Every day in training, he's relentless in wanting to be better and wanting to push everyone else to be better, he drives the intensity up."

Henderson played just six minutes for England at the World Cup, but he had an element of seniority in the 26-man squad, which meant he was more than just a player.

When celebrating the 3-2 win over co-hosts Mexico in the last 16, he fell over the advertising boards and suffered a freak broken arm as a result, which required surgery.

6 Henderson brushed off his injury to help England prepare for the quarter-finals Credit: Getty

It was later revealed that he had a 'completely smashed' forearm, but this did not deter him from joining in with the pre-match warm-up ahead of the 2-1 quarter-final win over Norway whilst wearing a cast.

Okay, in hindsight, this may have been a risky move for his long-term fitness, especially if a rogue ball managed to hit the stricken limb.

However, it's a testament to his commitment to the team that he was willing to risk his health by helping with their preparations, a strong trait that only strengthens his status as a leader.

Henderson can show Chelsea that, even if he does not appear on the pitch, he wants to remain a key part of the team and do everything he can to help contribute to their success.

If you can't beat them, sign them!

Every club has a player that seems to love facing them, no matter the time, place, competition or context surrounding their fixtures - for Chelsea, that's Welbeck.

He has scored or assisted against them over the past five campaigns, with three of his six strikes at Brighton coming in their league double last season.

Welbeck also netted versus Chelsea during his loan at Sunderland as he found their third in a shock 3-0 away win (Henderson played in midfield that day).

In fact, Stamford Bridge is a ground that he clearly enjoys going to - five of the seven total goals that have come against his new club were scored there.

6 Welbeck knows where the target is at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

Like Henderson, Welbeck is by no means guaranteed to lead the line for Chelsea on a regular basis, especially when Joao Pedro scored 20 goals in 50 appearances during his debut season.

The forward also turns 36 in November, but he has just had his best Premier League campaign to date with 13 goals scored, so what's not to like?

Nicolas Jackson and Liam Delap look likely to leave this summer, and Emmanuel Emegha would benefit from learning off Welbeck now that he's joined from sister club Strasbourg.

Manager Xabi Alonso will have a good balance of ready-made quality, experience and youth in his attacking options with Pedro, Welbeck and Emegha respectively.

Sports.title: England World Cup hero’s son reveals £200k Inheritance Tax row over winners’ medal
Sports.content:
Jack Charlton's son has been forced to give his World Cup winners' medal back to his mother due to an Inheritance Tax bill.

The England international was part of the side which lifted the Jules Rimet trophy in 1966.

4 Charlton's son is involved in a £200,000 Inheritance Tax row over his father's World Cup winners' medal Credit: Rex

Alongside his brother Bobby, Charlton helped the Three Lions beat West Germany 4-2 at Wembley Stadium after extra time.

However, on the 60th anniversary of the final, his son John has revealed he is not in possession of his father's winners' medal.

Instead, he has had to give it back to his mother despite being left the piece of memorabilia in his dad's will.

Charlton passed away aged 85 in 2020.

World Cup winners' medal

John spoke to Andy Goldstein and Stuart Pearce live on talkSPORT Breakfast on Thursday morning.

Having called in to discuss Eddie Howe's imminent exit from his beloved Newcastle United, he was asked about the World Cup triumph.

England's win over West Germany came on July 30, 1966, exactly 60 years ago.

Revealing both his dad and uncle had kept hold of their medals, he explained: "Funny enough, me and Eddie (Howe) were talking about his medal.

"I think there’s only him and my uncle Bobby who have kept their medals. Everybody else doesn’t have them anymore."

Asked where his father's medal is, he replied: "I've got it."

4 Charlton and his brother Bobby both kept their World Cup winners' medals, says John Credit: PA

Inheritance Tax row

John quickly added that it was not actually in his possession, though, due to a row over Inheritance Tax.

He continued: "Well, there’s a bit of a problem with it, actually.

"When I say I’ve got it, it was left to me in my dad’s will, but the tax man wants £200,000 off me in Inheritance Tax."

When asked if he is going to sell it, however, he added: "No, I’ve given it back to my mother because whilst she’s got it, I don’t have to pay that money."

In the United Kingdom, the standard Inheritance Tax rate is 40 per cent on the value of an estate above a £325,000 threshold.

John is hopeful the issue can be resolved, though, explaining: "There’s a journalist from the Daily Mirror who’s been working on it and helping us to try and sort it, but the same applies to Olympic gymnasts and people like that.

4 Charlton's son was left his World Cup medal, shirt and cap but faces a row over the Inheritance Tax Credit: Getty

"If they decide to sell their gold medals, they’re going to have to pay. Their family, sorry, pass it on, they’re going to have to pay Inheritance Tax on that. This is something that they’ve been trying to sort out."

It is not just his father's World Cup medal which he has, with John also in possession of his final shirt and England cap.

He revealed his cap from the tournament is the only one his dad kept hold of after his playing days.

John concluded: "I’ve got his shirt. Well, we’ve got his shirt as well. His shirt and his medal are in a safe place, tucked away.

"And the England cap that he got because he only got one cap for the tournament and that’s the only cap that he left. He gave the rest away."

Charlton won 35 caps for England between 1965 and 1970, scoring six goals.

4 Charlton guided the Republic of Ireland to three major tournaments during a legendary spell as manager Credit: PA

Meanwhile, he spent his entire club career with Leeds United, winning a league title, FA Cup, League Cup and two Inter-Cities Fairs Cups.

After retiring, Charlton went on to manage Middlesbrough, Sheffield Wednesday, Newcastle and the Republic of Ireland.

His time as Ireland manager saw him guide them to their first ever major tournament at Euro 1988.

Charlton also took the Boys in Green to the 1990 and 1994 World Cups, their first appearances at the finals.

Sports.title: UEFA to be joined in World Cup boycott across globe to leave Gianni Infantino’s controversial plans in disarray
Sports.content:
UEFA to be joined in World Cup boycott across globe to leave Gianni Infantino’s controversial plans in disarray

Several other confederations could follow UEFA's lead and boycott the World Cup, talkSPORT understands.

UEFA was the first to take the bombshell first step following an emergency meeting held remotely on Thursday.

4 UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin oversaw the meeting among the federation members Credit: AFP

All 55 member nations of UEFA unanimously agreed on the boycott decision. Meanwhile, CONCACAF, football's governing body for North America and the Caribbean, are holding an emergency meeting imminently.

The FA, who was one of those member nations to voice their opposition towards Infantino's plans, said via a spokesperson: "We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view.

"We oppose FIFA's plans - the FIFA World Cup belongs to football and always will."

And if other confederations take the same actions, Infantino could be left in an untenable position.

UEFA's statement on FIFA boycott in full UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions. UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors. The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale. It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football. National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game. But our opposition goes far beyond process. The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders. This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation. As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership. Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination. There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments. Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.

UEFA war with Infantino

UEFA's stance leaves a monumental dent in Infantino's plot given tournaments played without European nations would leave it significantly short on quality.

From 1998 onwards, a European nation has failed to win the World Cup only twice, with those exceptions being Brazil's triumph in 2002 and Argentina in 2022.

UEFA was prompted to call the emergency meeting after Infantino ignited a political storm across the footballing landscape when it emerged he planned to sell stakes in the World Cup.

The proposal, titled the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), would allow shares to be sold in tournaments like the World Cup and the Club World Cup.

Infantino informed the associations that made up FIFA they had until September 19 to make a decision on granting permission for investors to purchase stakes in the competition.

Unsurprisingly, the plan was met with widespread condemnation, as the FA, UEFA and CONCACAF all released strongly-worded statements in response.

4 Infantino's shameless cash grab looks set to backfire Credit: Getty

Infantino also expressed his intention to run the FFE as commissioner, should he be re-elected as FIFA president.

However, re-election may not be straightforward.

Next man up

There were growing calls among UEFA federations towards the end of the World Cup to back a candidate to run against Infantino at the next FIFA presidential election.

November 18 is the deadline to select a candidate for the elections, which will take place at March's FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco.

One name who had significant support in UEFA circles was Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi.

However, those close to Al-Khelaifi insist he had no aspirations to stand, nor give up his roles at PSG and beIN Sports.

4 Infantino shares a close relationship with US president Trump Credit: Getty

A spokesperson for Al-Khelaifi said: "Mr. Al-Khelaifi has absolutely no ambition, no intention and no interest in the FIFA role and all this media noise, and instead will continue to quietly and constructively support all the institutions of world and European football."

Infantino was already under fire prior to his FFE plans due to his conduct at the World Cup.

The 56-year-old received a call from US President Donald Trump, who requested a review into USMNT striker Folarin Balogun's red card.

Balogun had his suspension lifted shortly after Trump's intervention, although Infantino insisted the decision was made independently by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee.

However, it later emerged the call to let Balogun play against Belgium in the round of 16 was solely made by FIFA Disciplinary Committee chairman Mohamed Al Kamali.

Following the tournament, the Norwegian FA announced it intended to lodge a formal complaint to FIFA's ethics committee regarding Trump and his involvement in lifting Balogun's suspension.

4 Infantino is the ninth FIFA president but arguably the most controversial of the lot Credit: AFP

Infantino has served as FIFA's president since February 2016.

His tenure oversaw the expansion of the World Cup from 32 teams to 48, which was introduced for the 2026 edition of the competition.

Rory Jennings' verdict on Infantino

Although his time as president has seen several historic firsts, few have been appreciated by the football community.

And his latest act of villainy prompted talkSPORT host Rory Jennings to take a stunning dig in his direction.

"I think he is a tyrant and he needs to be stopped and I think it's really important to acknowledge that," Jennings said on talkSPORT Drive.

Jennings added: "Infantino has clearly been corrupted by power. He clearly loves the reputation, he clearly loves the limelight. If you look at his profile on social media, he's clearly infected by the stardust of it all.

"He loves the association with the president. He's clearly in Trump's pocket and Trump obviously loves football for what it's worth in terms of only happening because the World Cup went to the biggest commercial country it could."

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford issues update on future with farewell social media post
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford appears to have ruled out a return to Barcelona this summer in a farewell message on social media.

Rashford spent last season on loan with Barca and starred in La Liga, but they opted not to trigger his permanent clause.

3 Rashford won't be returning to Barcelona this summer after his loan spell Credit: Getty

The Spanish giants allowed his £26million option to expire in June, despite the forward admitting he wanted to stay.

They then went on to sign Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund for the same fee, indicating they wouldn't come back in for Rashford, despite talk they could look at a restructured deal.

And it does seem that Adeyemi's arrival, as well as the £70m signing of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle, have satisfied Barca.

That's because Rashford posted a goodbye to the club on his social media on Thursday afternoon.

Rashford's Barca farewell

He wrote: "I’m very grateful to everyone at Barcelona for making my time here such a positive and memorable experience.

"I’ve enjoyed every moment and will take many special memories with me.

Man United pre-season on MUTV Fans can watch Michael Carrick prepare for the new season and how the squad is shaping up across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Ireland. "I wish the club and all its supporters the very best of luck and every success in the season ahead."

Rashford also included a picture of his No.14 shirt and another image of him smiling during a game on his Instagram page.

Barcelona replied to his post, writing: "Thanks for everything Rashy. You will always be one of us."

Meanwhile, many of his former teammates sent messages to him in the replies, with Raphinha saying 'All the best, my brother' and Gavi writing: "I will miss you brother."

3 Rashford netted 14 goals and provided 14 assists in 49 games for Barcelona Credit: Getty

What next for Rashford?

So, Rashford won't be heading back to Spain - but where could he end up this summer?

Could he even reintegrate himself at Manchester United?

Well, he's set to return to training with Man United very soon after an extended break due to his involvement at the World Cup.

However, the England international has been warned that he may have to accept a bit-part role if he does end up staying.

If he is to leave, many teams have been linked with a move, including Premier League champions Arsenal.

But Rashford has been tipped for a switch to Tottenham instead, with manager Roberto De Zerbi hinting at a potential transfer 'bomba' coming this summer.

3 Rashford will be returning to Man United training this pre-season Credit: Getty

Spurs have been eyeing Manchester City's Savinho, but they have been told to take a look at Rashford instead.

And speaking on the rumours, talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook said: “I think if he goes anywhere in London, I'm keeping an eye on Tottenham.

“I could see that deal happening. Roberto De Zerbi believing that he can get the best out of Marcus Rashford.”

Rashford will hope to have his future decided quickly, with Man United's Premier League campaign starting on August 22.

He could be involved in that fixture against newly-promoted Hull City if he remains at Old Trafford this season.

But if not, the summer transfer deadline is set for 11pm on September 1, so the weeks are running out to find a new club.

Sports.title: ‘Sincerely sorry’ – EFL friendly moved as extreme weather conditions leave pitch underdeveloped
Sports.content:
An upcoming friendly between Reading and Charlton Athletic has been forced to move stadiums due to pitch conditions.

The pre-season fixture between the two EFL sides was set to take place at the Select Car Leasing Stadium on Saturday.



2 Reading have had to move their friendly away from their stadium due to the pitch Credit: Getty

However, Reading released a statement on Thursday revealing that their new pitch is not developed enough to host a match.

And therefore, the club have decided not to play the game at the ground, instead moving it to The Valley, Charlton's stadium.

The Royals wrote: "Following a period of unusually hot and dry weather during the growth of the Club's newly laid playing surface, it has become clear that the pitch is not yet sufficiently developed to host the fixture.



"While the pitch continues to progress, the recent weather conditions have slowed its development, meaning it is not where we need it to be at this stage.

"The Club has therefore taken the decision to protect the surface ahead of the start of the 2026/27 League One season, giving it the best possible opportunity to fully establish, with our focus firmly on ensuring the pitch is in the best possible condition when we welcome Luton Town for the start of the League One campaign."



All supporters who had bought a ticket for the match will receive a full refund due to the change.

And the match, which remains on Saturday, will now be played behind closed doors at The Valley.



Kick-off is scheduled for 2pm and Charlton will be streaming the action live for free.

'We're sincerely sorry'

Reading's Co-Chief Executive Officer, Joe Jacobson, has sent a message to supporters to explain the late change.

And he apologised to all fans after making the tough decision to protect the pitch for the League One season.

2 The friendly is now going to be played at The Valley in front of no fans Credit: Getty



Jacobson said: "This is not a decision anyone at the Club wanted to make, but it is the right one.

"We've invested significantly in providing the team with the best possible playing surface for the season ahead.

"Unfortunately, the recent spell of hot and dry weather has slowed the development of the new pitch and, after taking expert advice, we've concluded that protecting it now gives us the best chance of having it in the condition we all want for the start of the League One campaign.

"We know this will be disappointing for supporters who were looking forward to returning to the Select Car Leasing Stadium, and we're sincerely sorry for the inconvenience this causes.



"While we understand the frustration, our responsibility is to make decisions that are in the long-term interests of the football club, and this is one of those occasions.

"We're grateful to Charlton Athletic for their understanding, cooperation and support in helping us rearrange the fixture.

"We also thank our supporters for their patience and continued backing, and we look forward to welcoming everyone back to the Select Car Leasing Stadium when we begin our League One campaign against Luton Town."

Reading's meeting with Luton will take place on August 15, while Charlton begin their Championship season against Derby County on the same day.

Sports.title: Newcastle tipped for relegation immediately after Eddie Howe exit with worrying warning
Sports.content:
Stuart Pearce fears Eddie Howe's shock exit coupled with multiple high-profile departures could leave Newcastle flirting with relegation.

talkSPORT understands Howe is set to leave his post after almost five years at the helm and only weeks before the new Premier League campaign, with Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle lined up as his replacement.

3 Howe had already told Toon chiefs he wanted a break before news of his exit broke Credit: Getty

Unfortunately for Jaissle, he won't have star duo Anthony Gordon or Sandro Tonali at his disposal.

Gordon was snapped up by Barcelona for £70million while Tonali headed to Tottenham in a club record £100m switch.

The summer exits may not be done there though, as talkSPORT understands Arsenal are in advanced talks with Newcastle over skipper Bruno Guimaraes.

Although a deal is some way off completion, progress has been made on a verbal agreement north of £75m.

With the string of outgoings at St James' Park along with Guimaraes' uncertain future, Pearce believes Newcastle are 'closer to going down' than they are to winning the league.

Pearce: Premier League 'needs' Newcastle

"If you asked me that question [potential relegation battle] a year ago, I would have said they're a top of the Premier League, European side that look as though they're growing," Pearce said on talkSPORT Breakfast.

"Ask me the question now and I would say they look like a mid-table Premier League side that if they're not careful and they keep losing players and there's a downturn, they could flirt with relegation.

"That's how fragile the Premier League is, and it's a travesty because I've played there in front of their supporters and they're just incredible up there.

"I was delighted when Eddie went in to give the club a lift and see Newcastle on the rise because I remember the great days with Kevin [Keegan] there and beyond that and when Bobby [Robson] went there as well.

"As I say, it's a club synonymous with great things and great football and the Premier League needs a big Newcastle United."

3 Howe delivered Newcastle's first trophy in 70 years by winning the Carabao Cup in 2025 Credit: Getty

Pearce added: "I find it quite sad, I think Newcastle have lost an outstanding manager, I fear for them a little bit for nextyear.

"And to be fair, they're probably closer to going down today than they are winning the Premier League."

Newcastle fan and former England cricketer Steve Harmison, who now commentates on the club's matches for talkSPORT, echoed a similar sentiment to Pearce regarding his fears for the club's future.

'Careful what you wish for'

"It doesn't surprise me that [Howe] left," Harmison told talkSPORT hosts Adam Catterall and Darragh McAnthony.

"It looks like Bruno's going, it wouldn't surprise me if [Lewis] Hall goes or [Tino] Livramento.

"I fear for where my club is going, because the chief executive says we want to be the best team in Europe by 2030.

3 The Magpies could find themselves in a relegation scrap if they're not careful Credit: Getty

"If we're not careful, we might be the best team in the Championship by 2030. That is the sad case of what potentially [could happen because of] Eddie Howe leaving.

"The thing I said last year, the grass isn't always greener, be careful for what you wish for, because you've got no idea, I think, how good we had it. Time is going to tell whether that's right or wrong."

When was Newcastle last in the Championship?

Newcastle last featured in the Championship during the 2016/17 campaign having finished 18th in the Premier League the season before.

The Magpies secured an instant return though as they came first in the second tier, pipping Brighton to the title by one point.

Following promotion, Newcastle enjoyed a string of mid-table finishes in the Premier League before Howe guided them to 4th in the 2022/23 season.

However, Howe struggled to deal with a Champions League campaign in addition to the Premier League both times when they qualified for Europe's premier club competition.

Howe leaves the Magpies after they finished 12th, their lowest placing in the Premier League throughout his tenure.

Sports.title: Fulham bag £8.5m bargain from Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid reignite interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero - and Man City's talks over Ayyoub Bouaddi reach crucial stage: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Fulham bag £8.5m bargain from Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid reignite interest in Tottenham captain Cristian Romero - and Man City's talks over Ayyoub Bouaddi reach crucial stage: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Foxes eye Brighton winger Watson

Leicester City have enquired about taking Brighton winger Tommy Watson on loan.

The 20-year-old, who was key to Sunderland's promotion to the Premier League 18 months ago, had a spell on loan at Millwall last season.

Tommy Watson helped secure Sunderland's promotion to the Premier League via the playoffs

Porto keep tabs on Spurs man Souza

Porto are the latest team to show interest in Tottenham left wing-back Souza.

The 20-year-old joined from Santos for £13m in January and made four Premier League appearances last season.

Hail Cesar as Fulham get their man from Madrid

Fulham have agreed to buy Cesar Palacios from Real Madrid for a bargain £8.5million.

The deal has a similar structure to the one they have agreed for Gonzalo Garcia with Madrid retaining a 30percent sell on clause and matching rights for the 20-year-old.

Fulham are also among the clubs showing interest in Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri and Southampton midfielder Shea Charles.

Nwaneri also has interest from RB Leipzig and AC Milan.

Cesar Palacios has been secured for a fee of £8.5million

Fredricson moves on

Manchester United defender Tyler Fredricson has agreed a permanent move to Swiss club Lausanne-Sport, subject to registration.

Fredricson made four first-team appearances since he was handed a debut against Wolves in 2025 – when he also won the reserve-team player of the year award – and was on the bench on a number of occasions last season.

United have inserted a substantial sell-on clause and a buy-back clause into the deal.

The 21-year-old, who joined United at Under-9 level, played in every round of United’s successful FA Youth Cup campaign in 2022 until illness ruled him out of the final against Nottingham Forest.

The club confirmed Fredricson’s departure in a statement on Thursday, saying: ‘Everybody at United thanks Tyler for all his efforts during his time with the club and we wish him all the best for the next chapter of his career.’

Fredricson joins United loanee Sekou Kone at the Swiss Super League side.

CHRIS WHEELER

Rashford says no to Roma

Marcus Rashford has no interest in joining Roma this summer as speculation regarding his future grows.

The 28-year-old is set to report to pre-season training with Manchester United in the coming days after returning from his loan spell with Barcelona.

Roma had been one of several clubs linked with a move for the England attacker, but Daily Mail Sport understands a move to the Italian giants does not appeal.

Fulham to spend big on Garcia

Fulham are closing on agreement with Real Madrid over a deal worth £35m for striker Gonzalo Garcia. The deal also includes £2m in bonuses and matching rights.

Madrid have been discussing a buy-back option and a 30 per cent sell-on clause as talks draw to a conclusion.

Fulham also working to add midfielder Cesar Palacios on loan from Madrid.

Gonzalo Garcia looks set to join Fulham from Real Madrid in a deal worth £60m

Hull's Nobel quest

Hull are advancing in talks for Rayo Vallecano defender Nobel Mendy.

As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Hull had made enquiries and proposed a £15m offer for the 21-year-old who can play centre back and left back.

Rangers tried to sign Mendy a year ago from Real Betis but Vallecano got him for £2.5m and a 20 per cent sell-on clause.

Hull face competition from Ipswich for Burnley's Florentino Luis but have enquired about Augsburg's midfielder Mert Komur.

Coventry explore Hamer homecoming

Coventry City are exploring a deal to re-sign Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United.

The 29-year-old midfielder has one year left on his deal at Bramall Lane.

The Brazilian made 132 appearances for the club scoring 19 goals which included a strike in the Championship play-off final against Luton Town at Wembley.

Atletico reignite Romero interest

Atletico Madrid have rekindled their interest in Tottenham defender Cristian Romero.

The Argentina international's agents held talks with Inter Milan last weekend and director Piero Ausilio confirmed interest but that the deal would be complicated owing to the financial package.

Atletico Madrid are exploring a potential move for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero

Atletico had interest last year and are exploring the figures involved in a deal for the 28-year-old Spurs captain again.

Inter are in the market for centre backs this summer, with one new recruit expected to be John Stones if all goes to plan in his medical today.

Stones set for Inter switch

England defender John Stones has arrived in Italy ahead of his medical with Inter Milan.

Stones, 32, left Manchester City at the end of last season following 10 years with the club.

"Sono entusiasta di essere qui". John Stones è arrivato a Milano ⚫️🔵 pic.twitter.com/Xp2rS66VL9 — Fcinter1908 (@fcin1908it) July 30, 2026

Meanwhile, talks between Manchester City and Lille are reaching a crucial stage over the transfer of Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old Morocco international is ready to make the move now though his club have been keen to keep him in France for another season as part of negotiations.

City are ready to use him this season with Rodri a target for Real Madrid while interest is building in Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders.

City have lost Bernardo Silva and also have interest from Tottenham in Omar Marmoush and Savinho.

Bouaddi was valued around £60m before the World Cup but is now considered to be worth around £80m.

City also want to add another goalkeeper to replace Leeds-bound James Trafford with Marseille's Geronimo Rulli one name under consideration. They also want to strengthen at right-back and on the wing with Chelsea's Pedro Neto and Paris St Germain's Ibrahim Mbaye among names discussed.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Wednesday that the teenage Morocco international is ready to make the move now, though the French club would prefer him to stay for another season.

City would want Bouaddi for this season with Real Madrid ready to push for Rodri who is keen to return to Spain for family reasons.

Though they have added Elliot Anderson, they have lost Bernardo Silva and could also sell Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders who has interest from Galatasaray and earlier in the summer Atletico Madrid.
