Sports.title: Tottenham's 'bomba' signing: These are the two strikers they want, the game-changers they should be in for and the realistic targets that would fit perfectly with Roberto De Zerbi's style of play
Sports.content:
Trust Roberto De Zerbi to drop a bomb. Tottenham have already spent nearly £250million this summer, enough to give Daniel Levy the shakes, but the Italian made it clear Spurs were not done. ‘The transfer market, it’s not finished for sure,’ said De Zerbi. ‘We completed 60 per cent of our project in the transfer market. Now we have another bomba. Is it close? I hope, but it’s not finished for sure.’ Bomba. Both short for ‘bomba di mercato’, an Italian phrase meaning ‘market bombshell’, as well as a term used by Gen Z in online slang to mean a major surprise, a big piece of news, or a significant development. This is certainly one of those. ‘We have to increase the number of goals with the quality of the play, with the midfielders, with the attackers, but we have to bring players able to score goals. We have to consider set-pieces, we have to increase also the height, a lot of things.’ Roberto De Zerbi has promised Tottenham fans another 'bomba' signing in the forward line - and claims their already booming business this summer is only '60 per cent' finished They certainly need goals. They mustered 48 in the Premier League last season, fewer than most sides in the division. Eighteen of them came from corners, making up nearly 40 per cent of all their goals, by far the highest ratio in the division. So, perhaps, it’s not the set-pieces that need most of the attention. Spurs have completed huge deals for defender Jan Paul van Hecke for more than £50m and midfielders Mateus Fernandes for £85m and Sandro Tonali for £100m. They are in talks over signing winger Savinho from Manchester City but even he’s not believed to be the bomba. Whoever it is, it must be the man to bring them their much-needed goals. Daily Mail Sport assesses who De Zerbi’s mystery bombshell could be. Omar Marmoush De Zerbi is said to be a big admirer of the Egypt international and, despite making just eight league starts for Pep Guardiola last term, it’s easy to see why. As we saw with his use of Joao Pedro at Brighton, De Zerbi likes his strikers to drop deep and link up play, pulling defenders out of position to create space for wingers like Kaoru Mitoma or Simon Adingra to exploit and score goals. At Marseille, too, it was wide forward Mason Greenwood who finished as De Zerbi’s top scorer last season. That’s why Tottenham were so keen on Bournemouth striker Junior Kroupi before he was ruled out for up to four months with a foot injury. De Zerbi is a big admirer of Omar Marmoush (pictured), and it's easy to see why Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi (right) has been a target all summer - but has been ruled out for months with a foot injury When Marmoush played up front for City last season, often alongside Erling Haaland in a front two, he was usually the player to drop in to collect the ball and allow players to run on ahead of him. He did just that against West Ham last season (see below) as he holds the ball with Haaland, Nico O’Reilly, Antoine Semenyo and Bernardo Silva sprinting ahead of him. Marmoush draws his marker, slips in Silva, and he dinks the ball over the keeper with a sublime finish. Marmoush drops deep to get on the ball - just as De Zerbi likes his strikers to do - before slipping Bernardo Silva in down the left That ability to create space for those around him is ideal for how De Zerbi wants his Spurs team to play. But that’s not enough for De Zerbi. He wants forwards who, once that’s done, can turn and attack the box to get on the end of any chances created by the wide players. Marmoush can do that, too. That was clear in his finish when he led the line on his own without Haaland against Wolves in January, bursting to get ahead of his defender and on to the end of Matheus Nunes’ cross. Against Wolves last season, City's Marmoush attacks the space in the box and scores from Matheus Nunes' cross Marmoush also gives De Zerbi the option to play him in that striker role or as a left winger, where he’s also flourished. Few City fans will forget his hat-trick against Newcastle. Dominic Solanke is already a superb operator when it comes to coming short to help bring his team-mates into play and Marmoush is a fine, explosive option down the left. He’s quick, too. His top speed of 21.9mph put him inside the 25 fastest players at the World Cup. Cody Gakpo Tottenham are also understood to be interested in the Liverpool forward. De Zerbi, happy to say all the quiet things out loud when proclaiming what he’s looking for, declared Spurs have to ‘increase the height’ of his team. At 6ft 4in, Gakpo would certainly do that. Gakpo is another that fits the De Zerbi profile as a forward who likes to drift in off the left and attack the box but who also can play down the middle. And, when he does, he is the kind of striker who can drop in to mix it up. This is Gakpo’s touchmap from Liverpool’s final Premier League game of the Arne Slot era, a home draw to Brentford, where the Dutchman started as the lone striker but had most of the ball closer towards the halfway line. Cody Gakpo's touch map from Liverpool's home match against Brentford last season shows how he is far from a No 9, rather a forward who drops in to get on the ball Gakpo also has the wherewithal to nip in behind high lines, as shown below against Fulham in another game where he started as the lone striker. He latched on the ball over the top and raced through but couldn’t find the finish. Gakpo can also play on the shoulder of the defender and make runs in behind Gakpo, a regular starter last season, found himself cast as the fall guy for Liverpool’s dismal title defence under Slot. He was frequently the subject of fan derision while a return of just seven goals and five assists from 32 starts did little to help that perception, especially when he’d notched 10 goals from 23 starts during the title-winning campaign. He fits De Zerbi’s profile but not many Spurs fans would, perhaps unfairly, see his arrival as the bomba they would want. Gakpo is a good fit for the profile of player De Zerbi wants - but would he be the bomba Spurs fans are craving? Dusan Vlahovic Can a free transfer be a bomba signing? Zlatan Ibrahimovic’s arrival at Manchester United in 2016 would suggest so. Vlahovic, 26, remains a free agent after his four-and-a-half-year stint at Juventus came to an end. Tottenham are said to be interested in the No 9 and, like Gakpo, he would fulfil De Zerbi’s desire for added height as he stands at 6ft 3in. His 68 goals in 168 games was a fair old return at Juve and he reached double figures in his last six campaigns, stretching back into his tenure at Fiorentina. His 20 goals in 24 games for them in 2021-22 earned his big-money move to the Old Lady. Last season, too, he ranked among the division’s leading goalscorers when he was on the pitch with his trusty left foot. That, however, was the problem. He barely was. He missed huge chunks of the season with adductor and calf injuries.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Tottenham already have two injury-prone strikers in Richarlison and Solanke. They don’t need another. Not to mention Vlahovic was the highest-paid player in the whole of Serie A last season. He might be free to sign, but he’ll be far from that to keep. And he would be a completely different style of striker to those that De Zerbi likes to use. He’s an out-and-out front man. He rarely drops deep, he’s not the best at linking up play. That, for De Zerbi, is surely not the bomba. Serbia striker Dusan Vlahovic, who is now a free agent after leaving Juventus, is another option for Spurs but has had plenty of injury problems Marcus Rashford Despite 14 goals and 14 assists in all competitions (and nine goals which helped fire Barcelona to the La Liga crown), the Catalan giants opted not to cash in their £25m option to make Rashford’s loan move permanent, so he returns to Manchester United. Rashford hasn’t featured for his boyhood club since 2024 and is unlikely to feature in Michael Carrick’s plans for the season. As a forward who shifts in off the flank into central areas and can also play up front, naturally there has been some speculation that De Zerbi's Spurs could be a good move for Rashford. He ranked behind only superstars Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Raphinha for the most shot-ending carries in La Liga last season. He proved that he can still make things happen when he’s on the ball, doing his best work in the channels.

Your browser does not support iframes.

De Zerbi, though, for all his desire to play up and down and through the lines, is not renowned for his speed in moving the ball upfield. His Brighton side in 2023-24 produced the fewest fast breaks of any side in the division. He likes his side to build up patiently but then slice open defences with splitting passes. That’s why he’s signed defenders like Van Hecke and Marcos Senesi and midfielders like Fernandes and Tonali. That doesn’t suit Rashford quite so much, nor does De Zerbi’s desire for constant pressing and off-the-ball work. Marcus Rashford is available after Barcelona refused the option to take him on a permanent deal from Manchester United Lautaro Martinez Now, this would be a bomba. The top scorer in Serie A last season with 17 goals for Inter, and third behind only team-mate Federico Dimarco and Como winger Jesus Rodriguez for open-play assists. Tactically, he’s ideal for how De Zerbi plays. He drops off the front line, dragging defenders with him, to combine with his team-mates and then attacks the space that’s vacated. His heat map from 2025-26 (below) shows how he covered every blade of grass in the opponent’s half, with many of the chances he created coming from deeper areas. Lautaro Martinez's heat map in Serie A 2025-26 (deeper colour, more touches) shows how he covers every blade of grass Martinez creates chances from deep, he is not just a six-yard box player Martinez will be hard to get, though, as he loves playing for Inter Milan and has gone public about it Good luck getting him, though. ‘If they (Inter) don’t kick me out, I’m staying,’ he said recently. 'No doubt I would like to retire at this club.’ Julian Alvarez How about another Argentinian in Julian Alvarez? Arsenal have already been gazumped on Morgan Rogers, could it happen on Alvarez too? The former Man City forward has declared his desire to leave Atletico Madrid this summer to ‘fulfil his dream’. He does have a €500m release clause, though, and Atletico have already rejected a bid of £129m from Real Madrid. Now, here is a player who really does fit the De Zerbi brief - and 20 goals and nine assists in all competitions for Atletico last season show why. His 10 goals in the Champions League put him behind just Mbappe and Harry Kane. Argentina striker Julian Alvarez is a player who really does fit the De Zerbi brief Not only does he drop in, drag defenders around, and link up the play, he presses like a midfielder too. During the World Cup, starting up front alongside Lionel Messi, Alvarez did the hard yards. His touch map against England (below) showed just how much of it he did. Alvarez's touch map against England shows how he too likes to roam around the pitch During his final season at City, Alvarez won possession in the final third more often than any other striker. Now, he would be a bombshell signing.

Sports.title: Arne Slot says NO to replacing inbound Newcastle boss in Saudi Arabia as he eyes top European job after being sacked by Liverpool
Sports.content:
Arne Slot says NO to replacing inbound Newcastle boss in Saudi Arabia as he eyes top European job after being sacked by Liverpool

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Arne Slot is set to turn down the chance of a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia as the former Liverpool boss is committed to remaining in European club football.

The Dutchman left Liverpool at the end of last season and has been approached by Al Ahli to replace Matthias Jaissle, who is set to take over at Newcastle.

Mega-rich Al Ahli were ready to make him their top target.

But Slot is keen to find another top European club to take over and will reject Al Ahli’s official approach.

There has been vast speculation surrounding the Netherlands national team gig after Ronald Koeman was let go following the World Cup but it is understood that Slot is focused on staying in the club game for now, albeit flattered by the potential of managing his country one day.

Slot was sacked by Liverpool at the end of May, just one year after the Dutchman had led the Reds to the Premier League title.

His dismissal came after Liverpool finished fifth in the Premier League at the end of a campaign where Slot oversaw 20 defeats in all competitions.

Slot also came under pressure from supporters and saw several key players - such as the now-departed Mohamed Salah - speak out about the playing style.

Slot was sacked following a review into Liverpool’s troubled season that was led by Richard Hughes and Michael Edwards, chief executive of football at the club’s owner, Fenway Sports Group.

Prior to joining Liverpool, Slot had led Feyenoord to the Eredivisie title and the Dutch Cup, while they also finished as runners-up in the Conference League.

Al-Ahli are searching for a new manager with Jaissle poised to join Newcastle following the bombshell news that Eddie Howe will leave his role at St James' Park.

The German, 38, was previously in charge of Red Bull Salzburg between 2021 and 2023 and has since managed in Saudi Arabia, where he won the Asian Champions League in 2025 and 2026.

The expectation is Jaissle will be Newcastle's next manager.

His contract is currently with lawyers. He should be in charge when the squad travel to La Manga at the weekend.

Sports.title: England and fellow UEFA nations set to unanimously BOYCOTT World Cup after FIFA's plans to sell shares to private investors
Sports.content:
England and other UEFA nations have unanimously decided to boycott FIFA competitions amid Gianni Infantino's plans to sell shares in the World Cup.

UEFA held crisis talks virtually on Thursday after proposals to generate £3.1billion in private investment for FIFA tournaments, most notably the World Cup, faced widespread opposition.

Member associations were described to Daily Mail Sport as 'outraged' with more than 40 federations providing testimony, as UEFA coordinated their response to FIFA's proposals.

Daily Mail Sport also understands there was 'total unanimity' on the call with associations fuming that FIFA had left them in the dark - unilaterally developing plans to transform football governance.

One international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: 'This is at the nuclear button end of the spectrum, which is impressive'.

In a statement, cosigned by all 55 UEFA members, European football's governing body said: 'UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions.

'UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

'The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

'It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA's duty as the custodian of world football.

'National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has condemned FIFA's plans to allow private investors a share of the World Cup

'But our opposition goes far beyond process,' the UEFA statement continued.

'The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

'This model has no place in world football. Football's future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

'Europe's position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

'As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

'Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

'There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

'Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.'

An FA spokeswoman added: 'We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view. We oppose FIFA's plans - the FIFA World Cup belongs to football and always will.'

UEFA's decision to boycott tournaments could force FIFA to abandon its plans, just as they did when the continental confederation used the same tactic to compel FIFA to scrap a 2021 proposal to turn the World Cup into a biennial tournament.

Gianni Infantino has been widely criticised for his decision to put the World Cup 'up for sale'

Football Association chief executive Mark Bullingham came under pressure to take action

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: 'This is a principled decision that we strongly support. Football belongs to the fans, not billionaire investors. Enough is enough. It's time to take a stand to protect our game.'

FIFA are hoping to raise £3.1bn of private investment in a new company responsible for the commercial and operational aspects of tournaments.

Investment bank J.P. Morgan is FIFA's financial advisor on the project while Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group. Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.

Infantino tried to force FIFA's associations to decide on the proposal by September 19, while explaining the financial benefits in a letter to all 211 FIFA members.

UEFA, however, accused FIFA of trying to bribe associations into agreeing with the proposals, which could see them receive up to an additional £15million in revenue.

In another blow to the plan, the president of the Asian Federation Sheikh Salman wrote of his 'great concern and disappointment' in FIFA's decision to prepare the plans without consultation.

CONCACAF, which represents 41 countries in North and Central America and the Caribbean, is another federation to express early scepticism in the wake of the bombshell plans and are set to meet at 5.30pm.

Sports.title: SANDRO TONALI INTERVIEW: Why Tottenham's new £100m man chose Spurs over Man City and the 'mini connection' the star already has with Roberto De Zerbi
Sports.content:
Our interview with Sandro Tonali is over, but as we shake hands, we have a small correction to make with Tottenham Hotspur’s £100million summer signing.

Earlier on in the conversation, Tonali had explained how nice it was that he was now getting to speak in Italian – with his new manager Roberto De Zerbi and his assistants and team-mates such as Guglielmo Vicario and Destiny Udogie – after three years of only using English at Newcastle United.

Except, as those of us from the heart of the North East will tell you, we do not talk in English. We speak Geordie, and to Tonali’s credit, he appreciates the difference. He tells us how he grew to love the locals who supported him around St James’ Park, and explains how he wanted his old club to feel like they were getting their money’s worth once it became clear that he would be leaving this summer.

‘The first thing was to get the best deal for Newcastle,’ Tonali says when discussing his decision to leave his former side managed by Eddie Howe, whose exit from Newcastle was coincidentally revealed on the same day as we spoke in Sydney.

‘I met there some of the best people for football. They love football. They live for football. When I decided to move, I said to my agent and to Ross Wilson (Newcastle’s sporting director) that I wanted the best deal for Newcastle because they deserve everything. This is football. Sometimes you have to understand how everything can change in your life in five minutes.'

Newcastle are in bother this summer. Not only might Bruno Guimaraes follow Tonali and Anthony Gordon out of the door at St James' Park, they have now lost Howe now also. Tonali can only speak for himself, and he explains it was simply time for a change after three seasons and speaking with his family.

Sandro Tonali needed only a few minutes to convince him that Tottenham was his ideal Premier League destination

While sitting inside a makeshift boardroom set up inside Tottenham’s team hotel near the Sydney Harbour Bridge, Tonali explains how it was an easy decision to choose Spurs over others interested.

The £100m asking price that Newcastle placed on him influenced his options as he and his family were initially interested in returning to Italy. But they soon realised those in Serie A could not afford his services.

‘We stayed three years in Newcastle and after three years, we spoke all together, me and my family,’ Tonali says. 'It was impossible for the money (to return to Italy). For the salary, you can speak all the time, but if you don’t find the money for the transfer, you don’t have the chance to move.

'England was our solution and we found the best solution in England for me, for my career, for my football, for my happiness, for my family. I spoke with two teams. I understood after 10, 15 minutes that Tottenham would be my next team.’

Manchester City were believed to be the other club in for Tonali, who has won 32 caps for the Italian national team at 26 years old. He is rather liking the Little Italy connection developing within Tottenham now as he tells us: ‘After the last season, I spoke with my wife. We wanted to change our life. Not just for the city. We wanted to change everything. We spoke with two clubs.

‘When we spoke with Tottenham, we decided to sign for this team. They spoke with 100 per cent passion, 100 per cent seriousness. For this city, for my life outside of football for my family, OK, it’s like 10 per cent. Roberto and the director made the difference to the deal.

'I spoke after two minutes with my wife and my family and I said, “Probably it will be one of my best decisions of my career”. She told me, “You have 100 per cent the control over this decision”. I wanted to speak with her because it’s our life.

‘Roberto said the project will be tough but will be perfect for me, for you, for the city, an we can do one of the best seasons because we have big players. We just have to put a lot of work in.’

Alongside Tonali, Spurs have also spent £85m on signing Mateus Fernandes on West Ham, to complete their midfield. On officially being a £100m footballer, Tonali says: ‘You have to understand that this is football. The price is different now to 10 years ago. I know I have a lot of pressure but I know I’m a football player, I know my responsibilities, I know this team, I know the people here. I have to play like I’m a normal player, a normal Tottenham player, with passion, putting my energy in every day. It’s not £1m, £10m, or £100m. You just have to be a passionate player for this gaffer.’

Tonali previously spent a decade in Italy with Brescia, De Zerbi’s hometown. He and the Spurs boss have this ‘mini connection’, as Tonali describes it, and they previously met up there. ‘We spoke about him, about his work, about the passion that he puts into every single moment with the team for this work and I think now, after two weeks, I know everything is real,’ Tonali adds. ‘All gaffers are different. I passed three years with Eddie and he was fantastic, especially for me. But now I’ve found a different gaffer who works a lot on the pitch, a lot with the tactics, a lot with the ball. We love to play with the ball because we are a big team with big players.’

Sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz shows off striking new look ahead of tennis return - with Spaniard set to defend US Open title after FOUR months out injured
Sports.content:
Former Wimbledon champion Carlos Alcaraz has donned a new look ahead of his return from injury that saw him miss this year's championships.

The 23-year-old has been out of action since April due to the persistent wrist injury that saw him miss the French Open and this year's Wimbledon.

After failing to defend his Paris title in the spring, he had hoped to take part at SW19, but admitted the tournament had come too soon.

'My recovery is going well and I'm feeling much better, but unfortunately I'm still not ready to compete, which is why I have to withdraw from the grass-court swing at Queen's and Wimbledon,' he said.

'They are two truly special tournaments for me and I will miss them a lot. We'll keep working to come back as soon as possible!'

But he is edging ever closer to a return, and is showing off a new look ahead of that – with apparent braids.

Tennis star Carlos Alcaraz is donning a new look ahead of his highly-anticipated tennis return

Alcaraz usually dons swept short hair, but seems to have grown it out during his time off.

He shared a snap of a mirror selfie, wearing a white shirt with his hair split into braids.

The collection of photos was captioned: 'July,' accompanied by a sun emoji, and also featured snaps of the star celebrating Spain's World Cup win.

His Wimbledon absence meant rival Jannik Sinner took home the crown, with the two likely to face off sooner rather than later when Alcaraz returns.

Alcaraz is set to return to action in the Cincinnati Open, which starts on August 8 and finishes on August 23.

Then, he will look to defend his US Open title, with that competition beginning on August 23 too.

Alcaraz beat Sinner in last year's final in another chapter of their rivalry.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford sends emotional message to Barcelona fans ahead of expected return to Manchester United - after Spanish giants rejected chance to sign him for £26m
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford sends emotional message to Barcelona fans ahead of expected return to Manchester United - after Spanish giants rejected chance to sign him for £26m

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Marcus Rashford has sent a farewell message to Barcelona as the countdown continues towards his return to Manchester United.

Rashford spent last season on loan at the Nou Camp, contributing 14 goals and 14 assists as the Catalans won La Liga and reached the quarter-finals of the Champions League.

However, Barca decided not to trigger an option to buy him from United for £26million before a deadline in mid-June, and signed Newcastle’s Anthony Gordon for £70m.

On Thursday, Rashford posted a picture on social media of his No.14 shirt and another of him in action for the club with the message: ‘I am extremely grateful to everyone at the club for making my time here a positive and unforgettable experience. I enjoyed every moment, and I will keep many special memories. I wish the club and all its fans every success in the coming season. Visca Barca!’

Rashford is now set to rejoin United where he has a contract until June 2028 worth around £315,000-a-week. The England international is having some time off after helping England reach the World Cup semi-finals, and it remains to be seen if he will be involved in United’s training camp in Ireland next month which includes a friendly against Leeds at Croke Park on August 12.

With United in need of a left-sided attacker, and Rashford contracted to his boyhood club for another two seasons, it makes sense for the 28-year-old to come back and play under head coach Michael Carrick.

Marcus Rashford has sent a farewell message following his season long loan at Barcelona

It is looking increasingly like Rashford will be at Man United when the transfer window closes

There is no chance of a repeat of last summer when the more confrontational Ruben Amorim placed him in a ‘bomb squad’ of five players who trained separately from the main group at Carrington before Rashford left for Barcelona.

After initially putting a price of £40m on their top-earner this summer in the hope of moving him off the wage bill, it has been difficult for United to find a club willing to pay more than the £26m stipulated in the Barca loan as well as Rashford’s salary.

The club also discovered the high cost of replacing him when one option, West Ham’s Crysencio Summerville, joined Al-Hilal for £60m.

There is still time for some twists and turns before the window closes on September 1, but it’s looking increasingly likely that Rashford will be at United when it does.

Sports.title: JEFF POWELL MBE: It's time England led the football world again by standing up to mafia godfather Gianni Infantino - his plan to sell the World Cup is a bribe by any other name and there's only one way we can save our sport from extinction
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino. The very name has the ring of a mafia godfather.

All the more so when translated into English: Johnny Baby.

Not that he can be blamed for his genealogy. Just as it is no fault of the immigrant parents who named him that he has grown into the problem child of world football.

That is down to the greatest game on earth for standing by as he plunges his sticky hands into the goodie jar.

Oh, how tasty those treats are now. Trillions of dollars worth of global company investment, mega-brand sponsorships, gigantic advertising and mountains of merchandise.

Oh, how the corporate greed will trample on the purity of Pele's beautiful game, as it is worshipped by its hundreds of millions of faithful despite all its flaws. If Johnny Baby is allowed to flog off the World Cup in share lots as if it were just a pharmaceutical bloodsucker, high-tech upheaver of our daily life or mass armaments manufacturer profiteering off the human tragedy of all today's wars.

Gianni Infantino. The very name has the ring of a mafia godfather

Oh, how the corporate greed will trample on the purity of Pele's beautiful game, as it is worshipped by its hundreds of millions of faithful despite all its flaws

But who can stop Infantino who, like so many Italians before him, has found a pathway to power and riches via the American dream? When that wealthiest of all nations is governed by a patriot who frankly admits that his specialist expertise is in brokering business deals? When the presidents of FIFA and the US are a match made in boardroom heaven?

So, again, who can stop Johnny Baby from hocking the family jewels?

Time was when it would have been a steadfast, upright Englishman. When our own Sir Stanley Rous was president of a FIFA which held the good of the game above all else. As a family trust in the good old-fashioned way. Caring, not gluttonous.

Time now, surely, for THE Football Association – still the first FA in the esteem of much of world football – to take the lead.

To rally the diverse opinions of anxious believers on every continent, platitudinous politicians rushing to microphones, pious commentators et al behind an organised and concerted protest.

Don't leave it all to UEFA, whose concerns reflect all of ours but who have their own axes of rival authority to grind against FIFA.

Time for THE FA to throw off its obsequience to the demands of the Premier League and revive the nostalgia for English propriety.

Time to save the people's game, which it must remain, from piracy. To rescue the greatest sporting show of all, which the World Cup is still despite all the trials and tribulations of 2026. To preserve the future of football as a game, not a plaything of the stock exchanges.

Time was when it would have been a steadfast, upright Englishman. When our own Sir Stanley Rous was president of a FIFA which held the good of the game above all else

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) must stand up to what amounts to little more than a bribe

To protect the World Cup. Firstly from extinction by a European boycott. Secondly from reduction into a repetitive everyday occurrence by its staging every other year. Thirdly by expansion into the lopsided tedium of more and more finalists (48 this year, 64 next time, 128 sooner than we can blink). All for the money. All, it would seem, on the Infantino agenda.

THE FA can start by setting an example. Starting with a declaration that they would refuse their multi-million dollar handout if Johnny Baby's plan bears fruit.

A bribe by any other name for the poorer – and in some cases corrupt – countries on Planet Football if it all comes to a vote.

For FA's sake explain that this is an offer from the Infantino 'football family' which has to be refused. For the sake of all us football lovers, everywhere.

Sports.title: Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double
Sports.content:
Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double

Dan King, 21, who has been tipped to go all the way to the top, became the first rider for 42 years to win both the Galway Plate and Galway Hurdle

View 2 Images Dan King with his two Galway trophies (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

Rising star jump jockey Dan King made history on Thursday when he completed a huge Galway Festival double.

‌



The 21-year-old, who has been tipped to go all the way to the top in his profession, underlined his potential by pulling off a feat that had not been done for 42 years.

‌



On Wednesday, King netted the biggest prize of his burgeoning career as King Alexander defied odds of 20-1 to give Willie Mullins a third victory in the Galway Plate. The combination moved effortlessly into the lead from long-time leader Nouvotic at the second-last fence and ground it out from fast finisher Conyers Hill to win by half a length.

‌



Less than 24 hours after that success he rode Putapoundinthejar to capture the Guinness Galway Hurdle

Saving ground the whole way on the 10-1 winner, who was giving trainer Tony Martin his fifth victory in the race, King and Putapoundinthejar led at the final flight to beat Thisistheway by three and a quarter lengths.

‌



“It was plain sailing the whole way round,” he said after emulating the late Joe Byrne who was successful aboard Master Player and Tara Lee in 1984.

View 2 Images Daniel King (centre) riding Putapoundinthejar celebrates as he wins the Guinness Galway Hurdle (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

“He jumped savage the whole way round - he didn’t miss a beat. I took a chance going round the inside but when I wanted the gaps to open up they did.

Article continues below

“I’d never ridden a winner at the Galway Festival before but I was hopeful - I was coming here this week with a few nice rides. “When you get two of the biggest pots of the week, it’s class. “Dream stuff.”

Martin added of Putapoundinthejar: “He’s a big, old-fashioned horse. He was only coming to himself since Christmas and hopefully he’ll go on improving.”

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Friday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Friday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

View 8 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Coral Goodwood Handicap: DEFIANTLY narrowly missed out on a marquee success at Royal Ascot - but compensation is at hand. The son of Kameko is something of a slow burn - he didn’t race at two and managed one victory, in a Killarney maiden, from four starts as a three-year-old in 2025.

‌



There was very little to write home about when Defiantly finished last of 18 at Cork in April on his handicap debut, an effort which persuaded Joseph O’Brien to reach for the headgear.

‌



There was more encouragement in his visored fourth to stablemate Kizlyar in a conditions race over a mile and three-quarters back at Killarney the following month, but punters still let the four-year-old go off at 25-1 for the return to handicaps in the Ascot Stakes over an additional six furlongs.

‌



With his headgear cranked up to blinkers, Defiantly thrived for the step up to the marathon distance, hitting the front inside the final half mile and engaging in a stirring battle with old rival Kizlyar, just coming off the worse by a head.

Dylan Browne McMonagle’s mount is 4lb higher in the weights but is unexposed over a distance of ground and gets the vote to go one better. Alphonse Le Grande , Believitanducan and Maxi King are all strong candidates for the podium.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 DEFIANTLY, 2 ALPHONSE LE GRANDE, 3 MAXI KIN

‌



View 8 Images Talk Of New York: Newsboy's pick (Image: PA)

2.25 HKJC World Pool Thoroughbred Stakes: TALK OF NEW YORK enjoys a significant drop in class and should get back to winning ways. The son of Wootton Bassett - dam Usherette was a two-time winner at Group 2 level in the care of André Fabre - looked potentially out of the ordinary when scoring by five and a half lengths at Kempton Park last October on his racecourse debut.

The Charlie Appleby trainee’s tendency to race with the choke out proved his undoing when third in Listed grade at Meydan in February, so it was little surprise to see Talk Of New York wearing a hood when he reappeared at Newmarket’s Craven meeting in April.

‌



William Buick’s mount justified odds of 8-11 for a seven-furlong conditions stakes with ease and was even more impressive when landing the Listed Heron Stakes over a mile at Sandown Park next time.

That success, a five-and-a-half-length humbling of Time To Turn, pre-empted a step up to the top tier for the St James’s Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot.

Talk Of New York was anything but discredited in the meeting’s Tuesday feature, finishing a length and three-quarters back in third as Bow Echo denied Gstaad by a short head.

‌



It goes without saying that this rates a much less exacting task and there will be long faces at Moulton Paddocks if Talk Of New York doesn’t take advantage. Shayem is improving and is the choice to chase the favourite home, ahead of Saber Strike and Yazin .

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 TALK OF NEW YORK, 2 SHAYEM, 3 SABER STRIKE

View 8 Images David Menuisier: trainer of Tribal Chief (Image: PA)

‌



3.00 Coral Golden Mile: TRIBAL CHIEF keeps threatening to land a big one - and today could be the day.

There’s no getting away from the fact the David Menuisier-saddled son of Sioux Nation comes with risks attached - invariably left at the back of the field by a sluggish start, he needs a decent gallop to aim at and for the gaps to appear.

But his record over the past 12 months makes Tribal Chief a danger to all when he finally gets the breaks.

‌



A staying-on sixth in this race last year, my selection netted a valuable course-and-distance handicap 23 days later, beating Treble Tee by half a length.

Out of luck in the Cambridgeshire at Newmarket and the Balmoral Handicap on Champions Day at Ascot on his final two outings of 2025, Tribal Chief stormed home to take third behind Urban Lion in the Lincoln at Doncaster in March on his return.

Seven furlongs for Ascot’s Victoria Cup next time was on the short side but the five-year-old was again strong at the finish for a third to The Wizard Of Eye, before a sixth to Indalo on Sandown Park’s Coral-Eclipse undercard, when the leaders didn’t go quick enough.

‌



But there should be a fair pace up front here and there’s no better man to execute a hold-up gameplan than Jamie Spencer. The Golden Mile is its usual headscratcher, with Blue Brother, Bunyola Bay, Cerulean Bay and Mister Winston just four horses capable of getting involved.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3, 1 TRIBAL CHIEF, 2 BLUE BROTHER, 3 CERULEAN BAY

View 8 Images Newsboy tips Rumstar to be out in front at Goodwood (Image: PA)

‌



3.35 King George Qatar Stakes - RUMSTAR is a four-time Group 3 winner who gives the strong impression he can make his presence felt at a higher level.

Jonathan Portman’s stable stalwart, a nursery winner here in July 2022, opened his account at Pattern level in the Cornwallis Stakes at Newmarket the following October, doubling up in the

Palace House Stakes on the 2,000 Guineas undercard in May 2025. And the son of Havana Grey has completed the quartet in the past two runnings of the Coral Charge at Sandown Park on the first Saturday of July, most recently when getting the better of Luna A Inbhir by one length.

‌



But Group 3 sprints shouldn’t be the ceiling of Rumstar’s ambitions, as demonstrated by his four luckless forays into Group 1 company.

The five-year-old was drawn away from the action when debuting in the top tier with a 14th-of-20 finish in the King Charles III Stakes at Royal Ascot last year, before being tightened for room when fifth to Asfoora in York’s Nunthorpe Stakes a couple of months later.

The draw gods again refused to play ball in the Prix de l’Abbaye at Longchamp in October and in this year’s King Charles III Stakes. Rumstar beat just one home on both occasions.

‌



But Rob Hornby’s partner went under by just half a length to today’s favourite Night Raider in Newmarket’s Palace House Stakes on his previous start and, with a decent pace in prospect, this race should be run to suit. Night Raider is greatly respected, along with Jakajaro and defending champion Jm Jungle.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 RUMSTAR, 2 NIGHT RAIDER, 3 JAKAJARO

View 8 Images Andrew Balding: trainer of Jonquil (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

‌



4.10 Regent Seven Seas Cruises Bentinck Conditions Stakes: JONQUIL, proven at Group 2 level at Goodwood, gets the vote to bounce back to form after sub-optimal showings on his last two starts.

The son of Lope De Vega will return empty-handed to Andrew Balding’s Kingsclere stable if he can’t improve on a ninth-of-10 finish behind Notable Speech in the Group 1 Lockinge Stakes at Newbury in May or when beating one of seven opponents to the post in the Group 2 Summer Mile won by Zeus Olympios at Ascot 20 days ago.

But Jonquil was on-song prior to those disappointments, getting the better of the smart Holloway Boy by a length and a quarter for the Listed Paradise Stakes over a mile at Ascot at the beginning of May.

‌



And, while he didn’t shine in a messy running of the Group 2 Lennox Stakes won by Witness Stand when making his Goodwood debut at this fixture 12 months ago, Colin Keane’s mount showed the South Downs hold no terrors for him when accounting for Saqqara Sands by a neck in the Group 2 Celebration Mile next time.

An additional furlong here won’t be an issue for a colt who is very much a player if bringing his best form to the table. Galen, Boiling Point and Crown Of Oaks can fight it out for silver and bronze.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 JONQUIL, 2 GALEN, 3 CROWN OF OAKS

‌



View 8 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

4.45 Hawes And Curtis Nursery Handicap: REVELS looks fairly treated for his first appearance in the handicap sphere.

The son of Lope De Vega - dam Snooze N You Lose was a Listed winner for my selection’s trainer Karl Burke - fetched 350,000 guineas a yearling and had clearly been showing up prior to his debut at Redcar in May.

‌



Revels went off at 8-11 in a field of seven and his supporters were spared any anxious moments as he strolled clear under Sam James to win by three lengths.

Given his debut promise, the chestnut put up a so-so effort when 9th of 14 behind Nola Soul in the Listed Chesham Stakes at Royal Ascot last time - but there were excuses.

Drawn in stall two, Revels raced on the far side of the pack, occupying a track position that didn’t show him to best advantage.

‌



The evidence of his first start is Revels has the speed to cope with the step back from seven furlongs to six and he has plenty of potential to go past an opening British Horseracing Authority rating of 85.

In a field of two-year-olds whose best days lie ahead, Dubai Champion, Clash Of Hearts and Paper View are just three runners who merit a second glance.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 REVELS, 2 DUBAI CHAMPION, 3 PAPER VIEW

‌



View 8 Images Charlie Appleby: trainer of Into The Light (Image: Getty Images)

5.20 World Pool Bet with the Tote Handicap: INTO THE LIGHT didn’t shine when fancied to go well at Royal Ascot, but it’s early days to be writing him off.

Unraced at two, Dubawi’s son began to make up for lost time when lifting a 10-furlong maiden at Lingfield Park on St Valentine’s Day by a length from Al Azd.

‌



Into The Light finished a three-length second to Ravenspire when upped to a mile and a half at Southwell the following month and again claimed the silver medal when beaten a short-head by the progressive Lost Boys over two furlongs shorter at Sandown Park next time when making his handicap debut.

Charlie Appleby then sent my selection for the King George V Handicap at the royal meeting and punters liked Into The Light’s chances - he went off at 4-1 in a field of 19.

Things didn’t work out - William Buick’s mount came back in 11th of 19 behind Enceladus - but Into The Light, equipped with cheekpieces, retains potential and can go well. Kenergy is far from exposed and makes appeal, in company with Pierian and Mythical Valentine.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 INTO THE LIGHT, 2 KENERGY, 3 PIERIAN

View 8 Images James Fanshawe trains Newsboy's tip

5.55 British Stallions Studs EBF Handicap: ROOM FOURTEEN is three from four in handicaps and has yet to reach the bottom of the barrel.

‌



Hooded for her debut in the milieu at Great Yarmouth in April, the James Fanshawe-tutored daughter of Without Parole proved ahead of her opening mark with a short-head defeat of King Of Berkshire.

Room Fourteen ran second to subsequent Listed winner Venetia at Ascot 18 days later but was back in business with a three-quarter-length. Margin from Stoneacre Donny at Redcar on her penultimate outing.

And she went in again when justifying odds of 8-13 against seven opponents at Doncaster last time out, having a comfortable length and a half to spare over Brighton View.

‌



The British Horseracing Authority number cruncher’s latest intervention, a 6lb rise, takes Room Fourteen to a figure of 83 - 17lb higher than when she scored in Horatio Nelson country.

But there’s plenty more to come and Fanshawe’s booking of Ryan Moore is another plus. Favourite Silver Lake is on the up and shouldn’t be far away, while Zgharta and Wisper are other names to throw into the mix.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ROOM FOURTEEN, 2 SILVER LAKE, 3 WISPER

Sports.title: Max Verstappen told blunt truth about his F1 career as Red Bull quit decision looms
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen told blunt truth about his F1 career as Red Bull quit decision looms

Max Verstappen has been told there is nowhere realistic for him to go if he quits Red Bull, with one former F1 racer stating no top team has a vacancy for the Dutch champion

View Image Max Verstappen has yet to communicate a final decision on his Red Bull future (Image: Sona Maleterova, Getty Images)

Max Verstappen has been warned that there are no viable alternatives should he choose to walk away from Red Bull this year. With no available seats at any of the other leading Formula 1 teams, one former driver expects the Dutchman to "stay where he is and hope for the better", while also pushing to secure "a nice little extra bonus" on top.

‌



Verstappen holds a Red Bull contract until 2028, but it is widely known that it contains exit clauses which he can activate if specific performance targets are not achieved. It is understood that, as he does not currently sit second or higher in the drivers' championship at the start of this summer break, he has until October to trigger a departure should he wish to.

‌



For some time there has been a genuine threat that he might opt to walk away. Red Bull's performance relative to their rivals has declined significantly, and Verstappen has been thoroughly miserable behind the wheel of this new generation of F1 cars throughout the season.

‌



Even at the Hungaroring on Sunday, where he crossed the line in second place, he spent the entire race voicing his frustration over how poorly his car handled.

However, despite having threatened to quit F1 altogether earlier in the year, Verstappen now appears poised to remain on the grid for 2027 at least, following the FIA World Motor Sport Council's agreement to amend the engine regulations. Former F1 driver and current television pundit Christian Danner is firmly of the belief that it will be with Red Bull, given the absence of other realistic options.

‌



Michael Schumacher health update from family friend who's spoken with wife Corinna READ MORE :

He told The Express, via OLBG: "I always said, 'No way he's going to leave', because where could he go? Is Ferrari going fire Lewis Hamilton? No, because he's in form, and finally they get what they paid for. And the same with Charles Leclerc. He's a part of the Ferrari mentality, so they're not going to fire him. There's no room for Max at Ferrari.

"McLaren: is Zak Brown going to fire Oscar Piastri? Well, maybe, but what is he going to create? He's going to create an infinite fight between Lando Norris and Max because Lando is not prepared to accept the fact that Max is faster. Max would go there and take the break the whole thing into pieces. Zak Brown is, don't forget, the manager of Lando, so I don't think so.

If Toto Wolff wants to continue winning championships, he's got Kimi Antonelli, his own product, and he's got George Russell who I think is eventually going to do an exceptionally good job. He's not going to be erratic, he's not going to be stupid. So, also, no room for Max, because imagine Kimi versus Max. It's going to tear the team apart.

Sports.title: Ryan Moore hails ‘proper racing machine’ Diamond Necklace as she wins six on bounce
Sports.content:
Ryan Moore hails ‘proper racing machine’ Diamond Necklace as she wins six on bounce

The winner of the French 1,000 Guineas and French Oaks clinched her third Group 1 victory in the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood on Thursday

View 2 Images Ryan Moore and Diamond Necklace in the winners enclosure (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire. Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder)

Ryan Moore described Diamond Necklace as a ‘proper racing machine’ after she completed her sixth win in a row on Thursday.

‌



The winner of the French 1,000 Guineas and French Oaks clinched her third Group 1 victory of the year in the Qatar Nassau Stakes. The 4-6 favourite won in straightforward fashion, cruising up to Friendly Soul and pulling away to score by two and three quarter lengths.

‌



"That's the best she's felt, she's improving with her racing,” said Moore. “She gives you a classy feel. Every time I've rode her she's travelled with loads of pace, loads of enthusiasm and she has a turn of foot.

‌



“It was very easy. She's improved. She was very impressive today. She just feels like a proper racing machine now, doing everything right, travelled, quickened, does what she has to do.

"I think 10 [furlongs] is probably her optimum but with those classy horses, she does everything right so there's a chance she'd stay further, she'd have no trouble dropping back as well. We'll see I suppose. I can't answer that question [trip and next race]."

‌



View 2 Images Diamond Necklace gains straightforward win in Nassau Stakes (Image: Getty Images)

Diamond Necklace and the colt Constitution River are Aidan O’Brien’s two top three-year-olds this year, either of which could be considered for the Prix de l’Arc de Triomphe.

O’Brien said: "Whether she stays at a mile and a quarter and goes to the fillies' race in France, or to Leopardstown or an Arc trial, she's got all of those things open to her and she goes on soft ground as well as fast ground.

Article continues below

"Constitution River will get all the options too. At the moment he's going to York, so we're looking forward to him. The lads are never afraid to run against one another, but we'll get the next one out of the way and see where we're at."

Sports.title: England and UEFA nations WILL BOYCOTT World Cup in protest over Gianni Infantino sale plan
Sports.content:
UEFA have voted to boycott the World Cup and ALL FIFA COMPETITIONS after holding a meeting in response to plans that have emerged from FIFA president Gianni Infantino that would see private investment in the federation’s competitions.

Plans emerged that FIFA were looking to sell shares in its competitions, which would include the World Cup and Women’s World Cup, the latter of which will take place in Brazil next year.

The proposals have been criticised by leading organisations and individuals within the game, including UEFA, who had already issued two statements in response to the controversial plans. FIFA had written to their 211 member associations with the promise of $40m (£30m) if they were to show support for the scheme, something which UEFA have since criticised.

UEFA held a meeting between its member associations on Thursday amid rumours that they could consider boycotting the next World Cup in response to the controversial proposals.

‌



PSG chief makes decision over UEFA plea to replace FIFA villain Gianni Infantino READ MORE :

Man Utd prepare to take advantage of Newcastle carnage with own signing who wants out READ MORE :

Now UEFA's member associations, including England, have unanimously voted to boycott the World Cup and ALL FIFA competitions if the plans put forward by Infantino go ahead.

UEFA have issued a statement after the emergency meeting, which reads: "UEFA and its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions

"UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA’s proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

‌



"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football.

View 2 Images UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin led an emergency meeting on Thursday (Image: Toya Sarno Jordan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

"National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football’s greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a “democratic decision”, but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game. But our opposition goes far beyond process.

"The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders.

‌



"This model has no place in world football. Football’s future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain.

"Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation.

"As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

‌



"Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination.

"There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments.

"Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale."

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino faced severe criticism throughout the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The FA have also issued a statement to show their support to the stance taken by UEFA. “We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view," an FA spokeswoman said. "We oppose FIFA’s plans - the FIFA World Cup belongs to football and always will."

Several fans took to social media to react to the statements issued by UEFA and the FA.

One fan wrote: “This is necessary. Hopefully the other confederations follow suit,” while another added: “Great news! Hopefully CONMEBOL will join.”

‌



Another fan wrote: “Well done UEFA for standing up to Infantino,” while one more added: “Well done UEFA for having the best interests of the game at heart.”

In a video released on Wednesday, Infantino said: "FIFA Forward Enterprise, or FFE, is actually a proposal, an offer. It's part of a democratic process – a consultation process – and, above all, it is an opportunity but not an obligation

“It is a golden opportunity to turbocharge the development of the game globally. But again, it is just an offer, not an obligation."

He went on to add: "Capturing that value requires additional expertise, additional insight, distinct from governing and developing the sport.

‌



“It would simply commercialise and organise all FIFA-owned competitions along with sponsorship, broadcast, licensing and new ventures for the benefit of FIFA's 211 member associations."

Lisa Nandy, the government's Culture Secretary, said: “This is a principled decision that we strongly support. Football belongs to the fans, not billionaire investors. Enough is enough. It’s time to take a stand to protect our game.”

Meanwhile, PA reported that 'The Football Association of Wales and the Scottish FA also emphasised their unity with their fellow national associations and gave their backing to UEFA's statement'.

Sports.title: Five moments that defined Eddie Howe's rise and fall during Newcastle tenure
Sports.content:
Five moments that defined Eddie Howe's rise and fall during Newcastle tenure

Eddie Howe led a Newcastle team that was blossoming and on the up for several years, but he's presided over a decline over the last 12 months, which has ended with him stepping away

View 4 Images Eddie Howe's five year stay at Newcastle boss will come to an end (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Eddie Howe's time at Newcastle has come to an end - a tenure that promised so much has endured in a gradual decline over the past year.

‌



Even before the Magpies were well beaten by Bristol City on Wednesday night, it did not seem a happy camp. Howe has taken Newcastle from a side fighting relegation to one making the Champions League knockouts, but his hands have appeared increasingly tied.

‌



In recent years the club have appeared hamstrung and this summer Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali have been sold, while Bruno Guimaraes may yet follow.

‌



Newcastle's Saudi Arabian owners have spoken about being the world's best team sooner rather than later, but the club are tracking in the opposite direction right now. Howe has enjoyed the affection of the Toon Army, taking them to heights they haven't seen since Sir Bobby Robson managed them in the early 2000s.

Alan Shearer shares honest take on Eddie Howe’s Newcastle exit and selling best players READ MORE :

Eddie Howe told what made his Newcastle job 'unsustainable' before sudden departure READ MORE :

But last year's 12th-place finish followed years that have seen Newcastle lack consistency. Howe's full-season finishes read fourth, seventh, fifth and then comes their drop down to the bottom half. That has appeared a lot to stomach, the repercussions have been obvious, and Howe has called time.

The highs have been monumental, but the lows over the past year especially have not aligned with a club who want to be up there with the elite. We delve into the five moments that saw Howe scale the mountain, before falling down it at an alarming rate.

‌



His first January window

Newcastle walked in 2022 as a side in the relegation zone, but no team in the bottom three of the Premier League has ever had such an injection of cash given their takeover only months earlier. They spent it excellently though, recruitment the club conducted wasn't just to save them, but to set them up for the years that followed.

View 4 Images Newcastle signed Bruno Guimaraes from Lyon in 2022 (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Image)

Kieran Trippier was the first statement buy of the Saudi-era and the versatile full-back was signed for only £12million, which was excellent value. That same window they landed Guimaraes from Lyon, who was well thought of, but didn't have Europe's elite crying out for him. He's become the cornerstone of everything good that happened under Howe.

‌



Securing Champions League football

A year after securing a mid-table spot, armed by the addition of Alexander Isak, Newcastle begun 2022/23 in impressive fashion, losing just once in their first 24 games to start the season. They mixed it with the likes of Manchester City, Arsenal and Manchester United. They would later claim wins over the Red Devils and hammer Tottenham 6-1 in a memorable afternoon at St James' Park.

Qualifying for the Champions League was certainly on the radar, but there's no doubt Howe accelerated that timeline. Whether that changed the perception of what the club should be achieving, only those inside the four walls know, but they seized on poor years from the likes of Liverpool and Chelsea to finish fourth.

‌



Eddie Howe was FAILED by Newcastle United owners - he should have walked away earlier READ MORE :

Premier League rival and six other clubs Eddie Howe could join after shock Newcastle United exit READ MORE :

Winning the Carabao Cup

Nothing ignites tenures and gets fans excited more than a trophy and for all the times Newcastle had finished in the top four over the past three decades, never did they have their moment in the sun. Well, Howe changes that, and it was a managerial masterclass that day at Wembley.

View 4 Images Dan Burn was on the scoresheet as Newcastle's claim Carabao Cup glory (Image: Getty Images)

Having beaten Arsenal home and away, they were still underdogs when they came up against Liverpool, who had set the pace in the league and were tipped to claim the first trophy of the Arne Slot era. Instead goals from Dan Burn and Isak set Newcastle on their way to the most memorable of triumphs.

‌



Isak's exit and failed replacements

Only months after scoring to down Liverpool in the final, one of 27 goals that year, the Swede decided he wanted out. He was prepared to down tools to get his own way and this was the first time in the Saudi-era that Newcastle had one of their biggest names wanting to quit. Previously they had been upwardly mobile and it seemed everyone was here for the journey, but it appeared not.

Isak's desire to leave was a distraction. Newcastle claimed he wasn't for sale, but then let him leave on deadline day. In return they managed to land Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa - between them last year they scored 14 times and some games saw them sat on the bench alongside each other. Before that Newcastle had tried - but failed - to sign Hugo Ekitike and Benjamin Sesko. It was an unmitigated mess, and the season that followed reflected that chaos.

View 4 Images Newcastle have struggled to recover from the loss of Alexander Isak (Image: 2024 Getty Images)

‌



Sunderland complete the double

In a Premier League campaign that saw Newcastle lose 17 times, going down to Sunderland at St James' Park was perhaps the lowest point. The Black Cats were enjoying an excellent debut year, securing European football, and followed up their win at the Stadium of Light by silencing their rivals.

Sunderland scored their winner in the 90th minute - which was the fourth time in just over two months that Newcastle had conceded a losing goal after the 80th minute. The loss to their arch rivals was also during a period whereby they were beaten nine times in 12 games and their season dwindled to one of irrelevance.

Sports.title: It's time for the ECB to admit they have got The Hundred horribly wrong
Sports.content:
It's time for the ECB to admit they have got The Hundred horribly wrong

With crowds at venues up and down the country dwindling from previous seasons, The Hundred has come under fresh scrutiny as the height of summer passes without any international cricket

View 3 Images The Hundred has seen dwindling attendances this season (Image: ECB via Getty Images)

After playing a match-winning innings for the Trent Rockets against the Welsh Fire on Wednesday, Ben Duckett was left bemused.

‌



The England opener cracked an unbeaten half century for his Hundred franchise in Cardiff, but only 7,400 people were there to see it. It follows a trend of reduced numbers of people in attendance across the 2026 edition of the competition, its sixth season.

‌



"You look at every side, and it's just world-class opponents," Duckett told Cricinfo. "I'm so surprised that the crowds have been what they have, because I'd be desperate to watch some of these guys play cricket.

‌



"They've not been great. Just looking around the grounds, there must be a reason for it."

Let me enlighten you, Ben. Crowds are down because that powers that be have taken an already divisive competition and made it indisputably worse.

England name new Test coach as Joe Root returns as captain READ MORE :

Duckett is right; the star talent on show up and down the country is unquestionable. So why are fans staying away?

‌



Sporting fanaticism in the UK is built upon pillars of culture and identity. This is the antithesis of The Hundred.

When the ECB gave counties a 51% stake in their franchises allowing them to be subsequently sold on, they made a rod for their own back. Four of the eight sides are now at least part-owned by IPL teams.

The suits will tell you the money brought in from these sales has propped up a sport that was in dire need of a cash injection. But at what cost?

‌



The height of summer is now ring-fenced for a tournament that the general public are turning away from, while international cricket is shoehorned either side of it.

It would be remiss not to mention the positive impact The Hundred has had on the women's game. But could this have been achieved by investing in the already existing domestic T20 competition?

View 3 Images Sunrisers Leeds decked out in their orange strip (Image: ECB via Getty Images)

‌



Upon its inception, The Hundred was meant to bring new audiences to cricket, introducing a format that was supposedly easier for the casual fan to follow.

Taking the Headingley franchise as an example, then known as the Northern Superchargers, they hoped to attract families from across Yorkshire and the North East to enjoy some crash, bang, wallop with an array of stars on show.

The Superchargers had a dashing purple kit, were led by popular northerner Ben Stokes and had a smattering of representation from the White Rose county.

‌



Now known as Sunrisers Leeds, after being taken over by the Sun Group who own Sunrisers Hyderabad, they play in orange and have just two Yorkshire players on their books.

Many of those who had paid to watch the Superchargers over the last five years were from various parts of Yorkshire.

Simply put, the vast majority of people from Sheffield, Barnsley, Huddersfield, Bradford and other surrounding areas will not support a team called Leeds. It's not surprising crowds have dwindled, despite the offer of a free shirt with every pair of tickets.

‌



View 3 Images Ben Stokes in action for Durham in the Metro Bank Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Naively, the social media bods at Sunrisers Leeds even posted a video of their players awkwardly mumbling through their own version of 'Marching On Together', Leeds United's anthem, reading the words from a sheet in the dressing room after a win.

It went down like the proverbial lead balloon and was subsequently removed.

‌



Contrastingly, Yorkshire have put up the 'SOLD OUT' signs for back-to-back Metro Bank Cup games at York while Headingley is being used for The Hundred.

Granted, the venue can only house around 4,500 spectators. But it was bursting at the seams on Wednesday as the White Rose beat Worcestershire and will be so again on Friday as Stokes and Durham make the short journey down the A1.

There is a certain irony that Stokes, the biggest name in English cricket, is playing in this competition rather than the ECB's flagship tournament just a few weeks on from relinquishing the Test captaincy.

Article continues below

The 50-over competition is enjoying something of a resurgence as counties packed with local youngsters do battle in a more traditional format of the game at smaller venues.

Of the 11 Yorkshire cricketers that took to the field against Worcestershire, seven came through the club's academy system. Fans want to watch players they can identify with playing for clubs they care about.

They do not want random teams with random names playing in random kits.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
